The highlight of the night came in the fourth and fifth, when Roki Sasaki and Edwin Díaz hung a couple more zeroes in what were important appearances from each.
For Sasaki, the outing marked his first since returning from the injured list and making his own late-season move back to the bullpen, where he could reprise his role as closer from last year’s playoffs. He worked around a pair of singles with two strikeouts and a fastball that, even after being sidelined for the last month by a blister, sat at 99-100 mph.
For Díaz, Tuesday was not only a third-consecutive scoreless outing since his own return from the IL, but his most impressive yet as he makes a bid for the playoff roster. He retired the top of the Padres lineup in order with a pair of strikeouts, and has now retired 9 of 11 batters he has faced since rejoining the active roster.
Asked postgame if Díaz –– the $69 million offseason signing who lost the closer’s job amid a previously dismal debut Dodgers season –– could still pitch his way back into ninth-inning duties, Roberts said it’s “certainly possible.”
“The way he’s throwing, the ninth is possible, yes,” Roberts added.
By that point, the Dodgers had already pulled away from the Padres. They mounted a four-run rally with two outs in the second against King, who issued back-to-back bases-loaded walks to Tommy Edman and Mookie Betts before Freddie Freeman slashed a two-run single through the infield. The offense tacked on more runs in the fourth (on another Freeman RBI single), the sixth (on a solo home run from Tommy Edman), and the seventh (a Will Smith solo blast).
In what was the lineup’s toughest test in a while, they passed with flying colors.
Still, the night’s most encouraging developments came from the ‘pen, which capped off the game with two scoreless innings from Kyle Hurt, then stress-free appearances in the eighth and ninth from Alex Vesia and Jack Dreyer.
The unit’s most trusted arms at the moment, Tanner Scott (who figures to be vying with Sasaki for the postseason closer role) and Evan Phillips, weren’t even required. Nor was Edgardo Henriquez, who remains sidelined by a back injury but still could return in time for the playoffs.
“We know we have a good group, and anytime we get to carry the load and everybody has success and throws up zeros, it’s special,” Stewart said. “That’s really hard to do, for all eight guys or whatever it was today. So yeah, it’s cool.”
With a smirk, he added: “Write stories about it.”
Come October, of course, the Dodgers will be hoping their relievers are the main story.
But if the rotation falters, the club seems significantly better-suited to handle it than it did a year ago.
“That could change in a day, in a game, as we all know,” Roberts said. “But right now, feel really good about everyone out there.”

item.content:encoded:
【パドレス0-7ドジャース】ロサンゼルス／ドジャースタジアム、9月22日（日本時間23日）
すでに地区優勝とポストシーズン進出を決めているドジャースは本拠地でのパドレス3連戦がスタート。その初戦はブルペンゲームの投手陣を打線がしっかり援護し、7-0で快勝して5連勝となった。メジャー最高勝率のブルワーズが敗れたため、ドジャースはブルワーズまで1ゲーム差に接近。負傷者リストから復帰した佐々木朗希は4番手として四回に登板し、2安打を浴びながらも1イニングを無失点に抑えた（防御率4.56）。 ドジャースは先発のブロック・スチュワートと2番手のジャスティン・ロブレスキーが各1イニングを無失点に抑えると、二回2死からヒット2本と死球で満塁のチャンスを作り、トミー・エドマンとムーキー・ベッツが2者連続で押し出し四球を選んで2点を先制。さらにフレディ・フリーマンの2点タイムリーが飛び出し、4-0とリードした。 三回を3番手のブレイク・トライネンが無失点に抑え、四回は佐々木が登板。ジャクソン・メリルをセンターフライ、オースティン・ヘイズを空振り三振に仕留め、簡単に2死を取ったあと、連打で一、二塁のピンチとなったが、ジェイク・クロネンワースを見逃し三振に仕留め、無失点で切り抜けた。 その直後、ドジャースは2死からベッツが二塁打を放ってチャンスメイクし、フリーマンのタイムリーで1点を追加。五回は5番手のエドウィン・ディアスが三者凡退に抑える好リリーフを見せ、六回は6番手のカイル・ハートが無失点に抑えた。 すると、六回2死からトミー・エドマンの8号ソロで1点を追加。ハートは回跨ぎで七回も無失点に抑え、直後にウィル・スミスにも10号ソロが飛び出して7-0とリードを広げた。 八回は7番手のアレックス・ベシアがマウンドに上がり、2死から四球を与えたものの、メリルを空振り三振に仕留めて無失点。九回は8番手のジャック・ドライヤーが三者凡退に抑える好リリーフを見せ、8人の投手による完封リレーを締めくくった。 勝利したドジャースは最高勝率ブルワーズまで1ゲーム差に接近。ただし、ブルワーズとの直接対決で負け越しているため、第1シードでポストシーズンに進むためにはブルワーズを勝率で上回る必要がある。

item.title: [True Blue LA] Dodgers rout Padres in bulk in opener
item.dc:creator: Eric Stephen
item.description: LOS ANGELES — On a night the Los Angeles Queens won a championship in the inaugural season of the Women’s Pro Baseball League, the Los Angeles Dodgers beat a King. Four runs with two outs in the second inning off Michael King paced a 7-0 win for the Dodgers over the San Diego Padres in Tuesday night’s series opener at Dodger Stadium. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — On a night the Los Angeles Queens won a championship in the inaugural season of the Women’s Pro Baseball League, the Los Angeles Dodgers beat a King. Four runs with two outs in the second inning off Michael King paced a 7-0 win for the Dodgers over the San Diego Padres in Tuesday night’s series opener at Dodger Stadium.
With the win, the Dodgers are up five games on the Atlanta Braves for the No. 2 seed in the National League playoffs, with five games remaining in the regular season. The Dodgers’ magic number to clinch a bye into the NLDS is down to just one.
King hadn’t allowed more than three runs in any of his previous nine starts, with a 2.26 ERA during that span, and he retired his first five batters faced on Tuesday. Then with two outs in the second inning, the next six batters reached, breaking open the scoring.
Teoscar Hernández singles for the Dodgers’ first hit, then Josue De Paula singled on an 0-2 pitch before Andy Pages was hit by a pitch in his very first plate appearance back since getting hit by a pitch one month prior, to load the bases. Tommy Edman walked on four pitches for the game’s first run, Mookie Betts only needed five pitches to walk home another run, then Freddie Freeman grounded a single through the infield, and under the legs of a leaping Edman, to score two more.
Betts hit a ground-rule double in the fourth, followed by another RBI single by Freeman for a fifth run against King.
Solo home runs by Edman in the sixth and Will Smith in the seventh off the Padres bullpen padded the scoring.
With Emmet Sheehan optioned on Tuesday and Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list, the Dodgers have only three active pitchers they plan to use as starting pitchers in the postseason at the moment. That means they have 11 relievers, and on a day following an off day and the day before a start by the MLB leader in innings per start, the Dodgers used .. pitchers to cover the nine innings.
Starters Justin Wrobleski and Roki Sasaki — the latter just activated on Tuesday — each pitched only one inning, both scoreless. Sasaki was hitting 100 mph in his first game action in four weeks.
Kyle Hurt was the only Dodgers pitcher to toss more than one inning, taking care of the sixth and seventh.
Jack Dreyer was the first pitcher of Sunday’s game, and the last pitcher on Tuesday.
It’s only the third time in franchise history the Dodgers used eight pitchers in a shutout of no more than nine innings, done also on September 29, 2019 in San Francisco and May 15 this year in Anaheim. For some perspective, when the Dodgers beat the Expos 1-0 Montreal in 22 innings on August 23, 1989 — Rick Dempsey homered, Tommy Lasorda got Expos mascot Youppi ejected — the Dodgers only used five pitchers that day.
Tuesday particulars
Home runs: Tommy Edman (8), Will Smith (10)
WP — Justin Wrobleski (12-5): 1 IP, 1 hit
LP — Michael King (12-10): 4 IP, 6 hits, 5 runs, 2 walks, 5 strikeouts

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- Shohei Ohtani is expected to return to the lineup Wednesday, the first day he is eligible to be activated off the injured list, and Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts says he looks "considerably" healthier than he did a couple of weeks ago.
"If he was a five, he's probably an eight or a nine right now," Roberts said, referencing a 1-to-10 scale.
The Dodgers activated right-hander Roki Sasaki and center fielder Andy Pages off the IL on Tuesday, a major development in the leadup to October.
Sasaki, who has been recovering from a blister suffered in an Aug. 26 start, was available out of the bullpen for Tuesday's series opener against the San Diego Padres and could be an option to again close out games in the postseason. Pages, who fractured his left hand on Aug. 22, will reprise his role as an everyday player at a premium position.
Ohtani landed on the IL because of lingering pain in his right biceps and left knee on Sept. 8 but began a hitting progression seven days ago and advanced to taking as many as 40 swings off Trajekt, the popular pitching simulator, on Saturday. Ohtani also ran the bases that day. On Tuesday, he went through his typical pregame workout.
Ohtani, 32, will only hit the rest of this season and was struggling in that realm before landing on the IL, compiling only seven hits and 22 strikeouts over his past 54 at-bats. Roberts previously indicated the plan was for Ohtani to play in all of the Dodgers' remaining five regular-season games to get reacclimated to major league pitching.
Where he hits, though, is up for debate. In all likelihood, Ohtani will continue to lead off against opposing right-handed pitchers. But Mookie Betts' recent hot streak -- heading into this week, he was hitting.373/.468/.746 in September -- has Roberts weighing the possibility of batting him leadoff against lefties.
What Ohtani's return means for outfield prospect Josue De Paula is also an open question.
De Paula, 21, has eight hits and 10 walks in 38 plate appearances since temporarily replacing Ohtani at designated hitter. The Dodgers are strongly considering him as an option to be a left-handed bat off the bench during the postseason, though they might send him down as the corresponding move for activating Ohtani to give him at-bats in this week's Triple-A championship series.
The other candidate would be backup catcher Dalton Rushing, who has an elbow injury that is preventing him from throwing. Rushing is expected to be activated at some point in the next three days, but Roberts acknowledged it would be difficult for him to be thrust into a pinch-hitting role in October after playing in only four games since the start of September.
"There's potential slug with both those guys," Roberts said. "It's going to be a good debate."

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Roki Sasaki Could Close for Dodgers in Postseason
item.dc:creator: Los Royers
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CA — Roki Sasaki could pitch his way into the Los Angeles Dodgers’ closer conversation before the postseason begins. Manager Dave Roberts confirmed Tuesday that using Sasaki as a closer in October is an option, although the Dodgers have not assigned him the ninth inning—or any fixed relief role—as he returns from the injured list. “It’s certainly an option,” Roberts said. “A lot of it probably is contingent on how he throws here tonight.” Sasaki was activated with Andy Pages before
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CA — Roki Sasaki could pitch his way into the Los Angeles Dodgers’ closer conversation before the postseason begins.
Manager Dave Roberts confirmed Tuesday that using Sasaki as a closer in October is an option, although the Dodgers have not assigned him the ninth inning—or any fixed relief role—as he returns from the injured list.
“It’s certainly an option,” Roberts said. “A lot of it probably is contingent on how he throws here tonight.”
Sasaki was activated with Andy Pages before the Dodgers opened their series against the San Diego Padres. Rather than returning to the rotation, the right-hander will spend the final week auditioning for a postseason bullpen role.
Dodgers will evaluate Sasaki in multiple roles
Roberts said Sasaki could work two innings in his first appearance, entering at the start of a clean inning. That opportunity could arrive early, in the middle innings or late in the game depending on how the matchup develops.
“I could envision him pitching multiples,” Roberts said. “I can see him coming into a clean inning and pitching two innings. I’m not sure if that’s the third inning or the sixth inning or the eighth inning, but he’s ready.”
The Dodgers then expect to give Sasaki one or two shorter appearances before the regular season ends. Those outings will help determine whether he can handle a traditional closing assignment, provide multiple innings or fill another high-leverage role in October.
Roberts stopped short of labeling Sasaki the closer and noted that his late-inning success last season developed from the Dodgers’ needs at the time.
“I don’t want to say he’s going to finish games or be a closer,” Roberts said. “Last year was one of those things where it was a situation of need, as far as where we were at with performance, with health of guys, and he filled that role admirably.”
Dodgers do not have a designated closer
Sasaki’s opportunity comes as the Dodgers prepare to enter October without one reliever locked into the ninth inning. Roberts said he would prefer a set closer in a perfect scenario, but he does not currently see one pitcher holding that job.
“Right now, I don’t see a one-person closer,” Roberts said.
That approach would allow Roberts to deploy Tanner Scott against the most dangerous portion of an opponent’s lineup before the ninth rather than saving him for a lead that might never materialize. Roberts also said he would be comfortable asking Evan Phillips or Brock Stewart to close a game.
Phillips has looked more like himself over his last three appearances following an inconsistent beginning to his return from Tommy John surgery, according to Roberts. Stewart has also been one of the Dodgers’ most effective relievers when healthy.
The Dodgers therefore have several ninth-inning possibilities. Sasaki’s final regular-season appearances will determine whether he becomes one of their most prominent options.

item.title: [MLB.com] Sasaki returns in relief role as Dodgers assess bullpen options for postseason
item.dc:creator: Sonja Chen
item.description: LOS ANGELES -- Roki Sasaki opened eyes when he moved to the bullpen for last year's run to back-to-back championships. He'll reprise that role in the final days of this regular season -- and possibly be in the mix to close out games once again. Sasaki was activated from the 15-day injured list ahead of Tuesday night's series opener against the Padres amid a flurry of moves that also saw Andy Pages return from the IL and Emmet Sheehan and Eliezer Alfonzo get optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City. Sa
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- Roki Sasaki opened eyes when he moved to the bullpen for last year's run to back-to-back championships. He'll reprise that role in the final days of this regular season -- and possibly be in the mix to close out games once again.
Sasaki was activated from the 15-day injured list ahead of Tuesday night's series opener against the Padres amid a flurry of moves that also saw Andy Pages return from the IL and Emmet Sheehan and Eliezer Alfonzo get optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City. Sasaki last pitched on Aug. 26, when a blister on his right middle finger brought his start against the Braves to a premature end.
In his second Major League season, Sasaki was steadily growing closer to resembling the version of himself who was a phenom in Nippon Professional Baseball. He went 5-5 with a 4.60 ERA through 23 starts, but those numbers don't tell the full story. Working with an expanded pitch mix, including a new splitter, and increased fastball velocity, Sasaki put together his best sustained stretch as an MLB starter, recording a 2.63 ERA through seven starts before dealing with the blister.
"Excited to see Roki back," manager Dave Roberts said. "He's looking forward to this role. I think he can be very impactful, as it was last year."
In his return to the bullpen on Tuesday, Sasaki was available to pitch multiple innings. He will likely get a couple of additional relief appearances in the final five games of the regular season.
Last year, Sasaki's shift to relief was an unprecedented move. After underperforming to begin his rookie season and then missing more than four months with a shoulder injury, Sasaki's only chance to contribute to the Dodgers in the postseason was to move to the 'pen.
Sasaki didn't just contribute -- he became the Dodgers' postseason closer, allowing just one earned run in 10 2/3 innings (0.84 ERA). The confidence he gained from getting results at the big league level, with the stakes as high as could be, fueled the 24-year-old right-hander's return to the rotation and eventual midseason breakout this year.
The Dodgers are currently working without a set closer, as Edwin Díaz is pitching in low leverage amid his season-long struggles as he looks to earn a role in the postseason bullpen. It has been a long time since Sasaki has pitched in relief, but if he can show Roberts enough in the final week before the postseason, he could very well be an option in save situations.
"I think it's certainly an option," Roberts said. "A lot of it, probably, is contingent on how he throws here tonight. He'll probably get another one or two shorter stints before the season's end."
With Díaz missing time with elbow and neck injuries -- and not pitching well when healthy -- left-hander Tanner Scott has gotten the bulk of save opportunities. Scott leads the Dodgers with 23 saves, but he's also blown four saves, including two since the start of September.
Scott may still be the best option to close out games, but Sasaki could complement him from the right-hand side, which is important with leverage righty Edgardo Henriquez out for the rest of the regular season with a lower back strain (he is expected back during the postseason).
While Roberts would like to have a closer in the postseason, he acknowledged that it's more likely that he will play the matchups. At this time of year, some of the highest-leverage situations take place before the ninth inning, so having multiple options would free up Roberts to use his best relievers in the lanes that make sense.
"I think if there's an opportunity, for example, for Tanner to pitch a high-leverage inning in the seventh or the eighth inning, it's just hard to pass that up if he's the best option right there," Roberts said. "Because you just don't know where the ninth inning is going to be."

item.content:encoded:
LA 다저스는 22일 밤(미국 현지시간) 다저스타디움에서 샌디에이고 파드리스를 상대로 시작되는 중요한 시리즈를 앞두고 타선과 불펜을 보강했습니다.
다저스는 화요일 외야수 앤디 파헤스와 우완 투수 사사키 로키를 부상자 명단에서 해제했습니다. 이에 따른 후속 조치로 우완 투수 에밋 시한과 포수 엘리에세르 알폰소가 트리플A로 내려갔습니다.
앤디 파헤스는 지난 8월 21일 투구에 맞아 왼쪽 손가락 골절 부상을 당하기 전까지 타율 0.272, 홈런 21개, 도루 12개, OPS 0.796을 기록하고 있었습니다. 그는 회복 과정을 앞당기기 위해 나사 삽입 수술을 받았으며, 별도의 마이너리그 재활 경기 출전 없이 곧바로 부상자 명단에서 해제되었습니다. 다만 19일에 열린 확장 시뮬레이션 경기를 소화했습니다.
사사키 로키는 지난 8월 27일부터 오른쪽 손가락 가운데 물집 증세로 전력에서 이탈해 있었습니다. 그 역시 재활 경기를 거치지 않았지만, 16일에 4이닝 동안 48개의 공을 던진 시뮬레이션 경기를 포함해 최근 실전 타자들을 상대로 투구를 소화했습니다. 원래 계획은 선발 투수로 몸 상태를 다시 끌어올리는 것이었으나, 사사키는 정규시즌 마지막 날들에 다저스의 불펜 요원으로 대기할 예정입니다. 그는 이번 시즌 119.1이닝을 던지며 평균자책점 4.60을 기록하고 있습니다.
이번 선수단 활성화 조치는 다저스가 오타니 쇼헤이까지 복귀시킬 수 있는 시점을 단 하루 앞두고 이루어졌습니다. 오타니는 수요일에 부상자 명단에서 해제될 자격을 얻게 되며, 데이브 로버츠 감독은 일요일 인터뷰에서 오타니가 그때 라인업에 복귀할 "좋은 기회"가 있다고 시사했습니다. 왼쪽 무릎과 오른쪽 이두근 통증에 시달려 온 오타니는 남은 시즌 동안 마운드에 오르지 않을 것입니다.
96승 60패를 기록 중인 다저스는 내셔널리그 플레이오프 2번 시드 자리를 두고 브레이브스에 4경기 차로 앞서 있으며, 이 순위를 유지하면 다저스는 디비전 시리즈에 직행하게 됩니다. 만약 오늘 시즌이 종료된다면, LA 다저스는 3번 시드 애틀랜타 브레이브스와 6번 시드 필라델피아 필리스 간의 내셔널리그 와일드카드 시리즈 승자와 홈 경기를 치르게 됩니다.
그러나 필리스(86승 70패)가 컵스 및 파드리스(나란히 87승 69패)에 불과 1경기 차로 바짝 추격하고 있어 내셔널리그 와일드카드 순위 레이스는 여전히 혼전 양상을 보이고 있습니다. 샌디에이고는 최근 5연승 및 지난 14경기 중 13승을 거두는 상승세를 탄 채 화요일 차바트 라빈에 도착했습니다.

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Dave Roberts' Hyeseong Kim update confirms Dodgers' position battle never really ended
item.dc:creator: Katrina Stebbins

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are still fighting to keep their first-round bye, but they're already prepping for their 14th consecutive postseason appearance — and there are a number of questions they still need to answer.
Will Shohei Ohtani be ready? Does Edwin Díaz make the roster? Will Andy Pages be available? Is Roki Sasaki ready to return to his role as the Dodgers' vaunted postseason closer?
Every option to try to make up for these weaknesses is being considered. Even Hyeseong Kim, who has spent the majority of this season at Triple-A Oklahoma City.
"My expectation is Hyeseong will be here during the off-week and potentially be a conversation for the postseason — because he has the ability to run, play defense, and steal a base," Dave Roberts said, "So he's in the conversation, yes."
Alex Freeland is probably the most dispensable player on the Dodgers' active roster. If he's left behind, it'll be proof that their second base battle never truly declared a winner.
Dave Roberts hints at Hyeseong Kim return for Dodgers' postseason run
Kim was last seen in the majors from early April to late May. He was initially called up to replace Mookie Betts who went onto the injured list with an oblique strain. Kim hit .259 with a .651 OPS before being sent back down. His numbers in Triple-A have been nothing to write home about either (.675 OPS).
But Kim was on the Dodgers' postseason roster last season. His contributions were few — he earned a pinch-running appearance in the NLDS and was a defensive substitution during the World Series — and he didn't pick up a bat.
But Freeland is hot, and is hitting .375 with a 1.149 OPS over his last seven games. His ability to get on-base, the attribute that really put him on the map to begin with, has slowly come back to him. He has a .413 on-base percentage in September.
Clearly, this is a conversation the Dodgers are going to have to continue unless they trade one or both of these players. If Kim and Freeland survive the offseason together, they'll probably have to do it all over again next year.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Dodgers Lineup vs. Padres: Andy Pages, Roki Sasaki Are Back
item.dc:creator: Nelson Espinal
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are opening up for a blockbuster series, their last big test, against the San Diego Padres. Dodgers Lineup 1. Mookie Betts, SS 2. Freddie Freeman, 1B 3. Will Smith, C 4. Max Muncy, 3B 5. Kyle Tucker, RF 6. Teoscar Hernandez, LF 7. Josue De Paula, DH 8. Andy Pages, CF 9. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are opening up for a blockbuster series, their last big test, against the San Diego Padres.
Dodgers Lineup
1. Mookie Betts, SS
2. Freddie Freeman, 1B
3. Will Smith, C
4. Max Muncy, 3B
5. Kyle Tucker, RF
6. Teoscar Hernandez, LF
7. Josue De Paula, DH
8. Andy Pages, CF
9. Tommy Edman, 2B
Andy Pages is back in the batting order after being activated from the injured list. He broke his hand after getting hit by a pitch, had surgery, and after a month on the shelf, he is back.
It may take some time for him to shake off the rust at the plate, but his defense should not skip a beat.
The Dodgers are facing righty Michael King, but many of the hottest bats are righties.
Mookie Betts, Will Smith, and Kyle Tucker are among the most dialed-in hitters, and they should drive most of the offense.
Ideally, Freddie Freeman gets going again, since he hasn’t looked right in a while.
Who’s pitching for the Dodgers
The Dodgers will have Brock Stewart as the opener, with Roki Sasaki getting the bulk of the work out of the bullpen.
On Tuesday, hours before the game, Sasaki was activated off the injured list after recovering from his blister.
Sasaki has been great since the All-Star break, posting a 3.05 ERA with 37 strikeouts and 15 walks.
His splitter and slider are fantastic, while the fastball has been the difference-maker, showing some renewed life.
The Japanese righty is set to enter the bullpen in a varied role, either stepping in for a struggling starter or pitching late in high-leverage spots.
Stewart, meanwhile, has been a bit lucky, with a 2.55 ERA and a 3.91 FIP.
FanGraphs’ pitching models have appreciated his stuff and command, and while he has pitched better lately, he is prone to giving up hard contact.

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

23 Sep 2026, 02:10 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Kirby Lee)
The Los Angeles Dodgers activated a pair of key contributors in advance of a marquee series against the San Diego Padres, bringing back center fielder Andy Pages and right-hander Roki Sasaki from the injured list.
In corresponding moves, right-hander Emmet Sheehan and catcher Eliezer Alfonzo were optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Pages, 25, has not played since Aug. 21, when he was hit by a pitch on the left hand from Pittsburgh Pirates right-hander Bubba Chandler. An All-Star for the first time this season, Pages was batting .272 with 21 home runs and 80 RBIs in 128 games.
Sasaki, 24, last pitched Aug. 26 when he developed a blister on his right middle finger in an outing against the Atlanta Braves. He is 5-5 with a 4.60 ERA in 23 outings (all starts) this season and is scheduled to make an abbreviated appearance Tuesday.
Sheehan, 26, started the season in the Los Angeles rotation, was sent down in early August amid ongoing struggles and has returned for three outings this month where he recorded 24 strikeouts over 17 innings. He is 5-8 with a 4.57 ERA in 23 appearances (22 starts) this season.
Sheehan and Sasaki both are projected to have a bullpen role for the Dodgers in the playoffs, according to manager Dave Roberts.
Alfonzo, 26, made his major league debut in July and is batting .179 with four RBIs in 13 career games.
While the Dodgers enter Tuesday's play with a magic number of three to clinch a bye into a National League Division Series matchup, the Padres have a magic number of two to clinch a wild-card spot and a team-record third consecutive playoff appearance.
Also on Tuesday, the Dodgers sold Ryan Ward's contract to the Chunichi Dragons in Japan, according to multiple reports. A longtime minor leaguer, the 28-year-old Ward made his major league debut this season and hit three home runs in 20 games. The former Pacific Coast League MVP was designated for assignment last week.
--Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have activated outfielder Andy Pages and right-handed pitcher Roki Sasaki from the injured list ahead of Tuesday's series opener vs. the Padres and optioned right-handed pitcher Emmet Sheehan and catcher Eliezer Alfonzo to Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Pages, 25, has been out since August 21 after fracturing his left hand against the Pirates. The All-Star has played in 128 games, batting .272 with 21 homers and 80 RBI. He is in his third season with the Dodgers and he has played in 400 games with 61 homers and 212 RBI. He was signed by the Dodgers as an international free agent on March 1, 2018 out of La Habana, Cuba.
Sasaki, 24, has been on the injured list since August 27 with a blister on his right middle finger. In his second full season with the Dodgers, he is 5-5 with a 4.60 ERA, including a 2-0 record with a 3.05 ERA since the All-Star break. He has made 33 Major League appearances in his career, posting a 6-6 mark with a 4.57 ERA and 145 strikeouts in 155.2 innings. He joined the Dodgers as an international free agent on January 22, 2025 from Rikuzentakata, Japan.
Sheehan, 26, pitched 5.1 scoreless innings on Sunday against the Giants. He is 5-8 and a 4.57 ERA with the Dodgers in 2026, racking up 132 strikeouts in 112.1 innings. He is in his third season with the Dodgers, recording a 4.13 ERA with a 15-12 record in 51 games (45 starts). He was drafted by the Dodgers in the sixth round of the 2021 First Year Player Draft out of Boston College.
Alfonzo, 26, has played in 13 games for the Dodgers this season, batting .179 with two doubles and four RBI. He was batting .302 with two homers and 25 RBI with Triple-A Oklahoma City this season. He has appeared in 598 minor league games, batting .283 with 33 homers and 291 RBI. He signed with the Dodgers as a minor league free agent on November 17, 2025.

item.title: [True Blue LA] Dodgers activate Andy Pages, Roki Sasaki from injured list
item.dc:creator: Eric Stephen
item.description: LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers on Tuesday got a few regulars back as reinforcements heading into the final week of the regular season and into October, activating center fielder Andy Pages and pitcher Roki Sasaki off the injured list. Pages missed 27 games after getting hit by a fastball on his left hand on August 21. Sasaki left his start in Atlanta five days later with a blister on his right middle finger. Emmet Sheehan and catcher Eliezer Alfonzo were optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City on Monday.
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers on Tuesday got a few regulars back as reinforcements heading into the final week of the regular season and into October, activating center fielder Andy Pages and pitcher Roki Sasaki off the injured list.
Pages missed 27 games after getting hit by a fastball on his left hand on August 21. Sasaki left his start in Atlanta five days later with a blister on his right middle finger.
Emmet Sheehan and catcher Eliezer Alfonzo were optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City on Monday.
Pages was an All-Star starter this season, and when he got hurt was tied with Yoshinobu Yamamoto for second-highest FanGraphs WAR (3.9) on the team, behind only Shohei Ohtani. By Baseball Reference WAR, Pages is still third on the team now at 5.4, trailing only Ohtani and Yamamoto. That’ll happen with a .272/.338/.458 batting line with a 118 wRC+ combined with plus-defense in center field.
Before getting hit by an errant fastball on August 21, Pages started 125 of the Dodgers’ 129 games, and led the team in plate appearances (550) at the time. Pages and Ohtani are still tied for the Dodgers’ lead with 80 runs batted in. With Pages out, Alek Thomas was first called up to start six games in center field, followed by Tommy Edman starting 17 games, plus three starts by Alex Call and one by Kiké Hernández.
With Edman moving to the outfield and once Thomas was optioned, Miguel Rojas (10) and Alex Freeland (eight) have covered all but one of the starts at second base in September.
Sasaki struggled earlier in the season, but improved as the season progressed. He has a streak of six straight starts with no more than two runs allowed until his blister start in Atlanta. On the season, Sasaki has a 4.46 ERA and 4.42 xERA, but since July 8 he’s down to a 3.25 ERA and 3.76 xERA in eight starts.
With Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, and Tyler Glasnow set for the postseason rotation, the Dodgers will see over the next two weeks if Blake Snell will be hampered by his left groin discomfort, and will have Sheehan at the ready. That allows them to use Sasaki in relief, as they did last postseason out of necessity.
“I could see multiples [innings], but it’s not going to be bulk as in four or five innings,” manager Dave Roberts said on Sunday.
Last season was a different situation for Sasaki, who struggled mightily as a starter and spend four months on the injured list before returning in the final week of the regular season. There was no room in the rotation, so he pitched in relief in the postseason. He wasn’t dominant — only six strikeouts among his 43 batters faced, with five walks — but he was effective, allowing only one run over nine appearances and 10 2/3 innings, the highlight his perfect three innings of relief in the Dodgers’ NLDS Game 4 clincher over the Philadelphia Phillies.
Sasaki saved three games last postseason. Roberts said Sasaki probably wouldn’t get an opportunity in a save situation right away this week, but it could progress to that by the postseason.
“I trust Roki in any situation. I would say probably starting a clean inning,” Roberts said. “He’s done it, he’s really good. He’s a neutral pitcher, high-octane stuff. And you really just need four starters. So we’re in a good spot there, for now.”
Sheehan has been fantastic of late, allowing only one run in three starts for the Dodgers over the previous two weeks, with 24 strikeouts in 17 innings. The plan for Sheehan is to start on Saturday for Oklahoma City should the Comets advance to the Triple-A championship game.
Alfonzo was back with the Dodgers since September 6 when Dalton Rushing was placed on the injured list with elbow soreness. In the 14 games since, Alfonzo played only once, pinch-hitting as the designated hitter at the end of a 14-1 blowout of the Cincinnati Reds. He struck out.
Alfonzo made his major league debut against the Padres on July 5, and started nine games behind the plate. He had five hits in 28 at-bats with three doubles and four runs batted in.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers activated Andy Pages from the 10-day injured list and optioned Eliezer Alfonzo to Triple-A Oklahoma City. The move was made during the off day on Monday, but the Dodgers did not officially announce it at the time.
In addition, Roki Sasaki was also activated while Emmet Sheehan was optioned.
The Dodgers first recalled Alfonzo when Dalton Rushing was placed on the IL on Sept. 6. During his second stint with the club, Alfonzo only received one at-bat, which came against the Cincinnati Reds on Sept. 9 when he struck out.
Alfonzo was the third catcher on the roster, which Dodgers manager Dave Roberts explained was to allow the club to more freely use Will Smith and Hunter Feduccia as pinch-hitters when they didn’t start.
The Dodgers also did not need to make a 40-man roster move to call up Alfonzo, which likely played into their decision.
The 26-year-old has appeared in 13 total games this season, making his MLB debut and batting .179/.179/.250 with four RBI and three runs scored in 28 plate appearances. In Oklahoma City, he was hitting .302/.378/.409 in 256 plate appearances.
Pages is back with the Dodgers for the first time in a month after he landed on the IL with a left hand fracture on Aug. 22.
Pages suffered the injury when he was hit by a pitch from Pittsburgh Pirates starter Bubba Chandler. The 26-year-old underwent surgery shortly after to insert a compression screw in his hand to speed up the healing process.
Pages did not go on a rehab assignment before returning, but did workouts at Dodger Stadium, which included hitting on the field, running the bases, and doing outfield drills.
That makes this stretch of six games important for Pages to face live pitching and get as many at-bats as possible to prepare for the postseason. But even with that in mind, the Dodgers also have to be cautious about building him back up and not overworking him after a month of not playing.
“So we have obviously, assuming he gets back on Tuesday, then there’s six in a row, and that seems pretty aggressive,” Roberts explained.
“So I think that we do want to get him as many at-bats as possible, but we have to make sure that his legs are under him, feeling good, so we don’t go backward or get injured in that respect. So it is going to be a balancing act, and just keeping a keen eye on Andy for sure.”
Pages is batting .272/.338/.458 with 25 doubles, 21 home runs, 80 RBI and 72 runs scored this season. He has also been among the top defensive players in MLB.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are pacing toward having a first-round bye, avoiding the NL Wild Card round, and it would seem they are getting healthy at just the right time. The expectation in recent weeks was that Shohei Ohtani, Andy Pages, and Roki Sasaki would return before the end of the regular season, and the Dodgers quietly revealed the roster moves to map everything out.
Updating their transaction log overnight, the Dodgers have reinstated Pages and Sasaki from the IL, and optioned Emmet Sheehan and Eliezer Alfonzo to the minors. With Ohtani eligible to be reinstated from the IL on Wednesday, the expectation is that Alex Freeland will be the corresponding move.
For Ohtani and Pages, the goal was simply having them back before the start of the playoffs. They now have a runway to shake off the rust over these next handful of games, before likely having next week off before playing in the NLDS.
Circumstances are a little more dire for Sasaki, who hasn't secured a spot on LA's playoff roster. Dave Roberts has already confirmed that Sasaki will be used out of the bullpen upon his return, and it goes to one of the biggest questions facing the Dodgers ahead of the playoffs.
The Dodgers are getting healthy just in time, but there are still answers needed
The Dodgers need to find answers in the bullpen. Ironically, the stage is set for Sasaki to repeat a similar shift he made last season. While the Dodgers have been adamant that Sasaki's future is as a starting pitcher, he was used as a quasi-finisher during the playoffs last year, and thrived.
Considering the questions surrounding Edwin Diaz and Edgardo Henriquez currently dealing with an injury, Sasaki once again becoming an effective high-leverage option for the Dodgers would be a major development for the playoffs.
The story of the Dodgers since the trade deadline has been that they are leaking oil. Sure, they traded for Tarik Skubal, but the operation looked faulty. With the returns of Sasaki, Pages, and Ohtani likely on Wednesday, they are finally reaching a level of healthy they haven't had for most of the season.
In other words, despite how uneven things have looked, the Dodgers are once again in a position to do whay they do best and flip the swith on during the month of October.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] MLB Injury Report: Dodgers to get Shohei Ohtani, Andy Pages, and Roki Sasaki back for postseason run
item.dc:creator: Jorge Montanez
item.description: In this week's Injury Report, the Dodgers are getting a number of key players back this week as they prepare for another deep playoff run in their quest to three-peat. Alex Bregman hopes to return sometime in the postseason after suffering multiple facial fractures in a terrible, freak accident on the on-deck circle. And Dylan Cease has likely made his last start after experiencing shoulder fatigue. That and more in the final week's injury report. ⚾️ Baseball is back! MLB returns to NBC and Peac
item.content:encoded:
In this week's Injury Report, the Dodgers are getting a number of key players back this week as they prepare for another deep playoff run in their quest to three-peat. Alex Bregman hopes to return sometime in the postseason after suffering multiple facial fractures in a terrible, freak accident on the on-deck circle. And Dylan Cease has likely made his last start after experiencing shoulder fatigue. That and more in the final week's injury report.
⚾️ Baseball is back! MLB returns to NBC and Peacock in 2026! In addition to becoming the exclusive home of Sunday Night Baseball, NBC Sports will broadcast MLB Sunday Leadoff, "Opening Day" and Labor Day primetime games, the first round of the MLB Draft, the entire Wild Card round of the postseason, and much more.
Shohei Ohtani (knee, biceps)
Andy Pages (hand)
Blake Snell (groin)
Roki Sasaki (blister)
Ohtani has been out of action for the last two weeks, sidelined with lingering knee and biceps injuries. Manager Dave Roberts told reporters on Sunday that the 32-year-old star should be expected to return from the injured list and join the Dodgers lineup on Wednesday. Ohtani should be in the lineup for the remaining games to get some needed at-bats before the postseason. The team also gets Pages back this week, activating him from the injured list ahead of Tuesday's series opener against the Padres. He's been out for a month with a left hand fracture. The two additions this week are obviously a significant boost for a Dodgers team looking to three-peat. Their returns likely shift rookie Josue De Paula to a reserve or utility role.
On the pitching side, Snell left his start last Wednesday against the Reds with left groin tightness. He stated the issue was not serious and plans on making one more start before the postseason. That start isn't going to come when his spot in the rotation comes up on Tuesday, but the plan is for him to pitch over the weekend, according to Roberts.
From Yordan Alvarez to Zack Wheeler, an A-to-Z look at the players, performances, and trends that defined the 2026 MLB regular season.
Alex Bregman (face)
Bregman was struck by a foul ball while on the on-deck circle on Sunday against the Reds and was sent to the hospital, where he was diagnosed with multiple facial fractures. The freak accident is an unfortunate development this late in the season as the Cubs prepare to enter the playoffs. The team is hoping to get their 32-year-old star third baseman back at some point in the postseason, and it is a relief that the injury didn't result in anything more serious. Meanwhile, Sasaki was activated on Monday after missing some time with a blister issue and will pitch as a one-inning reliever, auditioning for a spot in the Dodgers bullpen in the postseason.
Dylan Cease (shoulder)
Cease has likely made his final start of the season. The 30-year-old right-hander underwent an MRI on his right shoulder over the weekend after experiencing some fatigue. The imaging revealed some shoulder inflammation, but no structural damage that would require surgery, and nothing that would bring into question his availability for next season. With the Blue Jays 3.5 games out of a Wild Card spot, it doesn't make much sense for Cease to push for one more start over the final weekend. If his season is indeed over, he'll end the year with a strong 2.40 ERA, 1.10 WHIP, and 239 strikeouts over 169 innings.
Andrés Muñoz (knee)
Muñoz left Sunday's game against the Rockies with a knee injury after giving up a home run and a walk. He was set to undergo an MRI on his right knee, the results of which are still unknown. The 27-year-old right-hander had a tough, disappointing season, posting a 4.24 ERA, 1.22 WHIP, and 89 strikeouts over 57 1/3 innings while converting 28 of 38 save chances. If he's unable to pitch over the final week, it could be Seranthony Domíguez closing out the remaining games.
Bryce Eldridge (concussion)
More Giants injuries that seemingly come out of nowhere. Eldridge was scratched from Friday's lineup against the Dodgers due to a head laceration after bumping his head on a low-hanging ceiling at the team hotel. He still "felt woozy" throughout the weekend and entered the concussion protocol before the team ultimately placed him on the 7-day concussion injured list. The move is retroactive to Friday, so there's a chance he could return for the final weekend series, though that's probably unlikely. The 21-year-old slugger flashed immense potential this season, hitting .269/.364/.461 with 17 homers and 57 RBI across 448 plate appearances.
Colt Keith (thumb)
Keith's season is over after the team placed him on the 10-day injured list with a left thumb sprain. It's an issue that the 25-year-old infielder has been playing through over the last several weeks. He ends the season hitting a modest .258/.322/.406 with 10 homers, 51 runs scored, 36 RBI, and six steals across 423 plate appearances.

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

22 Sep 2026, 03:25 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Denis Poroy)
The hottest team in baseball is racing toward a playoff berth, and the San Diego Padres can complete the chase as early as Tuesday's opener of a three-game road series against the Los Angeles Dodgers.
The Padres (87-69) have won 13 of their last 14 games to not only climb out of wild-card uncertainty but also give themselves a legitimate chance at clinching the National League's top wild-card spot over their final six regular-season games.
They can clinch a playoff spot Tuesday with a win and an Arizona Diamondbacks loss to the Colorado Rockies.
A postseason appearance would be the third consecutive for San Diego, which has never delivered a similar run in franchise history.
'This is so fun,' said Jake Cronenworth, who had two home runs and five RBIs for San Diego in its 7-3 home victory over the Miami Marlins on Sunday. 'It's hard to compare each (of the past three playoff chases). Each one's so fun in its own way and unique. But this one's been really awesome.'
Fernando Tatis Jr. added a home run, his 25th, and is batting .310 with 12 home runs and a 1.016 OPS over his past 30 games since Aug. 18.
Against their Southern California rival, the Padres are expected to send right-hander Michael King (12-9, 3.03 ERA) to the mound.
King is 4-0 with a 1.41 ERA over his last five starts and is 1-1 with a 3.12 ERA in three starts against the Dodgers this season, including an outing in May when he went seven scoreless innings. That start included a season-high nine strikeouts.
The Dodgers (96-60) also have plenty to play for after clinching the National League West title last week. They are two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers for the best record in the NL but do not hold the tiebreaker between the teams.
Los Angeles is 14-3 since Sept. 3 and has a magic number of three to clinch a top-two spot in the NL and a bye into the NL Division Series.While the Padres are on a five-game winning streak, the Dodgers have won four in a row after completing a three-game home sweep of the San Francisco Giants.
Tommy Edman hit a game-tying home run in the sixth inning for Los Angeles on Sunday, while Enrique Hernandez had a go-ahead RBI double in the seventh.
While right-hander Roki Sasaki (5-5, 4.60) is set to return from a blister issue, he will have an abbreviated outing and not necessarily as the starter. Manager Dave Roberts characterized the pitching plan as more of a bullpen game.
The Dodgers are also expected to see the return of center fielder Andy Pages for the series opener against the Padres. Pages has not played since Aug. 21 because of a broken hand.
While the Dodgers have found some success over the past three-plus weeks following a lackluster two months, their 14-3 run has not come against teams who are in playoff contention. A visit from the Padres changes that.
'I think it's going to be a good kind of primer,' Roberts said. 'They're a very talented team. They're playing as good as anyone in all of baseball. I'm looking forward to playing those guys and just kind of ramping it up a little bit more for our guys.'
--Field Level Media

■ポストシーズンへ頼もしいピースが帰還
ドジャースの佐々木朗希投手が、15日間の負傷者リスト（IL）からアクティブロースターに復帰した。MLB公式サイトが21日（日本時間22日）に公示した。
シーズン大詰めを迎えるドジャースにとって、これ以上ない朗報だ。右手中指マメのため調整を続けていた佐々木だったが、10月のポストシーズンを見据える大事な局面で戦線へ戻ってきた。
デーブ・ロバーツ監督は20日（同21日）の試合後、「次のシリーズではブルペンの一員として起用される見込みだ」とコメント。22日（同23日）から本拠地で行われるパドレス戦でブルペンに配置転換されることが決まった。
圧倒的な球威と勝負強さを誇る右腕の復帰は、ワールドシリーズ3連覇を狙う上でのやりくりにおいて絶大なインパクトを与える。連覇を狙うドジャースの「切り札」として、終盤戦の投手陣を強力に牽引することが期待される。
また、アンディ・パヘス外野手も10日間のILから復帰。代わって、エリエセル・アルフォンゾ捕手とエメ・シーハン投手が3Aオクラホマにマイナーオプションで降格となっている。（Full-Count編集部）

item.title: [thebiglead.com] Dodgers activate two key players immediately before big Padres series
item.dc:creator: J P Hoornstra
item.description: With one week left in the MLB regular season, the Los Angeles Dodgers are getting two key players back for a three-game home series against the San Diego Padres. Pitcher Roki Sasaki and center fielder Andy Pages, who have been on the injured list since August, were activated from it on Monday, an off day for the Dodgers and Padres. item.content:encoded:
With one week left in the MLB regular season, the Los Angeles Dodgers are getting two key players back for a three-game home series against the San Diego Padres.
Pitcher Roki Sasaki and center fielder Andy Pages, who have been on the injured list since August, were activated from it on Monday, an off day for the Dodgers and Padres. The two National League West rivals can each clinch something important at Dodger Stadium—a berth in the postseason for San Diego and a first-round bye for Los Angeles.
Sasaki posted a 3.05 ERA in seven starts after the All-Star break but developed a blister on his throwing hand in August. Pages played in his first All-Star Game in July but fractured a bone in his right hand when he was hit by a 100.2 mph fastball from Pittsburgh Pirates starter Bubba Chandler on Aug. 21.
The Dodgers were able to clinch the National League West without the two players, but both figure to play key roles in October for the defending World Series champions.
Postseason roles
The team lost hard-throwing reliever Edgardo Henriquez to a back injury earlier this month. For all his second-half success as a starter, the Dodgers need Sasaki more in their bullpen as a right-handed complement to left-handers Tanner Scott and Alex Vesia.
Pages, meanwhile, was excelling at the plate and in the field prior to his injury, which required surgery. He’ll have six games to tune up for the postseason—and a chance at redemption for last October.
The Dodgers won the World Series even though Pages had only four hits in 16 postseason games, managing just an .078 batting average across four playoff rounds.
Without Pages, the Dodgers moved veteran utilityman Tommy Edman to center field. Through week’s end, he was slashing .245/.328/.376 (94 OPS+) in 79 games this season.
The Dodgers are also expecting Shohei Ohtani to return during the Padres series, but he isn’t eligible to be activated from the 15-day injured list before Wednesday.
In corresponding 26-man roster moves, pitcher Emmet Sheehan and catcher Eliezer Alfonzo were optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City.

item.title: [FanSided] Dave Roberts' handling of Roki Sasaki shows why the Dodgers keep winning
item.dc:creator: Jake Elman
item.description: If you needed yet another reminder of why Dave Roberts has led the Los Angeles Dodgers to three championships in six years, look no further than his treatment of Roki Sasaki. Roberts has both built Sasaki up and held the Japanese import accountable through two up-and-down seasons. He hasn’t been stubbornly loyal to the 24-year-old righty, nor has he waved the white flag amid Sasaki’s continued control issues. As Sasaki nears a return from the IL, Roberts confirmed that Sasaki will start pitching
item.content:encoded:
If you needed yet another reminder of why Dave Roberts has led the Los Angeles Dodgers to three championships in six years, look no further than his treatment of Roki Sasaki.
Roberts has both built Sasaki up and held the Japanese import accountable through two up-and-down seasons. He hasn’t been stubbornly loyal to the 24-year-old righty, nor has he waved the white flag amid Sasaki’s continued control issues.
As Sasaki nears a return from the IL, Roberts confirmed that Sasaki will start pitching out of the bullpen this week. All signs point to Sasaki serving as a reliever for the second straight postseason.
Sasaki has missed nearly all of September with a hip injury, and he should have some extra time to recover. The Dodgers are closing in one of the NL’s top two playoff seeds, which includes a first-round bye.
Does Roki Sasaki deserve to make the Los Angeles Dodgers’ playoff roster?
Before looking ahead to October, let’s quickly travel back to this past spring. I repeatedly questioned Sasaki’s viability as an MLB starter, largely because of his control and what felt like an inability to handle the pressure associated with pitching Stateside.
Honestly? I really haven’t changed my opinion, though I’ll give Sasaki his flowers. He’s played some of his best baseball in the second half, recording a 3.05 ERA in seven starts. That’s down from 5.33 over 15 first-half outings, though he’s still struggling to make it through five innings.
Most importantly, he’s significantly cut down on his homers, allowing three in 38.1 innings. That’s a fantastic improvement from the 19 long balls he gave up in 81 first-half innings.
So what’s the problem? Walks. I’m old school, so I don’t like young pitchers only working five innings because they can’t hit the strike zone. Sasaki has issued 15 free passes in those 38.1 innings, and it drives up his pitch count.
At the end of the day, Sasaki has completed six innings in just seven of his 22 starts. Now is the perfect time to permanently transition him to a relief role.
But we asked whether Sasaki deserves to be on the playoff roster, and despite my criticism, the answer is an easy “yes.” There’s something to be said about a young player admitting to confidence issues yet powering through and trying to make things work rather than let things spiral.
What’s especially admirable about Sasaki is that he doesn’t complain or make himself out to be a victim. He’s never targeted the media, which has actually had his back for much of the last two years. He’s certainly not teammate Kyle Tucker, whose body language and work ethic have raised red flags dating back to his brief stint with the Cubs.
Maybe Sasaki is the Dodgers’ secret playoff weapon once again. We’d certainly feel more comfortable trusting him in October instead of embattled former closer Edwin Díaz.
Yikes. Imagine reading that on Opening Day.

佐々木朗希の配置転換の裏に潜むド軍の思惑 現実味を帯び始める108億守護神の“ロースター外し”「物事は計画通りに進んでない」
浮かない表情で球団幹部たちを話し込むディアス(C)Getty Images
米球界はMLBのレギュラーシーズンがいよいよ大詰めを迎え、ポストシーズンに向けた編成の動きも活発化しつつある。現地時間9月20日には、ドジャースのデーブ・ロバーツ監督は、負傷者リスト（IL）入りしている佐々木朗希を復帰後から救援起用をしていく意向を明らかにした。
今季の佐々木は開幕から23試合すべてで「先発」として投げてきた。しかし、「ポストシーズンに先発は基本的に4人いればいい」と持論を語ったロバーツ監督は、山本由伸、タリク・スクバル、ブレーク・スネル、タイラー・グラスノーを先発ローテーションの軸にする考えを示した。
もっとも、「どんな状況だろうと、ロウキを信頼している」と強調するロバーツ監督をはじめとするドジャース首脳陣の決断には、スター軍団が抱える不安が見え隠れする。それは「絶対的守護神」として君臨するはずだったエドウィン・ディアスのコンディション不良だ。
FAとなった昨オフに3年総額6900万ドル（約108億円＝当時のレート）の大型契約を締結したディアスだったが、開幕直後に右肘の関節遊離体除去手術を受けて離脱。丹念なリハビリを終えて7月9日にようやく復帰を果たすも内容は鳴かず飛ばず。今季ここまで18登板で、防御率10.34、WHIP2.36、被打率.361、与四球率6.32、被OPS1.043とキャリアワーストの水準に落ち込んでいる。

item.content:encoded:
Entering the final week of the regular season, the Dodgers more or less know their postseason fate.
They've locked up the National League West. They are a seemingly safe four games clear of the Atlanta Braves for a first-round bye. And, unless they can close a two-game gap on the Milwaukee Brewers without holding the tiebreaker, they will finish as the NL's No. 2 seed, getting home-field advantage at least for the NL Division Series.
Thus, the real intrigue for now is who might be on the Dodgers' postseason roster when the playoffs begin next month.
This year, injuries and fluctuating performances have forced them to cycle 53 different players through their clubhouse.
And while the core of the group is clear, many questions remain about how the club will construct its lineup and pitching staff for this fall's pursuit of a third-straight World Series.
Here is the California Post's best guess about how it will all shake out.
Lineup locks
Will Smith, Freddie Freeman, Tommy Edman, Mookie Betts, Max Muncy, Teoscar Hernández, Andy Pages, Kyle Tucker, Shohei Ohtani, Kiké Hernández, Miguel Rojas, Hunter Feduccia
There won't be any big surprises in how the Dodgers line up to begin the playoffs, assuming Ohtani is healthy enough to resume everyday DH'ing duties.
Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker have cemented their place as everyday hitters thanks to late-season surges. Andy Pages is due back on Tuesday from a fractured hand. Freddie Freeman still seems somewhat limited by his right knee injury, but has nonetheless been able to manage it well enough to this point. And while Tommy Edman has been slumping lately, he doesn't seem to be in immediate danger of losing at-bats.
On the bench, Hunter Feduccia has locked up the back-up catching job, and could be a left-handed hitting option as a pinch-hitter. Kiké Hernández and Miguel Rojas, meanwhile, each provide versatile defensive depth, as well as extensive track records for postseason heroics when called upon.
Entering the final week of the regular season, the core of the Dodgers' position player group looks as they expected.
Dodgers Lineup questions
Bubble candidates: Josue De Paula, Dalton Rushing, Alex Call, Alex Freeland, Hyeseong Kim
The Dodgers will still have one, if not two, position player spots to fill depending on how they construct their roster (i.e. an even 13 pitchers/13 hitters, or a 12/14 split like they used last year?)
And for those, they could have a number of difficult decisions.
First and foremost: Will Josue De Paula make the playoff roster?
If he does, it will likely be as a left-handed bench bat; though if there is any lingering uncertainty with Ohtani, he could also provide insurance as a backup DH option. His main competition right now figures to be Alex Call (who might be redundant to Rojas and Hernández as a right-handed bench bat) or Dalton Rushing (who is an intriguing alternative as a left-handed bat, but remains sidelined from the setback he suffered with his elbow injury earlier this month).
In just 10 MLB games, De Paula has quickly built a strong case, showing supreme plate discipline (10 walks to only four strikeouts) and the potential for power (three doubles, one home run, seven RBIs). At this point, it might be more of a surprise if he doesn't make it.
If the Dodgers elect to carry an extra position player on top of that, the choices are even more varied.
Last year, they rostered two base-running/defensive specialists throughout the playoffs in infielder Hyeseong Kim and outfielder Justin Dean. Dean is now gone, and Hernández could serve as a late-game defensive outfield replacement anyway. But Kim remains in consideration, manager Dave Roberts said, thanks to his speed and infield glove. Alex Freeland could also factor in here, as someone capable of providing more at the plate.
Lineup projection for Los Angeles
C: Will Smith
1B: Freddie Freeman
2B: Tommy Edman
SS: Mookie Betts
3B: Max Muncy
LF: Teoscar Hernández
CF: Andy Pages
RF: Kyle Tucker
DH: Shohei Ohtani
Bench: Kiké Hernández, Miguel Rojas, Hunter Feduccia, Josue De Paula, Hyeseong Kim*
*If the Dodgers carry 14 position players
Dodgers pitching staff locks
Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow, Roki Sasaki, Tanner Scott, Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips
The Dodgers' starting rotation is set, assuming no further setbacks with Blake Snell's groin injury. The back end of the bullpen has come into focus, too, with Tanner Scott and/or Roki Sasaki the most logical candidates to serve as closer, and Alex Vesia and Evan Phillips separating themselves as the team's next most-trusted high-leverage relief options.
The only real question here is how the Dodgers will line up the rotation. Yamamoto-Skubal would make sense for Games 1 and 2 of a division series (keeping them both on-line for a potential Game 5). But could Tyler Glasnow's potential issues with traveling tempt the Dodgers to use him primarily at home, if they can? All factors to consider in the coming weeks.
Pitching staff questions
Roster bubble candidates: Brock Stewart, Edwin Díaz, Blake Treinen, Kris Bubic, Jack Dreyer, Emmet Sheehan, Justin Wrobleski, Edgardo Henriquez, Will Klein, Eric Lauer
The first thing the Dodgers need to figure out here is health.
Edgardo Henriquez will almost certainly be on the playoff roster, and pitching in a high-leverage role, if he can make a full recovery from his recent back strain. Will Klein and Eric Lauer might also be available health-wise, though lack clear roles to step immediately back into.
Otherwise, the Dodgers will effectively have at least four open spots for six to seven other pitchers.
For added right-handed depth, they might be deciding between Brock Stewart (who has been a go-to weapon against right-handed hitters recently), Edwin Díaz (who is trying to salvage his dismal debut season, and did throw a pair of scoreless outings this weekend) and Blake Treinen (who has curiously pitched only five times in three weeks since being activated from the injured list, and not in the highest of leverage).
For another left-handed option, they could go with Kris Bubic (the trade deadline acquisition who has impressed with three scoreless appearances since returning from an injury) or Jack Dreyer (who was one of the Dodgers' best relievers from June to August, but has given up five runs in his last seven outings).
And for a multi-inning role, they will have Emmet Sheehan (who has looked like a different pitcher in three sterling starts since returning from a minor-league demotion) and Justin Wrobleski (the breakout All-Star who has finally shaken some of his home run problems since moving to the bullpen).
There are many permutations that the Dodgers could employ depending on opponent. They're still figuring out the exact hierarchy of all their bullpen arms, too.
But as long as their rotation is dominant, everything else should take care of itself.
Pitching staff projection
Rotation: Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow
Bullpen: Roki Sasaki, Tanner Scott, Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips, Brock Stewart, Kris Bubic, Edwin Díaz, Emmet Sheehan, Justin Wrobleski

item.title: [Dodger Blue] Dodgers manager Dave Roberts reveals new role for Roki Sasaki
item.dc:creator: Matt Borelli
item.description: Roki Sasaki is among the players expected to rejoin the Los Angeles Dodgers this week as they inch closer to full strength ahead of the postseason. The right-hander has been on the 15-day injured list since Aug. 27 due to a blister on his right middle finger, but made steady progress throughout his recovery. He has thrown multiple bullpen sessions and live batting practices this month, including 48 pitches over four innings last Wednesday. Sasaki was originally slated to return as a starting pit
item.content:encoded:
Roki Sasaki is among the players expected to rejoin the Los Angeles Dodgers this week as they inch closer to full strength ahead of the postseason.
The right-hander has been on the 15-day injured list since Aug. 27 due to a blister on his right middle finger, but made steady progress throughout his recovery. He has thrown multiple bullpen sessions and live batting practices this month, including 48 pitches over four innings last Wednesday.
Sasaki was originally slated to return as a starting pitcher, but he now appears headed to the bullpen for the remainder of the 2026 season. The 24-year-old is capable of pitching multiple innings as a reliever, but not in the traditional sense of a bulk pitcher.
“I can see multiples, but it’s not going to be bulk as in four or five innings. It won’t be that,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of Sasaki’s role.
Sasaki won’t be limited to simply providing length out of the bullpen. Roberts also indicated that he would feel comfortable using him in high-leverage situations, but only at the start of a “clean inning.”
As for whether Sasaki could get save opportunities, it’s something that Roberts might consider down the road.
“It won’t be in the ninth the first time, but it potentially could fall out (that way),” the Dodgers skipper said.
Tanner Scott has been the Dodgers’ primary closer in recent weeks, but Edwin Díaz recently returned from the 15-day IL and is hoping to eventually reclaim the role. Edgardo Henriquez also received save opportunities prior to landing on the IL with lower back discomfort.
Roki Sasaki’s postseason success
Sasaki shined as a reliever during the Dodgers’ World Series run last year, pitching to a minuscule 0.84 ERA and 1.03 WHIP with three saves in nine appearances. His previous success on baseball’s biggest stage played a role in the team’s decision to once again move him to the bullpen.
“Yeah. He’s done it, he’s really good, he’s a neutral pitcher, high-octane stuff,” Roberts said. “You really just need four starters, so we’re in a good spot there for now.”
Along with Sasaki, the Dodgers’ postseason bullpen could include other traditional starters such as Justin Wrobleski and Emmet Sheehan. The club’s starting rotation will feature two of the league’s best arms in Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tarik Skubal.

item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers hoped to keep pitcher Roki Sasaki stretched out as rotation depth as the postseason approaches. That move to the bullpen will continue throughout of the postseason. Sasaki had worked strictly as a starter befo
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers hoped to keep pitcher Roki Sasaki stretched out as rotation depth as the postseason approaches. Instead, the Dodgers will begin their playoff plans for Sasaki as soon as he is activated from the Injured List.
Sonja Chen of MLB.com reported that manager Dave Roberts said Sasaki will be available out of the bullpen beginning with their series against the Padres. That move to the bullpen will continue throughout of the postseason.
Sasaki had worked strictly as a starter before landing on the IL. Although his overall performance - a 4.60 ERA and a 1.332 WHiP over his 119.1 innings - is still far from what was expected when he signed during the 2024-25 offseason, it is a step in the right direction. Sasaki struck out 117 batters with 48 walks in that time as he improved his K/9 and BB/9 rates over his rookie campaign.
The Dodgers are hoping that Sasaki can replicate his success from the 2025 postseason. He quickly became one of the few relievers Roberts could trust as the Dodgers marched to a second consecutive World Series title, moving into high-leverage situations while seeing action as their closer. He posted a 0.84 ERA and a 1.031 WHiP over his 10.2 innings in the 2025 postseason, recording three saves while striking out six batters with five walks.
In some ways, the Los Angeles Dodgers are still trying to figure out what they have in Sasaki. If he can replicate his success during the postseason, the Dodgers may be closer to having an answer.

item.title: [MLB.com] Teen who plays ball at Ohtani's old high school nails her 1st pitch at Dodger Stadium
item.dc:creator: Ayako Oikawa
item.description: Yuri Teramoto wore the same number as one of her childhood idols and stood on a mound that has been graced by generations of baseball legends. What was going through Teramoto’s mind as she prepared to throw? Teramoto, a freshman at Hanamaki Higashi High School in Iwate Prefecture, Japan, threw out the ceremonial first pitch Sunday at Dodger Stadium before the Dodgers faced the Giants. The 16-year-old right-hander stands 5-foot-10 and can throw as hard as 73 mph. With Dodgers pitcher Roki Sasaki
item.content:encoded:
Yuri Teramoto wore the same number as one of her childhood idols and stood on a mound that has been graced by generations of baseball legends. What was going through Teramoto’s mind as she prepared to throw?
Teramoto, a freshman at Hanamaki Higashi High School in Iwate Prefecture, Japan, threw out the ceremonial first pitch Sunday at Dodger Stadium before the Dodgers faced the Giants.
The 16-year-old right-hander stands 5-foot-10 and can throw as hard as 73 mph. With Dodgers pitcher Roki Sasaki behind the plate, Teramoto delivered a strong pitch. The crowd erupted as the ball landed in Sasaki’s glove.
“This is a dream for anyone who plays baseball. It’s amazing.”
Teramoto looked around the enormous stadium, visibly thrilled by the moment.
Hanamaki Higashi is the high school that produced MLB stars Yusei Kikuchi and Shohei Ohtani, as well as Rintaro Sasaki, who was selected by the Miami Marlins in the 2026 MLB Draft. Roki Sasaki, who served as Teramoto’s catcher, also grew up in Iwate.
The trip was part of a youth development program organized by Iwate Prefecture and Iwate Nippo to mark the prefecture’s 150th anniversary and 15 years since the Great East Japan Earthquake and tsunami. Fifty high school students from Iwate, including Teramoto, traveled along the U.S. West Coast from Sept. 15-22.
On Sept. 19, the group visited Angel Stadium, where the students met Kikuchi and watched him throw a bullpen session. Teramoto watched closely as Kikuchi fired pitch after pitch into the catcher’s mitt, seeing firsthand what it takes to compete on a major league mound.
The following day, the group arrived at Dodger Stadium. This time, it was Teramoto’s turn to take the mound.
“I’m nervous, but I’m also really excited,” she said before the first pitch.
Once she stepped onto the mound, the nerves seemed to disappear. She delivered with confidence and finished the moment she had been dreaming about.
Teramoto moved from Kumamoto Prefecture in southern Japan to Iwate this spring to attend Hanamaki Higashi. Ohtani played a major role in her decision.
“Ohtani is someone I’ve always looked up to,” she said. “Whenever I struggle with baseball, I read books about him and use them as motivation. I’ve learned from the way he sets goals, and it has helped me enjoy practice more.”
There are increasingly more high schools with girls’ baseball programs in Kumamoto and elsewhere in Kyushu. But Teramoto chose to move nearly 900 miles north to Hanamaki Higashi because, she said, “it gives me an environment where I can focus on studying and baseball.”
With only three years of high school ahead of her, Teramoto wants to make every day count -- both in the classroom and on the field. That mindset helped convince her to leave home and pursue her dreams in Iwate.
And those dreams already extend beyond Japan.
“Someday, I want to study in the United States and play baseball here, too,” she said.
At Hanamaki Higashi, Teramoto wears No. 17, the same number Ohtani wore as a high school player. The number has also been worn by other Hanamaki Higashi standouts, including Kikuchi and Rintaro Sasaki.
“It’s my favorite number, too, so I’m really happy to wear it.”
On Sunday, “IWATE 17” was emblazoned across her back as she stood on the Dodger Stadium mound and fired her best pitch toward her hometown hero’s teammate.
Girls’ baseball has continued to grow in popularity in Japan in recent years, with more players taking up the sport. When Hanamaki Higashi established its girls’ baseball program, Ohtani donated a batting machine to the school.
“We use it every day. I’m really grateful for it,” Teramoto said.
The movement to support girls’ baseball is also gaining momentum. Earlier this month, Ichiro Suzuki played an exhibition game at Tokyo Dome against a selection of Japan’s top high school girls’ baseball players.
For a region that once struggled to produce even professional baseball players, Iwate has now become home to a remarkable baseball lineage. Kikuchi, Ohtani and Roki Sasaki have all gone from the prefecture to the biggest stage in the sport, while Rintaro Sasaki is now pursuing his own path toward the majors with the Marlins organization.
Now, Teramoto is following in their footsteps. With “IWATE 17” on her back, it was one small step toward carrying the dreams of those who came before her into the next generation.

item.dc:creator: Matt Sullivan
item.description: Why Dodgers have MLB's top-ranked playoff rotation even without Shohei Ohtani originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here. With his attempt to return to the mound not going well, he's not expected to pitch again for the Dodgers this season. When he comes back off the IL, he'll slot into the DH r
item.content:encoded:
Why Dodgers have MLB's top-ranked playoff rotation even without Shohei Ohtani originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Los Angeles Dodgers got some tough news in early July when Shohei Ohtani was taken off the mound and forced into a DH-only role for a while.
With his attempt to return to the mound not going well, he's not expected to pitch again for the Dodgers this season. When he comes back off the IL, he'll slot into the DH role as usual. But the Dodgers' rotation is more than capable without him.
ESPN's Kiley McDaniel ranked the Dodgers' rotation as the best in baseball, even if Ohtani isn't there. The reason why is simple: Los Angeles is stacked with starting pitchers, both in terms of high-end options and depth pieces.
Why Dodgers' rotation is best in MLB for playoffs even without Shohei Ohtani
"Yep, the Dodgers are still tops in this category -- even with the currently injured Shohei Ohtani likely not pitching again this season -- and by a pretty good margin," McDaniel writes. "They could start four arms over a seven-game series that are all better than any one arm on five or six of the teams listed below."
Of all the postseason teams this year, the Dodgers' rotation has four starters who could be those teams' No. 1 starting pitchers.
Tarik Skubal and Yoshinobu Yamamoto are the Dodgers' best starters, and they'd likely be the Game 1 and Game 2 starters if the Dodgers could choose who takes the mound.
After those two are Tyler Glasnow and Blake Snell, two incredible starters who have a very high ceiling and would be the No. 1 starter for teams like the San Diego Padres, Chicago Cubs, and Chicago White Sox.
That four-man starting rotation is probably more than good enough to consider this Dodgers' rotation the best in baseball. But they also have some incredible depth options.
Justin Wrobleski is an incredible No. 5 starter. Kris Bubic and Emmett Sheehan probably won't start a playoff game for the Dodgers, but they would be capable No. 4 starting pitchers on most playoff teams.
For the Dodgers, those two are likely to be key bullpen arms. That's not to mention Roki Sasaki, who's going to return to the bullpen for the Dodgers in October as they look to win a third straight title.
The Dodgers have eight starting pitching options that could reasonably start a playoff game, and no one would bat an eye. It's an incredibly deep rotation, and that's without factoring in Ohtani. That's how good this rotation is. No other team can compare.

item.content:encoded:
We’ve made it to the final week of the regular season. There are still two divisions in the American League up for grabs, a couple of long-shot playoff hopefuls looking to make a last-minute run, and playoff seeding to fight over. It should make for a dramatic end to a great season.
Our power rankings use a modified Elo rating system. If you’re familiar with chess rankings, you’ll know that Elo is an elegant ranking format that measures teams’ relative strength and is very reactive to recent performance. To avoid overweighting recent results during the season, we weigh each team’s raw Elo rank using our coin flip playoff odds (specifically, we regress the playoff odds by 50% and weigh those against the raw Elo ranking, increasing in weight as the season progresses to a maximum of 25%). The weighted Elo ranks are then displayed as “Power Score” in the tables below. As the best and worst teams sort themselves out between now and October, they’ll filter to the top and bottom of the rankings, while the exercise remains reactive to hot streaks and cold snaps. If you’re looking for a visual representation of the ups and downs of your team throughout the season, look no further than the brand new Power Rankings Board in the FanGraphs Lab.
First up are the full rankings, presented in a sortable table. Below that, I’ve grouped the teams into tiers with comments on a handful of clubs. You’ll notice that the official ordinal rankings don’t always match the tiers — there are times where I take editorial liberties when grouping teams together — but generally, the ordering is consistent. One thing to note: The playoff odds listed in the tables below are our standard Depth Charts odds, not the coin flip odds that are used in the ranking formula.
