It was a great week for the Brewers. They won their fourth straight NL Central title and sixth in the last nine years, and also set another franchise record for wins in a single season, one year after setting the previous record. They now have a chance to win 100 games for the first time in club history this week and still have the top seed in the NL to play for.
The Rays swept the Athletics and won their series against the Red Sox last week to put some distance between themselves and the Yankees in the AL East race. The gap in the division is now six games, and even though the two rivals play each other four times during the final week of the season, it would take a massive collapse from Tampa Bay to upset the current standings. Because the Rays also currently lead the season series with the Yankees, 6-3, all they need is to win one of the four games in New York to take the division title. With Shane McClanahan still recovering from his forearm injury — his availability for the playoffs is up in the air — Freddy Peralta has stepped up to lead the pitching staff over the last few weeks. Across his last five starts, he’s allowed just three runs in 28 2/3 innings. That’s the kind of production the Rays were hoping to get when they acquired him at the trade deadline.
| Team | Record | Elo | Opponent Elo | Playoff Odds | Power Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dodgers | 96-60 | 1580 | 1492 | 100.0% | 1621 |
| Padres | 87-69 | 1578 | 1501 | 97.2% | 1618 |
| Braves | 92-64 | 1565 | 1500 | 100.0% | 1610 |
| Yankees | 89-66 | 1556 | 1497 | 100.0% | 1603 |
The Dodgers are getting all their pieces in place for the postseason. Andy Pages and Roki Sasaki will be activated off the IL on Tuesday, and Shohei Ohtani should follow on Wednesday. There’s a lingering question about Blake Snell’s status after he injured his groin last week, but it sounds like he’ll be able to make a start during the final weekend of the season. And even though the majority of the year has been a slog for Kyle Tucker, his bat seems to have finally woken up at the right time; he collected nine hits and three home runs last week.
Having won 13 of their last 14 games, the Padres are peaking at exactly the right moment. They’ve surged five games ahead of the Diamondbacks and one ahead of the Phillies in the NL Wild Card standings, and are now tied with the Cubs for the top spot. San Diego’s final series of the season against Arizona still looms large, especially if the Friars stumble against the Dodgers in the series beforehand. You’re probably familiar with Fernando Tatis Jr.’s hot streak — he blasted four home runs last week to bring his total in September up to eight — but the biggest contributor to the Padres’ success recently has been Ty France. He had 12 hits and a home run last week and has posted a fantastic 168 wRC+ during the second half of the season.
After a couple of years away from the top, the Braves are NL East champions again — it’s their seventh division title in the last nine years. Atlanta’s dominance this year has been a welcome return to form. Even though his season has been a bit up and down, Ronald Acuña Jr. is looking like the superstar that won the MVP back in 2023 again. Last week, he smacked three home runs, including a go-ahead grand slam on Saturday, and is running a 191 wRC+ in September.
A little more than a week after being activated off the IL, Aaron Judge is back on the shelf, this time with a calf injury sustained on Wednesday. His availability for the playoffs is still up in the air, though he’s confident that he’ll be able to return sooner rather than later. Thankfully, Jazz Chisholm Jr. should be activated off the IL on Tuesday, and there’s some confidence that Trent Grisham will also be ready to return for the postseason. It helps that Ben Rice has bounced back from a rough August to post a 192 wRC+ in September. Still, Judge’s injury is a major blow to the Yankees’ hopes for a deep October run.
| Team | Record | Elo | Opponent Elo | Playoff Odds | Power Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Red Sox | 84-72 | 1544 | 1500 | 100.0% | 1594 |
| Phillies | 86-70 | 1546 | 1501 | 97.3% | 1593 |
| Cubs | 87-69 | 1539 | 1501 | 99.9% | 1590 |
Even though the Red Sox lost both of their series last week, they managed to clinch a postseason berth on Sunday. It’s the cap to a remarkable turnaround after the team looked completely lost in mid-June. Boston can officially secure the second Wild Card spot with a couple of wins against the Guardians this week. Then the team can turn its attention to the Yankees and the rematch of last year’s Wild Card matchup between these two historic rivals.
Nothing is going to come easy for the Phillies over the next few weeks. The team placed Jesús Luzardo on the IL last week with a shoulder injury, but thankfully, it sounds like he’ll be ready to pitch in the playoffs. But before they count their chickens, they need to actually clinch a playoff spot. Philadelphia is four games up on the Diamondbacks in the NL Wild Card race, but its upcoming opponents are no cake walk; the Phillies have the Brewers and Rays on the schedule to finish off the regular season. Facing two of the best teams in baseball is quite a test ahead of the postseason, and the Phillies haven’t exactly been playing well lately.
The biggest concern for the Cubs right now is the status of Alex Bregman. He was struck by a foul ball in the face while standing in the on-deck circle during Sunday’s game and was taken to the hospital for further evaluation. Alongside Pete Crow-Armstrong, Bregman has been one of the best hitters in baseball since the All-Star break. It would be a huge blow if the third baseman had to miss any significant amount of time at this point in the season. As for Crow-Armstrong, he’s two stolen bases away from joining the 40/40 club. He put a few finishing touches on his MVP case last week by bopping four more home runs, bringing his season total up to 45.
| Team | Record | Elo | Opponent Elo | Playoff Odds | Power Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Guardians | 81-75 | 1520 | 1498 | 97.6% | 1572 |
| White Sox | 80-76 | 1494 | 1500 | 96.2% | 1552 |
| Rangers | 78-78 | 1502 | 1496 | 56.5% | 1517 |
| Astros | 77-79 | 1493 | 1493 | 45.8% | 1481 |
There was some upheaval in the two division races represented in this tier. Entering last week one game behind the White Sox in the AL Central standings, the Guardians took two of three games against the South Siders in a dramatic series, which included a walk-off on Tuesday and an improbable go-ahead homer on Wednesday. From there, although Chicago took advantage of playing — and winning — on Thursday while Cleveland was off to pull back into a tie atop the division, the Guardians just kept winning, sweeping the the Athletics over the weekend to bring their winning streak to five. José Ramírez finally broke out of his extended slump, tallying nine hits, a home run, and four stolen bases last week.
As for the White Sox, they won three of their four games against the the Tigers, but that one loss was enough to drop them to a game behind Cleveland in the Central. Still, the Sox have a three-game cushion for the final AL Wild Card spot, and they own the tiebreaker over the Guardians, meaning both first place and a potential first-round bye are still in their sights. Miguel Vargas is carrying most of the load for the lineup right now, hitting three home runs last week, but he needs some support if Chicago wants to make some noise in the postseason.
Over in the AL West, the Astros were swept by the Braves this past weekend, allowing the Rangers to jump into first place with a .500 record. Texas enters this week one game up, but crucially Houston holds the tiebreaker. If the Rangers can manage to hang on, it would be just their second postseason appearance in the last decade. The last time they made the playoffs, they won the World Series.
The Houston bullpen was responsible for the backbreaking losses on Saturday and Sunday, but the lack of offense has been a much bigger problem. Over the Astros’ last 10 games, they’ve scored more than four runs in a game just once. Yordan Alvarez looked fine last week (eight hits, including two home runs) after his ankle scare the previous weekend, and Jeremy Peña has been great too (10 hits, three homers), but the rest of the lineup has been struggling. During this 10-game stretch, Houston hitters not named Alvarez or Peña have combined for an ugly 55 wRC+.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

The Diamondbacks managed to keep their slim playoff hopes alive with a pair of wins over the Yankees on Saturday and Sunday. The first victory was a walk-off and the second was highlighted by a go-ahead grand slam from Nolan Arenado. Arizona needs to take care of business in Colorado and get some help from the Dodgers to ensure that the final series against the Padres has some stakes. There’s a chance the Phillies could crash out, opening another window for the Snakes, but the direct path is through San Diego.
The Blue Jays’ hopes for a last-minute surge into the playoffs were dashed last week when they lost both of their series to the Tigers and Rangers. They’re three games back and have the Astros to contend with if they want to try and sneak into that final Wild Card spot. It’s probably too little, too late, but the team is activating Trey Yesavage off the IL on Monday as one more reinforcement ahead of a final push.

The series between the Orioles and Mets last week in Queens turned out to be more interesting than you’d expect from two teams mired in hugely disappointing seasons. Pete Alonso made his first appearance as a member of the opposing team at Citi Field and wound up hitting his 300th career home run on Tuesday, a game-tying shot in the ninth inning. He received a huge ovation from the hometown crowd, which drew some irksome comments from a few Mets players and staff after the game. Baltimore wound up sweeping New York to cut its deficit in the AL Wild Card race to 2.5 games. Alas, a sweep by the Brewers over the weekend slammed the door shut on any playoff hopes the O’s still had.
Even though the Marlins’ season essentially ended with that 12-game losing streak back in July, they have made some significant progress in their quest to become a contending club. Otto Lopez looks like a star they can build the lineup around, while Eury Pérez and Max Meyer should be strong enough to anchor the pitching staff in the years ahead. There’s also a cohort of young prospects in the upper minors who should be making their debuts soon. The future in Miami is brighter than it’s been in a while.
This is the huge step forward the Reds were hoping to see from Elly De La Cruz. In September, he has blasted seven home runs, including in five straight games earlier this month, and is running a major league-best 236 wRC+. It’s too bad the rest of Cincinnati’s roster is a bit of a mess. Sal Stewart has been excellent as De La Cruz’s sidekick, but the starting rotation has struggled mightily, and the big injury to Hunter Greene has thrown the ceiling of that group up in the air heading into next year. Still, building around a superstar like De La Cruz should make things easier if the resources to improve the rest of the roster are made available.

The AL Central crown runs through Kansas City; both the White Sox and Guardians travel to face the Royals during the final week of the season. Unfortunately, the Royals haven’t been playing well enough recently to act as a spoiler. They ended August with a 13-3 stretch, but they’ve been the worst team in the AL in September, with just five wins in 18 games.
It took a lot longer than expected, but the Twins were finally eliminated from the playoff race last week. It was a drama-filled week, too. They won a wild extra-inning walk-off affair against the Yankees on Wednesday and then were walked-off twice against the Angels between two shutout victories over the weekend. Even though they all made their big league debuts over the last few weeks, Walker Jenkins, Kaelen Culpepper, and Emmanuel Rodriguez never all appeared in a game together. That trio represents the future of the organization, so it’s a little disappointing that that future couldn’t be realized in a small way this year.

item.title: [True Blue LA] Emmet Sheehan on a hot streak: ‘My confidence stayed the same the whole time’

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Emmet Sheehan continued his late-season hot streak with another strong outing on Sunday against the San Francisco Giants, with nine strikeouts in 5 1/3 innings, allowing only a single and a walk.
“I’ve loved the version of Emmet we’ve seen the last three outings,” manager Dave Roberts said Sunday. “He’s been fantastic.”
Sheehan in three starts over the last two weeks since rejoining the Dodgers has allowed only one run in 17 innings, with 24 strikeouts against only three walks. It came after spending most of August in Triple-A.
“I don’t know if I proved anything to myself,” Sheehan said. “It was more just getting a couple of things right, and I’m in a much better spot now.”
Sheehan was in the Dodgers rotation from opening day through August 2, when he allowed three home runs and five runs in a loss to the Boston Red Sox. Twenty starts into the season, Sheehan wasn’t getting results (5.29 ERA, belying his 4.00 xERA), and was having issues holding his velocity throughout his starts. He was optioned to Oklahoma City the next day.
That time in the minors was productive for Sheehan. After a planned shortened outing in which he allowed two runs in 2/3 of an inning, Sheehan struck out 24 over three starts with one run allowed in 17 1/3 innings. That earned him a Pacific Coast League pitcher of the week award and pitcher of the month honors for August.
“My confidence stayed the same the whole time. I knew the coaches down there were going to help me, and I was going to get right,” Sheehan said. “I took that approach going into it. I wasn’t helping the team here, so I needed that a little bit. I feel like in a good spot.”
“We’ve seen confidence. When you’re essentially fighting for your life, to create an opportunity for yourself, that’s what I see. There’s urgency,” Roberts said. “I like the way he’s trusting his stuff, he’s in a good spot physically, and the performance has been fantastic.”
One tweak Sheehan made was throwing his curveball more. In his last three outings with the Dodgers, he threw the curve 21.9 percent of the time, up from his 12.3 percent over the course of the season.
“It’s something, Connor [McGuiness, assistant pitching coach], Mark [Prior, pitching coach], and I and the coaches down at Triple-A have been working on a lot is expanding the front-to-back game with the fastball and the curveball,” Sheehan said. “Some guys ended up throughout the season sitting more mid-speed, slider, changeup on me. I think having that change of speeds has been really important.
On Sunday against San Francisco, Sheehan induced 15 of his 18 swinging strikes on his fastball and curveball and finished off five of his nine strikeouts with those two pitches.
Sheehan’s first 26 outings this year were starts, but on Sunday he followed an opener, at the very least getting him oriented about his possible relief role in the postseason. After three solid months in the rotation last season, Sheehan pitched in relief in October, with mixed results (8.59 ERA, 13 hits and five walks in 7 1/3 innings). He allowed runs in each of his four appearances, though rebounded with 2 2/3 scoreless innings in extras in the marathon Game 3, when got three outs with two strikeouts in a scoreless outing in the seventh and eighth innings of Game 7.
“The routine of everything can be a little hard to adjust to, so having that experience helps a lot. Getting back into that, I know what I need to do to be ready to go in the game,” Sheehan said. “Execution was off in the first couple, but then I felt better as it went on.”
Sheehan returned Sunday when Tarik Skubal went on the bereavement list, and the plan is for Sheehan to be optioned back to Triple-A, perhaps as early as Tuesday when Roki Sasaki is likely activated from the injured list straight into a high-leverage relief role.
Roberts on Sunday said the plan is for Sheehan to start on Saturday in the Triple-A championship game, provided Oklahoma City beats Las Vegas in the best-of-3 PCL championship starting Tuesday. But after that, Sheehan will almost certainly be on the playoff roster. Most likely he’ll be in a relief role, but that might depend on how Blake Snell progresses over the next two weeks from his left groin tightness.
“After [Sheehan] makes that last start, we’ll evaluate where we are as a staff,” Roberts said.
“Whatever role they want me to do going forward, I’m ready to do it,” Sheehan said. “It was nice to get that experience coming out of the pen.”

item.dc:creator: TJ French
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are gearing up for another potential deep playoff run. LA clinched the NL West recently and is also looking to earn a first-round bye into the NLDS. If you remember the Dodgers' 2025 World Series run, pitcher Roki Sasaki was a huge piece to the bullpen puzzle, as he slotted in as the team's closer in many big moments. Well, Sasaki could be slated for a similar role this October. More MLB on Heavy: Atlanta Braves Announce Pitcher News Before Reds Series Roki Sasaki Set to
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are gearing up for another potential deep playoff run.
LA clinched the NL West recently and is also looking to earn a first-round bye into the NLDS.
If you remember the Dodgers' 2025 World Series run, pitcher Roki Sasaki was a huge piece to the bullpen puzzle, as he slotted in as the team's closer in many big moments.
Well, Sasaki could be slated for a similar role this October.
More MLB on Heavy: Atlanta Braves Announce Pitcher News Before Reds Series
Roki Sasaki Set to Be Used in Bullpen Role Upon IL Activation
The Los Angeles Dodgers expect Roki Sasaki to be activated off the IL this week (Blister).
"The original plan was for Sasaki to go long as either a starter or a bulk guy, but now it looks like this might be more of a traditional relief outing to get him ready for coming out of the pen in October. It'll be Sasaki's first appearance since he went on the IL with a finger blister at the end of August."
In conjunction with Sasaki, Andy Pages is also likely to be activated on Tuesday.
The Dodgers bullpen group doesn't need nearly as much help this October as they did last year, but the bottom line regarding Sasaki is although he was a solid starter at times for LA this season, the Dodgers' playoff rotation is already locked in.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Get Major Andy Pages Update Ahead of Padres Series
Inside Roki Sasaki's 2026 Season Thus Far
Roki Sasaki endured his blister injury about a month ago in a start against the Atlanta Braves.
Before that development, Sasaki had made 23 starts, and he boasted a 4.60 ERA over 119.1 IP with 117 strikeouts.
Across 31 starts in his MLB career, Sasaki holds an ERA of 4.57 with 145 strikeouts in 155.2 total innings.
If Sasaki does happen to have a prominent role in the Dodgers' bullpen plans in October, it would be remarkable if he could recreate his magic from 2025.

item.title: [New York Post] Roki Sasaki to return to Dodgers this week with a twist
item.dc:creator: Dylan Hernandez
item.description: Will Roki Sasaki again be the Dodgers’ closer in the playoffs? item.content:encoded:
Will Roki Sasaki again be the Dodgers’ closer in the playoffs?
The Dodgers have created a pathway to make that possible, as manager Dave Roberts said that Sasaki will be moved into the bullpen when he is activated from the injured list this week.
Sasaki has pitched in 23 games this season, every one of them starts. A blister on his pitching hand has sidelined him since Aug. 27, but Roberts said he expected him to be activated during an upcoming three-game series against the Padres that starts on Tuesday.
The Dodgers had refrained from turning Sasaki into a reliever up to this point because of concerns over their starting rotation. Blake Snell departed from his most recent start after one inning because of a tight groin, but the two-time Cy Young Award winner has since not experienced any problems in that area.
The team believes it has four healthy starters in Snell, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal and Tyler Glasnow. Emmet Sheehan figures to be the rotation’s new insurance policy, as Sheehan has allowed only one run in 17 innings pitched this month.
Roberts said he doesn’t plan to use Sasaki as a quasi-starter who pitches four or five innings following an opener.
Asked if Sasaki would be used in late-inning, high-leverage situations, Roberts replied, “I trust Roki in any situation. I would say probably start a clean inning, but, yeah.”
Could he close?
“It won’t be the ninth inning the first time,” Roberts said.
But Roberts acknowledged there was a chance Sasaki could end up in that role.
Sasaki became the Dodgers’ closer last year by default, as the team didn’t have any other options. He saved three games in the postseason.
His move to the bullpen last year came after he missed 4 ½ months because of shoulder problems. He agreed to try pitching in relief under the condition the Dodgers let him start again the next season.
Sasaki is 5-5 with a 4.70 earned-run average this year, but was 2-0 with a 3.05 ERA in the seven starts he made after the All-Star break.
The Dodgers started this season counting on $69-million free agent addition Edwin Diaz to be their closer, but the three-time All-Star has endured a nightmare of a season that has included two IL stints. In Diaz’s absence, Tanner Scott has served as the team’s primary ninth-inning option and has performed well. However, Scott has posted a 4.97 ERA over his last 14 games.

item.title: [True Blue LA] Dodgers Week 26: Back in the postseason saddle again
item.dc:creator: Eric Stephen
item.description: The Dodgers are taking advantage of the schedule in front of them, with 14 wins in 19 September games, including winning the last 10 in a row at home. This week that meant beating the Reds three times in four games in Cincinnati, then returning to Los Angeles to sweep the Giants. item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers are taking advantage of the schedule in front of them, with 14 wins in 19 September games, including winning the last 10 in a row at home. This week that meant beating the Reds three times in four games in Cincinnati, then returning to Los Angeles to sweep the Giants.
They went with a two-way under the Cincinnati skyline, first clinching a postseason berth on Monday, tying the Atlanta Braves record with 14 straight postseasons, followed by winning their fifth straight National League West title and 13 out of 14 on Thursday.
Entering the final week of the season, the Dodgers can clinch a bye week with a magic number of three over the Braves.
Batter of the week
Kyle Tucker is starting to turn things around at the plate, and followed up an excellent series the previous weekend in Miami with nine hits in 20 at-bats, with three home runs and two doubles, with six walks and just one strikeout.
Honorable mention goes to Mookie Betts, who tied a Dodgers record with three doubles on Saturday, part of a stretch of three consecutive games with at least three hits. Will Smith found his power again with two home runs and a double, and Alex Freeland reached base eight times in 14 trips to the plate, including a home run and a double.
Pitcher of the week
Yoshinobu Yamamoto pitched seven scoreless innings with seven strikeouts to beat the Reds on Tuesday, his third straight seven-inning start in September. Yamamoto this season has allowed zero or one run in 14 of his 27 starts.
Honorable mention goes to Justin Wrobleski, who retired all nine batters he faced with three strikeouts while starting Thursday’s division clincher in Cincinnati, and to Landon Knack, who got the win in that game with four scoreless innings in relief. Also to Emmet Sheehan, who continued his strong six-week run with nine strikouts in 5 1/3 scoreless frames on Sunday.
Week 26 results
6-1 record
39 runs scored (5.57 per game)
16 runs allowed (2.29 per game)
.836 pythagorean win percentage
Year to date
96-60 record
780 runs scored (5.00 per game)
587 runs allowed (3.76 per game)
.627 pythagorean win percentage (98-58)
Miscellany
Half a hundred: The Dodgers have won 10 games in a row at home, and Sunday’s win was their 50th win at Dodger Stadium this season. That’s six straight years with 50 wins at home, plus seven straight full seasons dating back to 2019. Since moving into Dodger Stadium, the Dodgers won 50 home games 12 times in 51 full seasons through 2014. But since 2015, they’ve won at least 50 games at home 10 times in 11 full seasons.
A crowded 10-K: Tyler Glasnow beat the Giants on Friday with a strong six innings, including 10 strikeouts. Glasnow is the eighth different Dodgers pitcher with a 10-strikeout game this season, the most in franchise history. No other MLB team this year has more than five such pitchers.
Parliamentary procedure: After making the All-Star team as a starter with the Kansas City Royals in 2025, left-hander Kris Bubic was on the 60-day injured list when the Dodgers acquired him just ahead of the August 3 trade deadline. Now he’s pitching in relief, angling for a spot on the postseason roster. With his appearance on Wednesday, Bubic became the 33rd different Dodgers pitcher used this season. So far, Bubic has four strikeouts in 2 2/3 innings in three appearances. “It’s just funk,” manager Dave Roberts said Sunday of Bubic. “It’s nothing overpowering, but there’s just funky swings, soft contact. I see him as a neutral pitcher, gets left and right out. I like those converted starters, because he knows how to navigate lineups.”
A quirk: The division clincher Thursday in Cincinnati was an 8-2 win, then came four home runs in the eighth inning Friday on the 20th anniversary of the 4+1 Game for another 8-2 triumph. That was the first time in Dodgers history they’ve won consecutive games by an 8-2 score.
Transactions
Monday: The fresh arm express was busy this week, beginning with Emmet Sheehan getting optioned the day after pitching six scoreless innings, in favor of Paul Gervase.
Monday: One day after a rare bad outing, Edgardo Henriquez was placed on the injured list with low back discomfort, ending his regular season and putting his playoff availability in question. Bobby Miller returned from Triple-A.
Wednesday: Trade deadline acquisition Kris Bubic was activated off the 60-day IL to make his Dodgers debut in relief, the team’s 33rd pitcher of the season. Gervase was optioned and Ryan Ward was designated for assignment.
Thursday: Miller was sent back to Oklahoma City, and Landon Knack was called up to pitch four scoreless innings in relief in the division clincher in Cincinnati.
Sunday: Sheehan got the call back up to the Dodgers, with Tarik Skubal placed on the bereavement list. Kyle Hurt was also called up, with Seth Halvorsen optioned.

item.dc:creator: TJ French

LA, after clinching the NL West, is still looking to secure the NL’s No.2 seed
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 21: Andy Pages #44 of the Los Angeles Dodgers reacts between Dave Roberts #30 and Rafael Flores Jr. #43 of the Pittsburgh Pirates, after he was hit by a pitch, during the third inning at Dodger Stadium on August 21, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images)
The Los Angeles Dodgers are coming off a three-game sweep of the San Francisco Padres this past weekend.
LA, after clinching the NL West, is still looking to secure the NL’s No.2 seed with just six games left on the schedule. Next up for LA is a series with the San Diego Padres, who are rolling right now in MLB. The Dodgers have Monday off after a long stretch of games.
As the Dodgers gear up for a playoff run, they recently received a great piece of news regarding outfielder Andy Pages.
“Andy Pages will be activated before Tuesday’s game vs. SD, Dave Roberts said, with Shohei Ohtani “shortly” after. Roki Sasaki will be available out of the bullpen as Dodgers begin to plot out their October relief roles. Big week for a lot of guys, including Edwin Díaz.”
The MLB regular season has just one week left until the playoffs begin starting next week.
Getting Andy Pages back will be a huge boost for the Dodgers lineup, as he’s been enjoying a solid campaign and contributing heavily to the team’s offense.
GettyLOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA – AUGUST 15: Andy Pages #44 of the Los Angeles Dodgers reacts at the plate during the game against the Milwaukee Brewers at Dodger Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images)
Andy Pages injured his hand after being hit by a pitch about a month ago, which landed him on the IL.
LA obviously wants to take things slow with Pages to avoid further injury, but the consensus is that he is good to go after doing a lot of off-field hitting work.
A first-time MLB All-Star this season, Pages is batting .272 with 21 home runs, 25 doubles, 80 RBI, and an OPS+ of 117.
TJ French covers the MLB for Heavy. TJ is a graduate of the University of Georgia. He has 2+ years of writing experience.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Roki Sasaki Heading Back to Dodgers' Bullpen With Postseason Looming
item.dc:creator: Aaron Coloma

Sasaki, 24, landed on the injured list at the end of August, putting an end to a dominant run which came after the All-Star break. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers will move right-hander Roki Sasaki to the bullpen when he returns from the injured list in their next series against the San Diego Padres.
Sasaki, 24, landed on the injured list at the end of August, putting an end to a dominant run which came after the All-Star break. He allowed two runs or fewer in each of his appearances leading into an Aug. 26 start against the Atlanta Braves, during which he allowed four earned runs.
Why Would the Dodgers Move Roki Sasaki to a Relief Role?
The Dodgers have to trim their rotation to four players when the postseason comes, so putting Sasaki back into the bullpen is only natural given the other players they have on their roster.
Tyler Glasnow, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell and Yoshinobu Yamamoto are all likely to remain starters, so Sasaki’s relief role isn’t especially surprising. Roberts revealed Sasaki could operate in slightly different situations upon his return, potentially handling several innings in relief.
“I could see multiple innings but it’s not gonna be bulk like 4 or 5 innings,” Roberts said, per Dodgers Nation’s Noel Sanchez.
“…I trust Roki in any situation. [His first appearance] won’t be in the ninth the first time. It could potentially fall out, but it won’t be that way.”
Sasaki has the stuff to be a high-leverage reliever and showed he was more than capable last season. His fastball ranks among the fastest in MLB, topping out above 100 mph, and his limited arsenal suggests he’ll see even more success as a reliever.
How Did Roki Sasaki Perform Out of the Bullpen Last Season?
Sasaki returned from a long-term stint on the injured list towards the latter end of last season. He made two appearances before the end of the year as a reliever, holding opponents scoreless in both before entering the postseason in the same role.
The right-hander looked like a brand new pitcher in the postseason, making nine appearances and only allowing one earned run through 10.2 innings pitched.
He took over as the team’s closer during their postseason run, and went 3-for-3 in save opportunities throughout October.
The Dodgers will hope he can find that same form in the bullpen this year as they chase a historic three-peat.

item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers begin their final regular season home series of the year, hosting the San Diego Padres beginning Tuesday night at Dodger Stadium.
Center fielder Andy Pages will likely be activated to start on Tuesday, after missing 27 games with a broken left hand.
It'll be a bullpen game for the Dodgers in the opener, who will start Yoshinobu Yamamoto on Wednesday and likely Tyler Glasnow on Thursday. Roki Sasaki is expected to be available out of the bullpen against the Padres, not as a bulk reliever, but will instead pitch in high-leverage relief, potentially for multiple innings on occasion.
"I trust him," manager Dave Roberts said of Sasaki in relief on Sunday.
Right-hander Michael King starts on the mound for the Padres on Tuesday.
Tuesday game info
- Teams: Dodgers vs. Padres
- Ballpark: Dodger Stadium
- Start time: 7:10 p.m.
- TV: SportsNet LA, TBS (out of market)
- Radio: AM 570 (English), KTNQ 1020 AM (Spanish)

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Is it still a rivalry? Dodgers complete sweep of woeful Giants
item.dc:creator: Kevin Baxter
item.description: Is it still a rivalry? Dodgers complete sweep of woeful Giants - Click here to listen to this article - Only the Pirates and Cubs have met more often than the Dodgers and Giants, who faced off for the first time in 1889. item.content:encoded:
Is it still a rivalry? Dodgers complete sweep of woeful Giants
- Click here to listen to this article
-
Only the Pirates and Cubs have met more often than the Dodgers and Giants, who faced off for the first time in 1889. And over all that time, the Dodgers are just two games better, with 1,294 wins to the Giants’ 1,292.
The Dodgers and Giants have also won more pennants, made more World Series appearances and have more players wearing their caps in the Hall of Fame than any other National League teams, all of which fueled a rivalry that was once among the most visceral and passionate in American sports.
But that was then and this is now.
After Sunday’s 3-1 victory over the Giants, the Dodgers’ 14th win in their last 17 games, the team could finish a season with 100 wins for the fourth time in six years. The Giants have had just one winning record in that time.
The Dodgers (96-60), who have won five straight division titles, are headed to the postseason for a record-tying 14th consecutive year. The Giants will miss the playoffs for a fifth straight season.
So is the rivalry dead? That depends on who you ask.
“It’s always a rivalry,” Giants pitcher Logan Webb. “We’d like to make it a little closer when it comes to the standings. But I definitely feel it when I throw against them.”
But then Webb, who is from Northern California, grew up with the rivalry and, as the longest-tenured Giant, pitched against the Dodgers in games that mattered. Giants coach Ron Washington, who made his major league debut with the Dodgers when the rivalry was still a thing, said many players on San Francisco’s roster don’t know that background.
Mookie Betts hits three doubles and the Dodgers piled up 15 hits in a 10-4 win over the San Francisco Giants with Shohei Ohtani’s return on the horizon.
“It should be a rivalry. But I don’t think the young kids we got know anything about a rivalry. They’re not history buffs.”
Webb said it’s the responsibility of the veterans on both sides to keep that history alive by explaining the enmity to the young players.
“I think there are still guys that came up in the system that know what it’s like,” he said. “It’s my job to kind of hype these guys up to play a game like this.”
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts, who played for the Dodgers and Giants during his 10-year career, agrees the rivalry now exists more in the history books than the current standings, where the Giants have been overtaken by the San Diego Padres, who will finish second to the Dodgers in the N.L. West for the fourth time in five seasons.
“It’s certainly a rivalry in the sense of the history, the fan bases,” Roberts said. “But obviously it’s about relevancy. The Padres have been successful the last handful of years, and so it’s certainly built some momentum. The geography lends itself to that too.
“But Dodgers Giants is always fun.”
It hasn’t been so much fun for the Giants lately. San Francisco hasn’t won the season series with the Dodgers since 2021 and has lost more than 90 games this year for the first time in nine seasons.
On Sunday they went in front three batters into the game with Johan Cox working Dodger opener Jack Dreyer for a leadoff walk, then making his way around the bases on Dreyer’s throwing error, a stolen base and a one-one single by Victor Bericoto.
But San Francisco didn’t get another hit until Jung Hoo Lee singled with one out in the sixth.
That allowed the Dodgers to tie the score in the sixth on Tommy Edman’s seventh home run of the season just inside the right-field foul pole. An inning later they went ahead to stay when Max Muncy singled under a sliding Cox at second, moved to third on a single by rookie Josue De Paula and scored on Kiké Hernández’s double to center.
A two-out single by Muncy, his second of the game, scored Teoscar Hernández, who also had two hits, in the eighth inning with the final run.
Even the slumping Freddie Freeman contributed to the Dodgers’ 11-hit attack, ending an 0-for-11 slide with a broken-bat single in the fourth then singling again in the eighth.
Sunday’s result helped clarify the Dodgers’ once-muddy playoff picture. With six games left in the regular season, the Dodgers lead Atlanta by four games in the race for the second seed in the National League playoffs, which would give them a first-round bye and the homefield advantage in the division series.
The team’s postseason roster may be getting clearer as well. Right-hander Emmet Sheehan, who made 22 starts this season, came out of the bullpen for the first time Sunday and was brilliant in his audition for the playoffs.
“If there is a role in the postseason, it will be out of the [bull]pen,” Roberts said of Sheehan, who gave up just a hit and walk, striking out nine — one off his season high — in 5 1/3 innings.
Tyler Glasnow hasn’t had the greatest of seasons, but the Dodgers will need him to deliver in the playoffs if they want to win another World Series title.
De Paula, meanwhile, who also doubled in running his modest hitting streak to four games, appears to have secured a job as the team’s left-handed bat off the bench while utility player Hyeseong Kim, who has spent the last four months in the minors, will rejoin the Dodgers after the triple-A playoffs and be considered for a roster spot as a pinch-runner and late-inning defensive replacement.
“My expectation is that Hyeseong will be here during the off week and potentially be a conversation for the postseason because he has the ability to run, play defense, and steal a base,” Roberts said.
After Monday’s off day, the final break of the regular season for the Dodgers, the team is expected to activate Andy Pages, Roki Sasaki and Shohei Ohtani from the injured list during its three-game series with the Padres.

item.title: [MLB.com] How Sheehan, Sasaki and others look to fit in LA's postseason 'pen plans
item.dc:creator: Sonja Chen

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- The saying goes that pitching wins championships, and that was true in different ways when the Dodgers won back-to-back World Series in 2024 and '25.
The 2024 Dodgers had to lean heavily on their bullpen out of necessity, while the '25 team rode its rotation to a successful title defense -- so much so that all four starting pitchers took the ball in the winner-take-all Game 7.
As the Dodgers go for a three-peat this year, they'll once again look for their starting four of Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow to set the tone. But their bullpen feels less volatile than it was last year, and it could be one of the most fluid position groups as L.A. considers how to piece together its postseason rosters.
One way or another, the Dodgers will carry their best 13 pitchers in the postseason, because as manager Dave Roberts has said repeatedly, like a mantra: "Every inning in the postseason is leverage."
The Dodgers got a look at several postseason 'pen candidates when they ran a bullpen game to success on Sunday afternoon at Dodger Stadium, capping a three-game sweep of the Giants with a 3-1 victory. Right-hander Emmet Sheehan struck out nine in 5 1/3 scoreless innings of bulk relief, giving L.A. an intriguing option to add to the mix.
The Dodgers' fourth straight victory maintained their four-game lead over the Braves for the second-best record in the National League -- and a first-round postseason bye -- with six games left to play.
The greatest need in the bullpen is right-handed leverage arms. Edwin Díaz, who signed a three-year, $69 million deal to be their closer, has been relegated to lower leverage for the time being amid his poor performance in an injury-ravaged season. Edgardo Henriquez, who stepped up to become L.A.'s most reliable righty in leverage, is out for the rest of the regular season due to a lower back strain. He could return during the postseason, but the uncertainty still creates a need.
Evan Phillips and Brock Stewart have been solid options, but they have been more valuable as part of the bridge to the ninth inning, rather than to close out games. In order to find such options from the right-hand side, the Dodgers can turn to the strength of their staff: the rotation.
Sheehan is one candidate, although he'll remain stretched out through the end of the regular season as rotation depth. Another is Roki Sasaki, who was also originally going to remain built up as a starter upon his return from the 15-day IL. Instead, Roberts said, Sasaki will likely be activated Tuesday and be available out of the bullpen, beginning his transition to relief in the final days of the regular season.
"He's done it. He's really good. He's a neutral pitcher, high-octane stuff," Roberts said. "You really just need four starters, you know. So we're in a good spot there for now."
Sheehan and Sasaki both got a crash course in short-burst relief last fall. While Sasaki thrived as the Dodgers' postseason closer, Sheehan was scored on in his first four appearances before rebounding for scoreless outings in Games 3 and 7 of the World Series.
For Sheehan, adapting his typical routine to relief was difficult, but he believes that he can build on last year if he gets the call to the 'pen again.
"Having that experience helps a lot," Sheehan said. "Just getting back into that, I know what I need to do to get ready to go into the game."
And don't count out Díaz. His pitch to earn a spot in the postseason 'pen began with two scoreless innings against the Giants this weekend.
When the postseason comes, the Dodgers may not be able to avoid using Díaz in leverage, even if they don't throw him into a comparable situation in the final days of the regular season. But if he shows enough this week, then L.A. will bet on his track record.
"I gotta show them I’m part of that bullpen," Díaz said. "I haven’t pitched [much] this year, and when I’ve been on the mound I’ve been struggling. So right now, I’m giving my 200% just to show them I will be in that roster spot."

item.dc:creator: Dylan Hernandez

Yuuri Teramoto, a first-year student at Hanamaki Higashi High School, threw out the ceremonial first pitch before the Dodgers’ series finale against the San Francisco Giants. item.content:encoded:
Earlier this month, Shohei Ohtani was ruled out from pitching again this season.
But on Sunday, a pitcher from his high school alma mater scaled the mound at Dodger Stadium.
Yuuri Teramoto, a first-year student at Hanamaki Higashi High School, threw out the ceremonial first pitch before the Dodgers’ series finale against the San Francisco Giants. Teramoto plays on Hanamaki Higashi’s girls baseball team.
Teramoto was one of 50 high school students chosen by Iwate prefecture to visit the United States as part of an exchange program. This is the 150th anniversary of Iwate’s founding, as well as the 15th anniversary of the Tohoku earthquake and tsunami.
Teramoto’s first pitch was caught by Iwate native Roki Sasaki, who is from the coastal town of Rikuzentakata and lost his father in the tsunami.
Teramoto is from the southern island of Kumamoto but said she was in part inspired by Ohtani to attend high school in Iwate, which is on the northern part of Japan’s mainland.
“He’s someone I admire,” Teramoto said in Japanese.
Like Ohtani, she added, “My dream in the future is to go to the United States.”
Hanamaki Higashi is also the high school alma mater of Angels left-hander Yusei Kikuchi and Miami Marlins prospect Rintaro Sasaki.
Teramoto said her team practices using a pitching machine donated by Ohtani.
“We used the machine every day and we’re very grateful,” she said.

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers starter Tarik Skubal moved to the bereavement list on Sunday, and will be there for a "couple of days," per Dave Roberts.
In corresponding moves, the Dodgers optioned Seth Halvorsen and recalled Emmet Sheehan and Kyle Hurt.
BREAKING: Tarik Skubal will be away from the Dodgers for a couple days due to personal reasons ?
Seth Halvorsen has also been optioned and Kyle Hurt and Emmet Sheehan are back.
Skubal last pitched for the Dodgers on Saturday, and had a frustrating outing—his worst since donning a Dodgers uniform. He lasted just five innings, allowing four earned runs on eight hits while recording a season-low three strikeouts.
What Does Tarik Skubal's Absence Mean?
The left-hander's presence on the bereavement list doesn't impact the rest of the Dodgers' season, as he will likely be ready for his next turn through the rotation if he stays out for a couple of days as Roberts said.
That should be a huge relief for the Dodgers, who have quite a few injuries among their starters as the postseason nears. Shohei Ohtani, Roki Sasaki and Eric Lauer are all on the IL, leaving LA with limited options.
An injury or extended period of absence for any of their remaining starters would throw a wrench in their plans for the postseason.
Additionally, Skubal's track record since joining the team is fantastic—serving as one of their best starters since the beginning of August. He has a 2.95 ERA through nine starts, striking out 60 batters through 55 innings pitched.
What Roles Will Kyle Hurt and Emmet Sheehan Play?
Hurt and Sheehan are likely to jump straight into the action, as the Dodgers are running a bullpen game on Sunday.
Jack Dreyer is getting the start, but using Hurt and Sheehan—both of whom have experience handling bulk innings—afterwards is the Dodgers' most likely move.
The duo have bounced between Triple-A and MLB over the past few weeks, but could very well find a spot on the team if they perform well Sunday. Sheehan is in the midst of a fantastic run of form, and has capitalized on both of his MLB opportunities in Setpember.
He only allowed one earned run through 11.2 innings pitched over his last two starts, and is a real candidate to make the postseason roster despite his recent stays in the minors.
Before that, though, he'll have to perform in Sunday's game against the Giants, which begins at 1:10 p.m. PT.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Andy Pages went through the paces on Saturday afternoon, grinding through an intense on-field workout in the clearest sign yet that he will be ready to return on Tuesday to open the final home series of the regular season.
Pages wore a fitness tracker, similar to what soccer players use to monitor all aspects of physical fitness. Coaches and staff put him through an estimated five simulated innings all in a compressed window of time.
The All-Star center fielder not only tested his broken left hand, but he also pushed his physical fitness to the limits.
Pages went from hitting to defense to base running and then doing it all over again to make sure he is ready for the rigors of play next week. His return is expected to come in the opener of a three-game series against the San Diego Padres.
While that kind of energy output is typically done in a rehab game, there aren’t many minor league options remaining this late in the season.
One thing Pages will not get is the chance to hit off a pitcher at full velocity.
“I think that from what I understand, we don’t have really any available arms,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said about the prospect of a live batting practice session. “A lot of our guys are playing in playoff games in the minors, and we have (Eric) Lauer, who’s on the IL. So, we don’t really have anyone.”
That’s not ideal for a player coming off the uncertainty that comes with a hand injury. But Pages did show that his hand soreness has subsided enough to hit multiple balls over the outfield wall.
“I’m expecting good at-bats,” Roberts said. “I can’t speak to the performance. I just want him to have good at-bats, and I’m not sure where he’s going to hit. Somewhere middle to the bottom (of the order), I think. I think I’m waiting just like you guys are waiting to see how it looks.”
The Dodgers close the season with six consecutive games, including the season-ending series in San Francisco next weekend.
“Six in a row, and that seems pretty aggressive (for Pages),” Roberts said. “So, I think that we do want to get him as many at-bats as possible, but we have to make sure that his legs are under him, feeling good, so we don’t go backward or get injured in that respect. It is going to be a balancing act and just keeping a keen eye on Andy, for sure.”
Regardless of what his swing looks like, the Dodgers still trust him in center field. After all, his World Series-saving catch in Game 7 last season came as a late-inning defensive replacement.
“Playing a premium position and playing it well is hugely important,” Roberts said.
ROTATING THE ROTATION
Left-hander Blake Snell is not expected to pitch in the upcoming series against the Padres, but he has not been ruled out for the series against the Giants next weekend.
Snell left his start Thursday after one inning in Cincinnati because of groin discomfort.
“He’s trending very well,” Roberts said about Snell’s recovery in recent days.
Right-hander Roki Sasaki is expected to pitch in the upcoming series against the Padres, although his role has not yet been specified. There is a chance Sasaki could start a game against San Diego, or come out of the bullpen, which had been his expected role in the postseason.
“It will be multiples for sure,” Roberts said about Sasaki’s innings count. “I just don’t know exactly when.”
A LEADING MAN
Shohei Ohtani is still expected to return to play before the regular season ends next Sunday, although there remains no target date.
In the meantime, the Dodgers continue to weigh their options in the leadoff spot. Tommy Edman was there immediately after Ohtani went on the injured list earlier this month, Josue De Paula took a turn there and Mookie Betts has been the latest to stake a claim.
Betts hit two home runs from the leadoff spot Friday and was back at the top of the lineup on Saturday.
“Yeah, I think that certainly there is an uncertainty with Shohei, all the while expecting him to be back,” Roberts said. “But you do got to kind of prepare for whatever, and I just think that Mookie’s swinging the bat well, has hit there many times throughout his career, so it just kind of makes sense.”
Betts had three hits Wednesday in Cincinnati and three more Friday against the Giants in the leadoff spot, including two home runs. He is batting .356 with six home runs and 18 RBIs in 15 September games.
ALSO
The Dodgers are expected to select a pitcher to pick up bulk innings on Sunday in a hybrid bullpen game against the Giants, but the exact plan remains undetermined.
UP NEXT
Giants (LHP Matt Wilkinson, 1-3, 4.58 ERA) at Dodgers (TBA), Sunday, 1:10 p.m., SportsNet LA, 570 AM, 1020 AM

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angele Dodgers are getting Roki Sasaki back for the team’s last marquee regular-season series against the San Diego Padres.
Sasaki is on the injured list because a blister formed on his right middle finger during his last start.
He last pitched on August 26th against the Atlanta Braves, throwing 3.1 innings and 66 pitches before he was pulled with the training alongside him.
The Japanese pitcher took a few days to rest and let the blister heal, and Sasaki has since done multiple bullpen sessions and a live batting practice outing.
Roki Sasaki threw another bullpen session on Saturday, September 19th, before the San Fransico Giants game, Dodgers Nation’s Noel Sanchez reports.
According to manager Dave Roberts, the organization plans to start Sasaki at some point early next week, during the last home series of the year against the Padres.
“We haven’t settled yet, but I think it’s going to be in that San Diego series,” Roberts said to the media, including Dodgers Nation.
“Whether it’s to start the game or pitch innings out of the bullpen, it will be multiple innings for sure.
“I just don’t know exactly when, but it’ll be in that San Diego series.”
The plan for Roki Sasaki changed
The Dodgers were not sure about Sasaki’s status for a long time, not due to his health, but rather how they want to deploy him.
In the playoffs, he is set to join the bullpen as long-relief coverage or a high-leverage arm.
However, Blake Snell’s injury scare left his status unclear, with a possible rotation spot opening up.
Since Snell’s early exit in his last, things have started trending up, and all signs point to him pitching in the postseason.
This leaves Sasaki once again looking at the bullpen in October, but for the remainder of the regular season, to make sure their starters get rest, the Dodgers want Sasaki to make a starter and transition to the bullpen outright in the postseason.

Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said Saturday that Sasaki (finger) will return during next week's series against the Padres, David Vassegh of AM 570 LA Sports reports.
Sasaki made it through an extended side session Wednesday (48 pitches) and is now ready to return, though the team is still undecided on whether he will start or pitch multiple innings out of the bullpen against San Diego. A bullpen role in the postseason seems likely for a Dodgers club chasing its third straight championship.

item.title: [True Blue LA] The growing Dodgers 10-strikeout club

item.description: Tyler Glasnow on Friday night struck out 10 Giants in his six innings, his most in a start this season. item.content:encoded:
Tyler Glasnow on Friday night struck out 10 Giants in his six innings, his most in a start this season. Aside from securing Los Angeles-area folks a free Jumbo Jack with a purchase of a large drink for the 130th time this season and the 27th time in the last 28 days, Friday affirmed the Dodgers’ unique spot in double-digit strikeout games this season.
The Dodgers now have a dozen individual 10-strikeout games this season. That’s not the most, it’s tied for fourth-most with the Toronto Blue Jays, behind the Milwaukee Brewers (16), Cleveland Guardians (15), and Philadelphia Phillies (14).
But what makes the Dodgers unique this season is that eight different pitchers have achieved double-digit strikeouts in a game:
- Yoshinobu Yamamoto (May 31, July 4, September 9)
- Emmet Sheehan (April 24, September 7)
- Blake Snell (August 11, August 29)
- Shohei Ohtani (April 15)
- Roki Sasaki (June 5)
- Justin Wrobleski (June 30)
- Tarik Skubal (August 22)
- Tyler Glasnow (September 18)
The next-closest team is the Minnesota Twins, with five different pitchers striking out at least 10 in a game this season. The Houston Astros, Brewers, New York Yankees, Pittsburgh Pirates, Texas Rangers, and Seattle Mariners have four pitchers each.
The Dodgers have eight different pitchers, which is at least one measure of their depth.
Eight pitchers with 10 strikeouts is the most the Dodgers have ever had in a season, two more than in 2022.
Saturday game info
- Teams: Dodgers vs. Giants
- Ballpark: Dodger Stadium
- Start time: 6:10 p.m.
- TV: SportsNet LA, MLB Network (out of market)
- Radio: AM 570 (English), KTNQ 1020 AM (Spanish)

item.title: [DodgerBlue.com] Dodgers make decision on Roki Sasaki's role, but it might only be temporary

item.content:encoded:
With just over one week remaining in the regular season, the Los Angeles Dodgers expect to soon activate Roki Sasaki off the 15-day injured list.
After some initial uncertainty in terms of Sasaki’s, manager Dave Roberts indicated the right-hander will make a start upon returning.
“Roki’s in a good spot, Roki is anxious to pitch. As we sit here on Friday, I could see him back in there soon,” Roberts said. “I’m not sure what day, but I see him starting a game.”
Sasaki threw 48 pitches over four innings of live batting practice this past Wednesday as seemingly a final checkpoint to test the blister on the middle finger of his right hand.
“Pitched with the Dermabond, which he can use legally in a game. He came out of it well,” Roberts noted earlier in the week. “So we’ve got to huddle up here and figure out what’s his role? The No. 1 thing is he came out of the session well. Now we’ve got to figure out how to plug him in. He’s going to be important. I just don’t know right now in what role.”
Roberts’ comments came just before Blake Snell was forced to leave his start early because of left groin tightness. There is optimism with Snell moving forward, but that unexpected injury — even if it is minor — prompted the Dodgers to settle on keeping Sasaki as a starter for the time being despite previously suggesting a role change was coming.
Of course, the bullpen bath is an equally valid choice if the Dodgers foresee Sasaki being used as a reliever in the postseason.
“That’s the great thing about the question. There’s benefit both ways,” Roberts said. “One could argue it’s best to take down a couple starts, keep him built up because if something does happen, he’s built up. The other side is you can assimilate him to the ‘pen and get comfortable in that role, if that is the role.”
Possible options with Roki Sasaki
Although the Dodgers are planning to have Sasaki make a start in his return from the injured list, that could be followed with a move into the bullpen.
Last season the Dodgers had Sasaki make two relief appearances during the final week as an audition and preparation for what wound up being his October role.

item.title: [DodgerBlue.com] Mookie Betts shares his hope for Dodgers mindset to finish the season
item.dc:creator: Blake Williams
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers have been on a hot streak in September, and it starts with their offense getting back on track after an awful month of August. Their lineup breaking out has coincided with Teoscar Hernandez, Kyle Tucker and Mookie Betts starting to produce at expected levels, and the return of Will Smith from the injured list. However, it has come without Shohei Ohtani as he’s currently on the 15-day injured list, and Freddie Freeman has been in a major slump due to right knee tendinitis.
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have been on a hot streak in September, and it starts with their offense getting back on track after an awful month of August.
Their lineup breaking out has coincided with Teoscar Hernandez, Kyle Tucker and Mookie Betts starting to produce at expected levels, and the return of Will Smith from the injured list. However, it has come without Shohei Ohtani as he’s currently on the 15-day injured list, and Freddie Freeman has been in a major slump due to right knee tendinitis.
Even without two of their biggest bats producing, the Dodgers have answered a lot of questions about their offense. They have taken better at-bats, they’re hitting the ball harder, and there is an increased focus and intensity with each pitch.
But with little left to play for after clinching the National League West and currently in a great spot to lock up the number two seed, that could lead to the Dodgers taking their foot off the gas in their final few games.
“We’re just playing good ball right now,” Betts said. “Just got to keep playing good ball and keep going through the end of the season. We don’t want any letups; we don’t want to try turning anything on once the postseason starts. We just want to play good ball and we want that to be our identity.”
The Dodgers are also starting to get healthy at the right time, which further boosts their confidence heading into October.
Andy Pages and Ohtani are both on the verge of returning, and Roki Sasaki should re-join the pitching staff soon as well. In addition, the Dodgers remain optimistic that Edgardo Henriquez will be back for the playoffs.
“It’s been good. We just have to keep playing,” Betts said. “Get guys to come back, like (Edwin) Díaz tonight. Get a couple more guys back and we should be ready to roll.”
What Mookie Betts thinks of Dodgers lineup
With nearly everyone in the lineup hitting well right now, Betts has seen both a positive and a negative effect from it. Betts described it as taking pressure off because you can trust the players behind you, but you’re also coming up to bat in RBI situations and big moments far more often because of the success of the hitters in front of you.
“It’s easier, but it’s also tough,” Betts began. “Because there’s constantly guys on base, so the constant need for that hit. But I think that’s the beauty in it. We just keep giving ourselves opportunities, and eventually something will crack like it did tonight.
“We just have to keep getting guys on base and giving ourselves a chance. The hits will fall.”

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers esperan que Snell (ingle) haga una apertura más antes de la postemporada
This browser does not support the video element.
LOS ÁNGELES -- Dos días después de salir de su apertura tras apenas una entrada debido a rigidez en la ingle izquierda, Blake Snell lanzó desde 90 pies de distancia en el terreno del Dodger Stadium antes del primer juego de la serie del viernes contra los Gigantes. Salió sintiéndose bien, y los Dodgers creen que evitaron lo peor con una lesión que ha sido un problema recurrente a lo largo de la carrera del zurdo.
"Feliz de que lo detectamos a tiempo", indicó el manager Dave Roberts, quien señaló que Snell no fue enviado a hacerse ninguna prueba de imagen.
Los Dodgers se mantienen optimistas de que el dos veces ganador del Premio Cy Young hará otra apertura en la temporada regular en algún momento durante sus nueve juegos restantes. El día específico está por verse -- su turno regular en la rotación caería durante la serie de tres choques de Los Ángeles ante San Diego que comienza el martes -- pero no se espera que lance con ninguna limitación.
"Creo que sería más una apertura normal", aseguró Roberts. "Tal vez no lo exijamos muchísimo, dado que no sabemos cómo se desarrollará la temporada. Pero esta será su última salida de la temporada regular, así que creo que sería más una apertura regular".
This browser does not support the video element.
Snell inició la campaña en la lista de lesionados de 15 días con fatiga en el hombro izquierdo, haciendo su debut de temporada apenas el 9 de mayo. Casi de inmediato volvió a la lista de lesionados debido a cuerpos libres en su codo izquierdo, los cuales fueron removidos mediante el procedimiento NanoNeedle Scope. Desde que regresó el 11 de agosto, Snell ha lucido como si no hubiera perdido el ritmo, registrando efectividad de 1.01 en siete aperturas, con 47 ponches y 14 bases por bolas en 35.2 entradas.
Para un lanzador que comparte la rotación con Yoshinobu Yamamoto y Tarik Skubal, Snell es una pieza absolutamente vital en los planes de los Dodgers para los playoffs. Si su condición empeora, la profundidad del pitcheo abridor de Los Ángeles de repente luce bastante mermada. Está Tyler Glasnow, quien abrió el viernes contra San Francisco pero que ha lidiado con sus propios problemas de lesiones este año. También se espera que Roki Sasaki (fuera desde el 27 de agosto por una ampolla en el dedo medio derecho) regrese pronto para una última apertura en la temporada regular.
Dada la historia de Snell de lanzar bien luego de largas ausencias de acción en Grandes Ligas, ¿han considerado los Dodgers permitirle saltarse su próxima apertura, que siga descansando y esperar a que vuelva a la loma una vez que comiencen los juegos de postemporada?
"Se ha pensado en eso", reveló Roberts. "Pero todavía estás hablando de unos posibles 17 días, algo así... es mucho tiempo para no estar en competencia. Donde normalmente, con su historial, todavía tienes rehabilitaciones y cosas por el estilo. Así que no es sólo cuestión de conectarlo y ya, que descanse dos semanas y lance en un juego de playoffs".

item.title: [DodgerBlue.com] Dalton Rushing's treatment, Dodgers optimistic with Pages, Snell & Ohtani

item.content:encoded:
With just over one week left in the regular season, the Los Angeles Dodgers are still looking to secure the No. 2 seed in the National League postseason bracket and perhaps more importantly, get to a better state of health.
Edwin Díaz returned from the injured list on Friday, but the Dodgers are still waiting on the likes of Andy Pages, Dalton Rushing, Roki Sasaki and Shohei Ohtani. Fortunately for L.A., there is optimism with that group, and Blake Snell as well after he came out his most recent start due to left groin tightness.
Dodgers updates
Blake Snell
Snell played catch from flat ground on Friday, getting out to 90 feet as signs point to avoiding the 15-day injured list.
“I’m very hopeful that he’ll make a start before the end of the season,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said.
Snell has a history of missing roughly one month because of adductor/groin strains, but he and the team believe the latest issue did not advance to being that significant.
“Don’t know the answer exactly,” Roberts said when asked what may have caused the tightness, “but happy that we caught it early.”
If — or when — Snell does pitch again, Roberts indicated it would be a normal start rather than an abbreviated final tuneup before the postseason begins.
Andy Pages
After previously sharing the expectation is for Pages to return during the homestand, Roberts offered a slightly more concrete timeline by saying that should come during the Dodgers’ series against the San Diego Padres.
Dalton Rushing
According to Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic, Rushing received a PRP injection in his right forearm.
Dalton Rushing got a PRP injection a week ago to address his flexor in his right arm. Still holding out hope he can be an option as a bat going forward — will hit off a machine in the coming days to test it out.
Surgery still doesn’t appear on the table yet.
— Fabian Ardaya (@FabianArdaya) September 18, 2026
Rushing had a brief return at the start of September after going on the 10-day injured list last month because of a slight tear in the UCL of his right elbow. The Dodgers have suggested a best-case scenario is to have Rushing available as a pinch-hit option off the bench in the playoffs.
Shohei Ohtani
Ohtani took swings against a coach pitching in the batting cage and “came out of it well,” per Roberts. Although the superstar talent is making progress, Roberts said more clarity won’t come until Ohtani faces live pitching or hits off the Trajekt machine.
“But everything I’ve heard, it’s been a really productive last three to four to five days. He’s in a good spot,” Roberts added.
Roki Sasaki
Roberts further confirmed Sasaki is nearing a return and will start despite the prior plan being to shift him into a bullpen role. Some of the change is due to the uncertainty that arose from Snell’s groin trouble.
However, Sasaki still figures to be utilized as a reliever in the postseason if the Dodgers rotation remains healthy.

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Dodgers surge late to beat Giants as they work to get healthy for playoffs
item.dc:creator: Kevin Baxter
item.description: Dodgers surge late to beat Giants as they work to get healthy for playoffs - Click here to listen to this article - - Tyler Glasnow gives up three hits, two runs and strikes out 10 over six innings in the Dodgers’ 8-2 win over the San Francisco Giants. - The Dodgers hit four home runs in the eighth inning, including a pair of back-to-back homers. Mookie Betts finished with two home runs. With eight games left in the regular season, the Dodgers have already ticked off the most important box
item.content:encoded:
Dodgers surge late to beat Giants as they work to get healthy for playoffs
- Click here to listen to this article
-
- Tyler Glasnow gives up three hits, two runs and strikes out 10 over six innings in the Dodgers’ 8-2 win over the San Francisco Giants.
- The Dodgers hit four home runs in the eighth inning, including a pair of back-to-back homers. Mookie Betts finished with two home runs.
With eight games left in the regular season, the Dodgers have already ticked off the most important boxes on their postseason to-do list.
They clinched a playoff berth for a record-tying 14th straight season and won the division title for the fifth time in a row. And with Friday’s 8-2 victory over the San Francisco Giants, the Dodgers (94-60) also have an outside shot at their fourth 100-win season in six years.
But that doesn’t mean they don’t have a lot of work to do between now and the start of the playoffs — the most important task being determining exactly where and when they’ll open the postseason.
With Friday’s win and the Milwaukee Brewers’ victory in Baltimore, the Dodgers trail the Brewers by two games in the race for the league’s best record and the home-field advantage in the postseason that goes with it. They also lead the Atlanta Braves by four games for the league’s second-best record, which would give them a first-round playoff bye and an extra five days to get their sizable contingent of walking wounded healthy.
The magic is indeed missing, and after two seasons of conjuring up postseason greatness, these back-to-reality Dodgers appear headed for an early fall.
“To get one of these top two seeds is important. And our guys understand that,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. “Winning the division is great, but I still think our best baseball is ahead of us.”
Achieving that, however, will require emptying an injury list that is almost as long as the team’s starting lineup. If the season ended today, the Dodgers would have at least seven players who wouldn’t be ready to play.
The Dodgers are also hopeful left-hander Blake Snell, who came out of Wednesday’s game after an inning with groin tightness, will be healthy enough to return for one more regular-season start.
Center fielder Andy Pages, who shares the team lead in RBIs with Shohei Ohtani despite missing a month with a fracture in his left hand, is expected to be activated for the series against the San Diego Padres, which begins Tuesday, while backup catcher Dalton Rushing is swinging a bat and will hit against a pitching machine this weekend.
Right-hander Roki Sasaki threw 48 pitches in a bullpen session Wednesday and could come off the IL next week but right-hander Edgardo Henriquez, second among Dodger relievers in innings and strikeouts, will miss the rest of the regular season with a back strain. He could join the team for the playoffs.
Then there’s Ohtani, the four-time MVP. He’s dealing with injuries to his left knee and right biceps. He has resumed taking batting practice and is eligible to come off the IL Wednesday. Roberts said he hopes to get Ohtani 10-12 at-bats before the playoffs.
“I’m just really waiting to hear when he’s going to get on the field, let alone take live BP,” Roberts said. “He’s not there yet. But everything I’ve heard, it’s been a really productive last three to four to five days.”
One player who did return was closer Edwin Díaz. Limited by multiple injuries to just 16 appearances this season, he was activated off the injured list Friday and threw 17 pitches in the ninth, giving up a single and striking out two batters.
For Roberts, the last month has looked like an episode of “The Pitt,” with medical crises piling up, one atop the other. Yet that’s hardly slowed the Dodgers, who opened their final homestand of the season having won 11 of their past 14 games.
Now the focus becomes continuing that momentum while getting as close to full strength as possible.
“They can go hand in hand,” Roberts said. “We have a lot of good players that are more than capable of helping us win baseball games, at the same time making sure we try to get our best players to optimum health when the postseason starts.”
The Dodgers got a big lift Friday from rookie Josue De Paula, a player who didn’t figure in their postseason plans until a week ago, when he was called up to take Ohtani’s place. In his Dodger Stadium debut, De Paula singled and scored on a Teoscar Hernández single in the fifth, then roped a double to the wall in right-center an inning later, scoring Kyle Tucker to put the Dodgers ahead to stay.
Tucker, Max Muncy, Mookie Betts and Will Smith all homered in a five-run eighth inning, turning a nail-biter into a comfortable win.
Dodgers owner Mark Walter and multiple insurance companies he owns are being sued for allegedly failing to disclose an ongoing federal probe to customers.
That gave right-hander Tyler Glasnow (5-1) his second win since April 23. Glasnow gave up just three hits in six innings, striking out a season-high 10 batters.
Hernández, who had two hits, is batting .368 with 17 RBIs in September; Tucker, who also had two hits, is hitting .424 with five home runs and 13 runs scored in his past 10 games; while Betts, with two homers Friday, has six hits in his past eight at-bats, lifting his average to a season-high .254.
That’s helped make up for Freddie Freeman’s struggles. Freeman, who went hitless in four at-bats Friday, striking out twice, has just six hits — and 13 strikeouts — in his last 48 at-bats.
“We still have a lot of work to do,” Roberts said before the game.
They have just over a week left to get it done.

item.dc:creator: Sarah Wexler

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- Two days after he exited a start following just one inning due to left groin tightness, Blake Snell threw from 90 feet on the field at Dodger Stadium prior to Friday’s series opener against the Giants. He emerged feeling good, with the Dodgers believing they avoided the worst with an injury that’s been a recurring issue throughout the left-hander’s career.
“Happy that we caught it early,” said manager Dave Roberts, who noted that Snell was not sent to receive any imaging.
The Dodgers remain optimistic that the two-time Cy Young Award winner will make another regular-season start sometime during their remaining nine games. The specific day is to be determined -- his regular spot in the rotation would come up during L.A.’s three-game series vs. San Diego that begins on Tuesday -- but he is not expected to pitch with any limitations.
“I think it'd be more of a normal start,” said Roberts. “Maybe not pushing him a ton, given that we don't know how the season's going to play out. But this will be his last regular-season start, so I think it'd be more of a regular start.”
Snell began the season on the 15-day injured list with left shoulder fatigue, not making his season debut until May 9. He almost immediately went back on the IL due to loose bodies in his left elbow, which were removed using the NanoNeedle Scope procedure. Since returning on Aug. 11, Snell has looked like he hasn’t missed a beat, pitching to a 1.01 ERA over seven starts, with 47 strikeouts and 14 walks in 35 2/3 innings.
For a pitcher who shares a rotation with Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tarik Skubal, Snell is an absolutely vital part of the Dodgers’ postseason rotation plans. Should his condition worsen, the Dodgers’ starting pitching depth suddenly looks pretty thin. There’s Tyler Glasnow, who started on Friday against San Francisco but has dealt with injury issues of his own this year. Roki Sasaki (out since Aug. 27 with a right middle finger blister) is also expected to return soon for one final regular-season start.
Given Snell’s history of pitching well following long layoffs from Major League action, have the Dodgers given any consideration to letting him skip his next start, continuing to rest and waiting to have him pitch again once postseason games get underway?
“There is a thought,” said Roberts. “But you're still talking about a potential 17 days, something like that -- that's a long time to not be in competition. Where typically, with his history, you still have rehabs and things like that. So it's just not kind of a plug-and-play, sit it out for two weeks and pitch in a playoff game.”

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers could be getting one of their All-Stars back from injury. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts told Dodger Insider that Andy Pages will return when the club hosts the San Diego Padres.
It had been previously reported that Pages would return on the Dodgers’ final homestand of the 2026 season. This update gives a firmer timeline for when the 2026 All-Star will return to the lineup.
Pages has been a huge boost to the Dodgers’ lineup. The 25-year-old has slashed .272/.358/.458 with 21 home runs and a 119 wRC+ in 127 games this season. He also provides elite center field defense, rated at +18 Defensive Runs Saved and +9 Outs Above Average.
Dodgers Provide Andy Pages Return Timeline
With a return date set for Andy Pages, that means he’ll get roughly six games of action to prepare for the postseason. Ideally, the Dodgers center fielder can shake off a month’s worth of rust, since he won’t have the luxury of a rehab assignment.
Pages suffered a fracture of his left hand when he got hit by a 100 MPH fastball from the Pirates‘ Bubba Chandler. The club has turned to Alek Thomas and Tommy Edman in center field in his absence.
Edman is currently penciled in as the everyday center fielder after Thomas struggled in a short stint. The former Diamondback was later DFA’d, then outrighted to Triple-A after seven games in the lineup.
With Pages returning, the Dodgers have some tough lineup decisions. Edman will most likely return to the infield, bumping Alex Freeland off second base and off the roster. With Teoscar Hernandez on a hot streak, the club is unlikely to take him out of the lineup.
Dodgers Right Now
At 93-60, the Dodgers are currently up four games in the loss column over the Atlanta Braves, meaning they’re in great position to earn a bye for the Wild Card round.
They’ve already taken care of the first step by securing their fifth straight National League West division title. Now it’s just setting themselves up for the best chance to make a run in the postseason.
There are a lot of injuries the club needs to navigate. Shohei Ohtani, Roki Sasaki, and Edgardo Henriquez are the big ones to follow. Getting Ohtani back and healthy is going to be important if the Dodgers want to finish their three-peat bid.
Los Angeles will finish their 2026 season in California. They host the San Francisco Giants and San Diego Padres on their final homestand. Then they’ll finish out the year in San Francisco.
The Dodgers will send right-hander Tyler Glasnow for the series opener against the Giants. First pitch at Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium is set for 7:15 p.m. PT, with the game being broadcast on Apple TV+.
