item.content:encoded:
ドジャースージャイアンツ（18日、ロサンゼルス）「右手中指のまめ」で負傷者リスト（IL）入りしている米大リーグ、ドジャースの佐々木朗希投手（24）が先発として実戦復帰間近であることが明らかとなった。試合前に取材に応じたデーブ・ロバーツ監督（54）が右腕の状態について語った。
「朗希は良い状態にあるし、投げたがっている。近いうちに復帰できると思う。日付は未定だけど、再び先発として投げることになるでしょう」
16日（日本時間17日）にIL入り後2度目となるライブBP（実戦形式の打撃練習）に登板し、4回を投げて50球を消化するなど復帰に向けて順調にステップを踏んでいる。
一方でチームの先発陣はポストシーズンに向け、不安要素を抱えている。16日のレッズ戦に先発したスネルが左股関節の張りを訴え、1回19球で緊急降板。万全な状態でポストシーズンを迎えることができるか不透明な中、復帰間近の佐々木が重要な存在になりそうだ。
指揮官は「防げるのであれば、先発陣の枚数が不足する事態は避けたい。だからこそ、朗希には4、5イニング程度を投げられるスタミナを維持させておく必要がある」と期待を寄せ、「状況に応じて役割を移行できる選択肢を残しておきたい」と先発でも救援でも起用が可能な24歳を〝ジョーカー〟としてスタンバイさせていく考えを示した。

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers Injury Updates: Shohei Ohtani, Blake Snell, Andy Pages and More
item.dc:creator: Noah Camras; Unknown

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are beginning their final homestand of the season on Friday night against the San Francisco Giants.
The Dodgers have just nine more games in the regular season. After clinching the National League West for the 13th time in the last 14 years, they're still battling for playoff positioning with the Milwaukee Brewers and Atlanta Braves.
If the Dodgers clinch one of the top two seeds, they'll secure a first-round bye. That is especially crucial this season as the team deals with injuries to a handful of key players.
Here's the latest updates on six of those players.
Shohei Ohtani Injury Update
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts told reporters on Friday that Ohtani is continuing to progress in his swinging progression.
“Everything I’ve heard it’s been a really productive last three, four, five days," Roberts said. "He’s in a good spot.”
Ohtani has not yet progressed to hitting in live batting practice or off the Trajekt machine. Thus, a return doesn't appear to be imminent.
Ohtani is eligible to return on Wednesday, just five days before the final day of the regular season.
Blake Snell Injury Update
Snell gave the Dodgers a major scare when he exited his Wednesday start after one inning with left groin tightness.
Fortunately, Snell said the exit was more precautionary than anything, as he didn't want to make it worse by staying in the game.
Snell expressed optimism he'd be able to make another start before the end of the regular season. On Friday, Roberts struck a similar tone, saying he was "more confident" the left-hander would be able to make a normal start sometime next week in his regular season finale.
Snell didn't undergo imaging on his groin.
Andy Pages Injury Update
Pages has been out since Aug. 21 when he suffered a fractured hand that forced him to undergo surgery.
However, he rejoined the team at home on Friday, and is expected to be activated at some point during the homestand that goes through Thursday.
Pages told David Vassegh of AM570 that he's hoping to be activated by Tuesday's series opener against the San Diego Padres.
Dalton Rushing Injury Update
Rushing told Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic that he had a PRP injection to address his elbow injury that forced him to go back on the IL in early September.
The catcher remains hopeful he'll be able to return as a pinch-hit option off the bench for the postseason, but will know more after hitting off a machine in the coming days.
Roki Sasaki Injury Update
Sasaki threw four simulated innings this week and is expected to start "soon," per Roberts.
The team initially planned to move Sasaki to the bullpen, but will instead keep him stretched out as a starter as an insurance option.
Edgardo Henriquez Injury Update
Henriquez surprisingly went on the IL with a low-grade back strain this past week, ending his regular season.
The Dodgers remain "hopeful" he'll be able to return in the postseason, per Roberts.

Noah Camras graduated from the University of Southern California in 2022 with a B.A. in Journalism and a minor in sports media studies. He was born and raised in Los Angeles and has extensively covered Southern California sports in his career. item.title: [DodgersBeat] Dodgers Temper Stone, Miller Expectations

item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA, GA — Gavin Stone and Bobby Miller delivered encouraging performances during their rehabilitation assignments this week, but Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts tempered expectations that either right-hander is close to claiming a significant role in the major-league pitching staff.
Stone threw four scoreless innings for Triple-A Oklahoma City, allowing one hit and striking out five. Miller followed with three scoreless innings, one hit allowed and five strikeouts. Their performances naturally raised questions about whether the Dodgers could use either pitcher during the final month of the regular season.
Roberts said both pitchers are progressing, but described their immediate value to the organization in one word.
“Right now, to be quite honest, I think it’s depth,” Roberts said.
Dodgers Temper Expectations for Stone and Miller
The Dodgers entered the season hoping Stone and Miller could eventually strengthen their pitching options, but injuries have prevented both from building a normal workload.
Stone has spent the entire season on the injured list with right shoulder inflammation after missing all of 2025 while recovering from shoulder surgery. He began his rehab assignment with Oklahoma City on August 6 and made his fourth appearance Wednesday.
The right-hander threw 58 pitches, including 41 strikes, and retired the final 10 batters he faced. It was his strongest performance since beginning the assignment and represented another positive step in a comeback that has required considerable patience.
Miller has been on the 60-day injured list all season because of right shoulder soreness. He began his Oklahoma City rehab assignment on August 5 and threw 49 pitches, including 33 strikes, during his three-inning outing Wednesday.
“They’re both doing well. They’re both coming back,” Roberts said. “But I think right now, to be quite honest, I think it’s depth.”
Health and Workload Remain the Priority
Roberts explained that both pitchers have experienced abbreviated seasons without enough competitive innings to immediately be considered finished products.
“Both those guys have had a very abbreviated season, not a lot of competitive baseball,” Roberts said. “And where we’re at on the calendar, I think it’s just getting these guys back to healthy and taking down starts or outings and sustaining that, which they both haven’t done in quite some time.”
That does not eliminate the possibility that Stone or Miller could contribute if the Dodgers need another arm. It does show that the organization is prioritizing their long-term recovery over forcing either pitcher into an immediate role because of one strong outing.
The Dodgers currently have a crowded rotation that includes Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow and Roki Sasaki. Shohei Ohtani is also nearing a return to game action, while Eric Lauer is available to provide length from the bullpen.
That depth gives Los Angeles the flexibility to let Stone and Miller continue rebuilding without rushing them. Roberts had previously discussed Stone as a possible multi-inning bullpen option down the stretch, but his latest comments indicate Stone must first prove he can sustain his workload.
Strong Rehab Outings Still Matter
Roberts’ caution should not erase the progress both pitchers have made. Stone and Miller returned to game action earlier this month after extended absences, giving the Dodgers two additional options who were unavailable for most of the season.
Their long-awaited returns to competitive pitching were important steps by themselves. Their latest results offer more evidence that the rehabilitation process is moving in the right direction.
For now, however, the Dodgers are viewing both starters as insurance rather than building their stretch-run plans around them. Stone and Miller must continue taking down innings, recovering well between appearances and showing that their shoulders can handle a consistent schedule.
If they accomplish that, the Dodgers could revisit their roles. Until then, their strongest contribution may be providing organizational depth while positioning themselves to enter next season healthy.

item.content:encoded:
Mookie Betts: “Nos queda un largo camino por recorrer”
El campocorto de los Dodgers coloca en perspectiva la participación de la novena en la postemporada por decimotercera vez en los últimos 14 años.
PUBLICIDAD
Cincinnati. Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles aseguraron su quinto título consecutivo de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional y el 13ro en las últimas 14 temporadas al vencer el jueves 8-2 a los Reds de Cincinnati.
“Es algo muy importante. Creo que mucha gente piensa que es solo un rito de paso (pero) no es fácil”, declaró el mánager de los Dodgers Dave Roberts. “Así que es algo de lo que todos estamos muy orgullosos, pero entendemos claramente que ese no es el objetivo final”.
Los Dodgers (93-60) disputarán los playoffs por 14 temporada consecutiva, con lo que igualan el récord que los Bravos de Atlanta establecieron de 1991-2005.
Sights and sounds from the clubhouse. 👀 pic.twitter.com/0UTzHdvvpK
— Los Angeles Dodgers (@Dodgers) September 18, 2026
“Es el primer paso”, dijo Mookie Betts mientras se secaba el champán de los ojos. “Nos queda un largo camino por recorrer”.
La celebración en el terreno de juego fue algo calmada tras el último out el jueves. Pero los jugadores se soltaron en el vestuario, donde el champán y la cerveza salpicaron desde el suelo hasta el techo.
“Creo que es una de esas situaciones en las que, como en el béisbol se juega a diario, los jugadores se centran en rendir”, dijo Roberts. “Así que no hay muchos momentos para celebrar. Por eso es agradable ver a los chicos soltarse un poco”.
A pesar de todos sus laureles, los Dodgers creen que todavía tienen algo que demostrar.
El año pasado, el equipo pulverizó el récord de gasto de las Grandes Ligas con una nómina total de 515 millones de dólares, dando alas a críticas de que tienen una supuesta ventaja injusta.
“Lo que estamos creando aquí es especial”, afirmó Max Muncy. “Definitivamente no se le da el reconocimiento que merece. Todo el mundo se fija en la nómina, pero nunca hablamos de cómo hacemos las cosas bien, de cómo nos preparamos adecuadamente o de cómo cuidamos todos esos pequeños detalles. De eso no se habla”.
Doc and the boys are ready for October. pic.twitter.com/krnwXYR7ap
— Los Angeles Dodgers (@Dodgers) September 17, 2026
Los bicampeones defensores de la Serie Mundial aún pujan por el primer puesto de preclasificación de la Liga Nacional, que actualmente está en posesión de los Cerveceros de Milwaukee. Los Ángeles comenzó el día con una ventaja de tres juegos y medio sobre los Bravos (89-64) por el segundo puesto, pero está por detrás de los Cerveceros (95-57).
“Seguimos luchando por uno de los dos primeros puestos”, dijo Roberts. “Creo que hacemos bien celebrando, pero sin dejar que eso afecte a lo que sigue. Tenemos que tomar el vuelo y jugar contra los Gigantes mañana”.
Los Dodgers buscan convertirse en el primer equipo en conquistar tres campeonatos consecutivos de la Serie Mundial desde que los Yankees lo lograron de 1998 a 2000.
Este es el cuarto título divisional asegurado más temprano para los Dodgers. Aseguraron el Oeste de la Liga Nacional el 10 de septiembre de 2019, el 13 de septiembre de 2022 y el 16 de septiembre de 2023.
Los Ángeles aprovechará ese tiempo para recuperar lesionados. Eso empieza con Shohei Ohtani.
El cuatro veces Jugador Más Valioso ha estado en la lista de lesionados de 15 días desde el 8 de septiembre por una inflamación en el bíceps derecho y les dijo a los reporteros a principios de este mes que ya no lanzará más en lo que resta de temporada. La estrella de dos vías hizo swings desde un tee por primera vez el martes y se sintió bien. Se espera que regrese como bateador antes de que termine la temporada regular, aunque no está claro si podrá llegar al 100% de salud antes de octubre.
Roki Sasaki, en la lista de lesionados por una ampolla en el dedo medio, lanzó en una práctica de bateo en vivo el miércoles en Cincinnati y salió bien. Roberts indicó que su próxima aparición será como abridor.
Blake Snell salió prematuramente de la apertura del miércoles después de un inning por rigidez en la ingle izquierda. Su situación es incierta.
Se espera que el cerrador puertorriqueño Edwin Díaz, quien ha estado en la lista de lesionados desde agosto por una inflamación en el cuello, sea activado el viernes. El venezolano Edgardo Henríquez, un preparador de mesa en el bullpeb, está en la lista de lesionados por molestias en la parte baja de la espalda. Se le realizó una resonancia magnética en Los Ángeles el miércoles, que reveló una distensión lumbar, y su rehabilitación se pausará por unos días.
El primera base Freddie Freeman, aquejado por dolor en la rodilla derecha, regresó a la alineación el martes y cortó una mala racha de 3 hits en 30 turnos con tres imparables. Sumó otros dos hits el jueves.
Los Dodgers protagonizaron el mayor impacto de la fecha límite de cambios al adquirir a Tarik Skubal, ganador en dos ocasiones del premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana, procedente de los Tigres. Skubal tiene marca de 3-2 con efectividad de 2.52 en ocho aperturas con los Dodgers.
La incorporación de Skubal convirtió a los Dodgers en los grandes favoritos en las apuestas para ganar la Serie Mundial. Pero después de comenzar la temporada con marca de 61-36, los Dodgers tienen registro de 31-24 desde la pausa del Juego de Estrellas.
Los Dodgers dejaron a 12 corredores en base y se fueron de 0 en 11 con corredores en posición de anotar en la derrota del miércoles ante los Reds, algo que, según Roberts, necesita mejorar.
“Se trata de poder rematar a los equipos cuando tenemos oportunidades. En la postemporada no se presentan muchas oportunidades. Hay que saber aprovecharlas”, dijo Roberts.
___

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have faced multiple injury scares in the pitching rotation. Still, they remain focused on preparing for a third straight World Series win.
One question about the Dodgers’ pitching centers on right-hander Roki Sasaki. The 24-year-old has been sidelined since revealing a blister on his throwing hand. He is eyeing a return before the postseason, although his role in Los Angeles’ rotation remains unknown.
Learning of Blake Snell’s recent groin injury has forced the Dodgers to pivot to a new strategy.
“To be safe, the Dodgers are likely to keep building up Roki Sasaki as a starter,” wrote The Athletic’s Katie Woo. “Sasaki threw a four-inning simulated game Wednesday in Cincinnati. While the Dodgers would prefer to use Sasaki in relief in the postseason, keeping him stretched out on a starter’s workload is smart insurance as they await further developments with Snell.”
Roki Sasaki’s Success as a Postseason Relief Pitcher
While struggling in his first year with the Dodgers in 2025, the team moved Roki Sasaki to a relief role during the postseason. This change worked out well for Los Angeles on its path to a World Series win.
Through nine appearances during the 2025 postseason, Sasaki finished with a 0.84 ERA, 1.03 WHIP, three saves, and two holds. He allowed just one earned run across his postseason run.
Sasaki transitioned into 2026 with similar struggled as the year prior. In 23 starts this season, the second-year starter has a 5-5 record, 4.60 ERA, and 1.33 WHIP across 119.1 innings pitched.
Los Angeles is preparing to have a stacked postseason rotation. It includes 2025 World Series MVP Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, and Tyler Glasnow.
Dodgers Are Closing in on a First-Round Bye
With a little over a week left of the MLB regular season, the Dodgers have their eyes set on clinching a first-round bye in the postseason. Earlier this week, Los Angeles earned the NL West title.
Now, finishing as a top-two team in the National League will secure a top seed and a much-needed break before their postseason run. Entering Friday, the Dodgers hold a four-game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the No. 2 seed.
The top position in the NL is also very much on the table. The Milwaukee Brewers currently own the spot, but hold just a two-game lead over the Dodgers.
It will definitely be something to monitor heading into the weekend. Los Angeles faces the San Francisco Giants in two separate series and the San Diego Padres to finish out their regular season.

item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI -- Heralded by the thumping beat of "Bailalo Rocky," Roki Sasaki opened eyes and electrified Chavez Ravine as the postseason closer during the Dodgers' run to back-to-back championships. The 24-year-old could be poised for a return to the 'pen for L.A.'s three-peat bid -- but he'll make at least one more start before the end of the regular season.
Sasaki has been sidelined since exiting his Aug. 26 start in Atlanta due to a blister on his right middle finger, and he should be activated from the 15-day injured list during the Dodgers' final homestand, likely in next week's series against the Padres.
The Dodgers had been considering getting Sasaki reacclimated to the bullpen before the postseason, but they kept the option of him starting open. Sasaki has remained stretched out during his time on the IL, most recently throwing four simulated innings on 48 pitches on Wednesday afternoon in Cincinnati.
"There's benefits both ways," manager Dave Roberts said. "One can argue it's best to take down a couple starts, keep him built up. Because if something does happen, he's built up. The other side is you can assimilate him into the 'pen and get comfortable in that role -- if that is the role. And so again, that's why we have to be really thoughtful with that."
On Wednesday night, the benefit of having additional rotation depth in Sasaki became clear when Blake Snell exited his start against the Reds after just one inning due to left groin tightness. Removing him from the game was seen as more of a precautionary move, but it exposed the somewhat tenuous state of the Dodgers' starting pitching at present.
If the projected postseason rotation of Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Snell and Tyler Glasnow remain healthy, then the Dodgers will be in a great place. But there are question marks behind the Big Four. Shohei Ohtani will not pitch again this season. Justin Wrobleski moved to the bullpen and has been much shakier in the second half. Emmet Sheehan, who's currently with Triple-A Oklahoma City, is trending upward after his two most recent starts in the Majors -- but has been inconsistent overall.
Yamamoto is the only member of L.A.'s rotation who has not missed a start this season. Both Skubal and Snell had surgery to remove loose bodies from their left elbows. Glasnow spent more than three months on the IL due to lower back spasms, a recurring issue for him. The Dodgers have been proactive with managing Glasnow's back, as Roberts said he flew back to L.A. early to cut out an additional flight segment in between last Saturday's start in Miami and his next scheduled start on Friday.
Should anything happen to those four, Sasaki would figure to be the next arm up in the rotation. Sasaki has broken out in his second Major League season, even though his 5-5 record and 4.60 ERA may seem underwhelming at first glance. After a shaky start to the campaign, Sasaki introduced a new splitter and began to consistently throw his fastball harder, helping him achieve sustainable success as a starter. He posted a 2.63 ERA in seven starts before the blister issue arose.
Because Sasaki is returning from an injury, there may be some rust for him to knock off. He is still pitching with the blister, but Roberts said he felt good after covering it with Dermabond in his most recent bullpen session and simulated game.
"It's playable," Roberts said. "Given the Dermabond, the time that he'll have in between this next outing, the hope is that it's dang near close to being healed."
The Dodgers expect Sasaki to play an important role on their postseason pitching staff, even though they're not sure which role he'll fulfill -- but it is easier to shorten him up to pitch in relief rather than have to build him back up to start. After the latest injury concern, opting to keep starting on the table for Sasaki has already proven wise.

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Roki Sasaki is set to return as a starter, though his postseason role remains unclear.
The Dodgers’ plan changed after Blake Snell suffered an injury on Wednesday, September 16th, during his start against the Cincinnati Reds.
Why the Dodgers changed plans
Snell had a sore left groin and left after one inning. The southpaw was optimistic he avoided the worst of the injury, but the Dodgers still face uncertainty about his status.
As a result, if Snell cannot pitch to finish the season or even the start of the postseason, the Dodgers will need to build up Sasaki as a starter to cover themselves.
Sasaki isn’t at his best right now — the Japanese righty is on the injured list with a blister on his middle finger.
He is eligible to be activated, and he just threw a 48-pitch live batting practice that went well, but the organization is waiting to see how they want to roll him out, either throw him in the bullpen now or have him make starts.
“One can argue it’s best to [let him] take down a couple starts and keep him built up,” Roberts said. “Because if something does happen, then he is built up.”
Will Roki Sasaki make a start?
After Snell’s injury, Roberts was asked again about Sasaki’s likelihood of returning as a starter rather than a reliever, and the skipper said that, to rest everyone properly and for build-up reasons, Sasaki will get a start at some point in the closing days of the season.
“You know, just trying to make sure that guys have ample rest,” Roberts said. “I think his next outing will be as a starter.”
While many fans thought it was a foregone conclusion that Sasaki would move into a reliever role, he could make his first-ever postseason start after a breakout campaign this year.
In his last seven games, he has a 3.05 ERA with 37 strikeouts, 15 walks, and a 1.28 WHIP.
His splitter is a nasty putaway pitch that he throws for strikes, while the slider is coming along as a nice complement.
More importantly than his two offspeed pitches, his fastball sits in the high 90s and has more movement. With that profile, Sasaki would be a devastating postseason reliever, but now he may be called upon for a role no one expects.

item.content:encoded:
Lo que hace de Shohei Ohtani el jugador más extraordinario en la historia de MLB podría ser también su único defecto fatal.
A diferencia de cualquier jugador que haya existido antes que él, Ohtani puede dominar en el plato y en el montículo, pero ha llegado el momento de decidir si lanzar vale la pena por el desgaste que ha provocado en su cuerpo.
Te puede interesar: La decisión de los Dodgers de descansar a Shohei Ohtani como pitcher es la correcta
Los Dodgers colocaron a Ohtani en la lista de lesionados la semana pasada debido a lesiones en la rodilla y el bíceps que han persistido durante meses. Los problemas de rodilla comenzaron oficialmente el 11 de junio, mientras que el problema en el bíceps existe desde algún momento de mayo. No ha realizado una apertura desde el 3 de julio y cada vez que intentaba aumentar su carga de trabajo para regresar, el problema de rodilla generaba un estrés adicional en el bíceps, frenando su progreso. Es muy poco probable que vuelva a subir al montículo esta temporada.
Francamente, no deberíamos volver a verlo lanzar.
Sería una decisión difícil, por decir lo menos. En 14 aperturas esta temporada, Ohtani ha sido dominante. Tiene marca de 8–2, con efectividad de 1.79, WHIP de 0.95 y 95 strikeouts contra 26 bases por bolas en 85 ⅔ innings. Generó 2.9 fWAR como pitcher esta temporada, su mayor cifra desde 2022, cuando realizó 28 aperturas, la mayor cantidad de su carrera. Se nos ha recordado la increíble capacidad que lo convirtió en la primera auténtica estrella de dos vías de este deporte. Desafortunadamente, mantener esa capacidad ha tenido un costo en repetidas ocasiones.
Ohtani ha sufrido una larga lista de lesiones a lo largo de los años mientras intentaba ser un pitcher abridor de tiempo completo y un bateador de todos los días. Esos esfuerzos anteriormente no habían afectado sus capacidades en el plato, pero ahora que tiene 32 años, parece que eso ha comenzado a suceder.
Ohtani ha estado intentando regresar al montículo desde aquella apertura del 3 de julio y su producción como bateador ha disminuido desde entonces. En 49 partidos, registra una línea ofensiva de .259/.342/.518, con 12 home runs, 30 carreras impulsadas y un wRC+ de 127. La mayoría de los demás jugadores de MLB estarían encantados con esos resultados, pero su OPS de .860 durante ese periodo está muy por debajo de las marcas superiores a 1.000 que registró en cada una de las tres temporadas anteriores. Su wRC+ en ese periodo sería el más bajo desde 2020 y casi 50 puntos menor que el de la temporada pasada (172). La lesión de rodilla también ha limitado la velocidad que lo ayudó a robar 59 bases hace dos años. Este año solo suma 11 en 14 intentos.
Las lesiones relacionadas con el pitcheo ya se estaban acumulando durante las primeras temporadas de Ohtani en Estados Unidos. Después de 10 aperturas en 2018, sufrió un desgarro del ligamento colateral ulnar de su brazo derecho y necesitó una cirugía Tommy John. No lanzó en absoluto en 2019 y, cuando regresó al año siguiente, sufrió una distensión del flexor después de dos aperturas y no volvió a lanzar.
En 2021 y 2022 estuvo mayormente saludable y realizó 51 aperturas combinadas sin problemas importantes. A eso le siguieron 23 aperturas en 2023 antes de volver a sufrir un desgarro del UCL y someterse a su segunda cirugía importante de codo en cinco años. No lanzó al año siguiente y regresó al montículo después de casi dos años en 2025, cuando lanzó 47 innings en 14 aperturas. Esta temporada, ni siquiera llegó a los 90 innings antes de volver a ser apartado.
Ohtani está en su novena temporada en MLB y ha lanzado 614 ⅓ innings en su carrera; 428 ⅓ llegaron durante un periodo de tres años entre 2021 y 2023. Eso significa que casi 70% de sus innings de carrera se produjeron durante esas tres temporadas. En sus otras seis campañas combinadas, solo ha lanzado 186 innings.
Cuando Ohtani no está en el montículo, sigue siendo uno de los dos bateadores más valiosos del planeta, junto con Aaron Judge. Cuando está saludable, destroza a los pitchers rivales. Ganó un MVP en 2024 sin lanzar un solo pitch y volvió a ganarlo en 2025 a pesar de lanzar apenas 47 innings. ¿La lección? No necesita estar en el montículo para ser uno de los mejores jugadores del beisbol.
A medida que envejece, el desgaste físico de continuar lanzando se vuelve cada vez más difícil de justificar. Esta temporada es simplemente el ejemplo más reciente. Sigue siendo un jugador de nivel All-Star, pero no ha sido sobrehumano. Los Dodgers no le pagaron $700 millones para ver cómo su mayor habilidad se deteriora mientras persigue inútilmente más innings.
Ohtani lanzó a nivel de as esta temporada cuando estuvo en el montículo y, de haber mantenido ese ritmo, habría estado en la pelea por el Cy Young de la Liga Nacional. En lugar de perseguir un nuevo reconocimiento, el cuatro veces MVP ahora está en la lista de lesionados mientras se acercan los playoffs. Es la misma historia que hemos visto una y otra vez, con pequeñas variaciones, desde que debutó en MLB. Las exigencias físicas de ser tanto pitcher abridor como bateador de todos los días simplemente podrían ser demasiado para que su cuerpo las soporte.
A estas alturas, la única solución es que Ohtani deje de lanzar y se concentre en ser bateador. Incluso si los Dodgers encontraran de alguna manera la forma de reducir su carga de trabajo como pitcher, todavía tendría que prepararse como lanzador todos los días. Ohtani tendría que realizar sesiones de bullpen, mantener su programa habitual de pitcheo y preparar su codo derecho, operado quirúrgicamente en dos ocasiones, para lanzar a 100 mph cada pocos días. Esa es la carga que repetidamente ha descarrilado su carrera como pitcher.
Los Dodgers no necesitan que Ohtani lance. Tienen una rotación repleta de talento encabezada por Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow y, por el momento, Tarik Skubal. Snell y Glasnow han tenido problemas para mantenerse en el montículo, pero ambos tienen contrato al menos hasta la próxima temporada. Mientras tanto, jugadores como Justin Wrobleski, Emmet Sheehan y Roki Sasaki proporcionan profundidad adicional para la rotación. El pitcheo de Ohtani es un lujo del que Los Angeles puede darse el lujo de prescindir.
Durante años, Ohtani ha maravillado al beisbol con sus enormes home runs, velocidades de salida de otro mundo y actuaciones ofensivas que el juego nunca había visto antes. Su capacidad para lanzar lo hizo único, pero ya no vale la pena correr el riesgo. Su experimento de dos vías fue una de las hazañas más impresionantes en la historia del deporte. Continuarlo no vale la pena si eso significa perder la magia que puede crear con un bat en las manos.
En el plato, Ohtani es un superhéroe. En el montículo, es frágil. Ya no tiene sentido arriesgar al Ohtani bateador por tener la posibilidad de contar con el Ohtani pitcher.
Ohtani podría ser el Ícaro del beisbol. Aquello que lo hizo milagroso podría terminar siendo lo que lo haga volver a tocar tierra.
La diferencia es que Ohtani puede alejarse de su defecto fatal antes de que se convierta en su caída.
Publicado originalmente en www.sportsillustrated.com el 15/09/2026, traducido al español para SI México.

item.content:encoded:
La tambaleante asignación de rehabilitación del puertorriqueño Edwin Díaz ha llegado a su fin.
Se espera que Díaz sea activado de la lista de lesionados el viernes en Los Ángeles, informó el manager Dave Roberts antes del juego del jueves en Cincinnati. Completó un inning en blanco en su quinta salida de rehabilitación con Triple-A Oklahoma City el miércoles, un paso hacia adelante luego de permitir cinco carreras limpias en dos tercios de entrada en su presentación anterior el domingo.
La primera temporada del contrato de tres años y US$69 millones de Díaz con los Dodgers ha estado llena de adversidades. Dos pasantías por la lista de lesionados — primero debido a una cirugía para remover cuerpos libres de su codo derecho en abril, y actualmente una inflamación en el cuello que lo marginó en agosto — lo han mantenido alejado de la lomita de Grandes Ligas durante la mayor parte de la campaña. Cuando ha estado sano, no ha rendido, registrando efectividad de 11.85 con cuatro salvamentos desperdiciados en 11 oportunidades.
Lee también: Miguel Rojas castigó a Cincinnati
Los Dodgers inicialmente esperaban que la asignación de rehabilitación de Díaz fuera breve, pero necesitaban ver más de él antes de activarlo de la lista de lesionados. En cinco oportunidades con Oklahoma City, Díaz permitió seis carreras en 4.1 entradas (efectividad de 12.46). Sus problemas de control han continuado, ya que otorgó más boletos (siete) que ponches (cuatro).
Tal como estaban las cosas, Díaz ya estaba destinado a ser utilizado en situaciones de menor apremio al regresar de la lista de lesionados. Pero también es posible que tenga que ganarse su lugar en el bullpen para la postemporada, ya que Roberts reconoció el lunes que podría quedar fuera del roster si no muestra avances.
“Creo que, como todo, debería ser una meritocracia”, señaló Roberts. “Tienes que ganarte el derecho a las oportunidades, pero luego también tienes que rendir, ¿verdad? Eddie entiende eso. Creo que en el punto en el que estamos ahora, necesitamos que los muchachos se comprometan, rindan y a partir de ahí veremos”.
Aquí tienes todo lo que debes saber sobre la última salida de rehabilitación de Díaz:
¿Cómo le fue?
Díaz realizó 15 pitcheos (11 strikes) para completar la novena entrada en blanco, sorteando un doblete con dos outs que salió del bate del dominicano Miguel Andújar, quien también se está rehabilitando, a 104.3 millas por hora. No indujo ningún swing en blanco en los ocho swings que hicieron en su contra (seis ante su slider y dos frente a su recta de cuatro costuras).
¿Qué están diciendo?
A pesar de que los números subyacentes detrás del inning en blanco de Díaz no fueron ideales, pudo trabajar con lo que tenía para conseguir tres outs — lo cual era lo que los Dodgers necesitaban ver de él.
“Calidad a la hora de lanzar strikes. Sacar outs. Probablemente sea eso”, indicó Roberts. “A medida que entras a la postemporada, cada entrada es de alto apremio”.
¿Qué sigue?
Los Dodgers vieron lo suficiente el miércoles como para traer de vuelta a Díaz para sus últimos nueve juegos de la temporada regular. Comenzará lanzando en situaciones de bajo apremio, pero podría ganarse oportunidades de mayor responsabilidad si rinde.
¿Qué más?
- Los Dodgers recibieron un refuerzo para el bullpen el miércoles, activando a Kris Bubic, adquisición de la Fecha Límite de Cambios, de la lista de lesionados de 60 días. El zurdo tiró un inning en blanco en su debut con el equipo para comenzar a presentar sus argumentos de cara al bullpen de postemporada de Los Ángeles.
- El venezolano Edgardo Henríquez mantiene las esperanzas de regresar para la postemporada luego de que unas imágenes de su espalda revelaran una distensión de bajo grado, informó Roberts. En medio de la incertidumbre con Díaz, Henríquez sería una opción para cerrar juegos en octubre si está sano.
- El cerrador de la postemporada del año pasado, Roki Sasaki, podría asumir un rol de similar este año una vez que sea activado de la lista de lesionados de 15 días debido a una ampolla en el dedo medio derecho. Sin embargo, los Dodgers lo mantendrán como abridor por ahora mientras evalúan sus necesidades.
MLB.com.

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Los Dodgers vuelven a reinar en el Oeste de la Nacional y buscan un tricampeonato pese a lesiones

item.content:encoded:
Los Dodgers vuelven a reinar en el Oeste de la Nacional y buscan un tricampeonato pese a lesiones
CINCINNATI — Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles aseguraron su quinto título consecutivo de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional y el 13ro en las últimas 14 temporadas al vencer el jueves 8-2 a los Rojos de Cincinnati.
“Es algo muy importante. Creo que mucha gente piensa que es solo un rito de paso (pero) no es fácil”, declaró el mánager de los Dodgers Dave Roberts. “Así que es algo de lo que todos estamos muy orgullosos, pero entendemos claramente que ese no es el objetivo final”.
Los Dodgers (93-60) disputarán los playoffs por 14 temporada consecutiva, con lo que igualan el récord que los Bravos de Atlanta establecieron de 1991-2005.
“Es el primer paso”, dijo Mookie Betts mientras se secaba el champán de los ojos. “Nos queda un largo camino por recorrer”.
La celebración en el terreno de juego fue algo calmada tras el último out el jueves. Pero los jugadores se soltaron en el vestuario, donde el champán y la cerveza salpicaron desde el suelo hasta el techo.
“Creo que es una de esas situaciones en las que, como en el béisbol se juega a diario, los jugadores se centran en rendir”, dijo Roberts. “Así que no hay muchos momentos para celebrar. Por eso es agradable ver a los chicos soltarse un poco”.
A pesar de todos sus laureles, los Dodgers creen que todavía tienen algo que demostrar.
El año pasado, el equipo pulverizó el récord de gasto de las Grandes Ligas con una nómina total de 515 millones de dólares, dando alas a críticas de que tienen una supuesta ventaja injusta.
“Lo que estamos creando aquí es especial”, afirmó Max Muncy. “Definitivamente no se le da el reconocimiento que merece. Todo el mundo se fija en la nómina, pero nunca hablamos de cómo hacemos las cosas bien, de cómo nos preparamos adecuadamente o de cómo cuidamos todos esos pequeños detalles. De eso no se habla”.
Los bicampeones defensores de la Serie Mundial aún pujan por el primer puesto de preclasificación de la Liga Nacional, que actualmente está en posesión de los Cerveceros de Milwaukee. Los Ángeles comenzó el día con una ventaja de tres juegos y medio sobre los Bravos (89-64) por el segundo puesto, pero está por detrás de los Cerveceros (95-57).
“Seguimos luchando por uno de los dos primeros puestos”, dijo Roberts. “Creo que hacemos bien celebrando, pero sin dejar que eso afecte a lo que sigue. Tenemos que tomar el vuelo y jugar contra los Gigantes mañana”.
Los Dodgers buscan convertirse en el primer equipo en conquistar tres campeonatos consecutivos de la Serie Mundial desde que los Yankees lo lograron de 1998 a 2000.
Este es el cuarto título divisional asegurado más temprano para los Dodgers. Aseguraron el Oeste de la Liga Nacional el 10 de septiembre de 2019, el 13 de septiembre de 2022 y el 16 de septiembre de 2023.
Los Ángeles aprovechará ese tiempo para recuperar lesionados. Eso empieza con Shohei Ohtani.
El cuatro veces Jugador Más Valioso ha estado en la lista de lesionados de 15 días desde el 8 de septiembre por una inflamación en el bíceps derecho y les dijo a los reporteros a principios de este mes que ya no lanzará más en lo que resta de temporada. La estrella de dos vías hizo swings desde un tee por primera vez el martes y se sintió bien. Se espera que regrese como bateador antes de que termine la temporada regular, aunque no está claro si podrá llegar al 100% de salud antes de octubre.
Roki Sasaki, en la lista de lesionados por una ampolla en el dedo medio, lanzó en una práctica de bateo en vivo el miércoles en Cincinnati y salió bien. Roberts indicó que su próxima aparición será como abridor.
Blake Snell salió prematuramente de la apertura del miércoles después de un inning por rigidez en la ingle izquierda. Su situación es incierta.
Se espera que el cerrador puertorriqueño Edwin Díaz, quien ha estado en la lista de lesionados desde agosto por una inflamación en el cuello, sea activado el viernes. El venezolano Edgardo Henríquez, un preparador de mesa en el bullpeb, está en la lista de lesionados por molestias en la parte baja de la espalda. Se le realizó una resonancia magnética en Los Ángeles el miércoles, que reveló una distensión lumbar, y su rehabilitación se pausará por unos días.
El primera base Freddie Freeman, aquejado por dolor en la rodilla derecha, regresó a la alineación el martes y cortó una mala racha de 3 hits en 30 turnos con tres imparables. Sumó otros dos hits el jueves.
Los Dodgers protagonizaron el mayor impacto de la fecha límite de cambios al adquirir a Tarik Skubal, ganador en dos ocasiones del premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana, procedente de los Tigres. Skubal tiene marca de 3-2 con efectividad de 2.52 en ocho aperturas con los Dodgers.
La incorporación de Skubal convirtió a los Dodgers en los grandes favoritos en las apuestas para ganar la Serie Mundial. Pero después de comenzar la temporada con marca de 61-36, los Dodgers tienen registro de 31-24 desde la pausa del Juego de Estrellas.
Los Dodgers dejaron a 12 corredores en base y se fueron de 0 en 11 con corredores en posición de anotar en la derrota del miércoles ante los Reds, algo que, según Roberts, necesita mejorar.
“Se trata de poder rematar a los equipos cuando tenemos oportunidades. En la postemporada no se presentan muchas oportunidades. Hay que saber aprovecharlas”, dijo Roberts.
___

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers right-handed pitcher Roki Sasaki has been sidelined for the last three weeks due to a lingering blister.
After dealing with the blister during a late-August start, Sasaki was removed from the game and later added to the injured list.
"When I was facing the first hitter in the fourth inning, I actually didn't feel anything coming beforehand," Sasaki said through an interpreter after that game. "My skin just ripped off, and then after that, it got worse. ... I thought I was able to manage at first because the skin was still there, but after that, it kept getting worse, and I think it affected my slider afterwards."
As he has continued to recover and trend back towards the mound, Sasaki threw a simulated game on Wednesday, in which he completed four innings.
The Dodgers were thinking about having Sasaki pitch in Thursday's series finale against the Cincinnati Reds, but instead elected for the sim game, and to have him set up to return next week.
“He came out of it well,” Roberts said on Wednesday. “So we have to huddle up here and figure out what’s his role. ... So the number one most important thing is that he came out of that session well, and then now we got to figure out how to plug him in. He’s going to be important, but I just don’t know right now what role.”
At first, the Dodgers weren't sure if Sasaki would be back in the rotation — where he appeared for 23 starts this season — or if he would head to the bullpen.
However, after Blake Snell exited Wednesday's start after one inning, Roberts confirmed Sasaki would rejoin the rotation for the time being.
Sasaki had a 4.72 ERA across the first eight starts of his MLB career last season before he was placed on the injured list with a shoulder impingement for over four months. Upon his late-September return, he was not placed back into the rotation, but rather into a bullpen role that saw plenty of success.
In his first two innings of work, Sasaki struck out four and allowed just one hit and zero runs. His next appearance came in the postseason.
For the remainder of the postseason — one that included the first three saves of his MLB career, the pivotal 8th through 10th innings of an NLDS thriller and even 2.2 innings in the World Series — Sasaki established a 0.84 ERA across 10.2 innings of work.
Sasaki will likely return to the bullpen for the postseason this year, especially with the question marks surrounding Edwin Díaz. However, for now, he appears set to make one more start, and improve upon his 4.60 ERA over 119.1 innings this season.

item.content:encoded:
ドジャースが敵地でレッズに快勝し、5年連続の地区優勝を決めた。通算24度目で、2013年以降は14年間で13度目と圧倒している。16年に就任したデーブ・ロバーツ監督は11年で10度目の優勝となった。
1回、タッカーの16号2ランで先制。2回はフリーマンの犠飛、タッカーの適時二塁打で2点を追加。4回には無死満塁からマンシーの2点適時二塁打、デパウラの適時打で3点を奪い7－0とリードを広げた。9回には今季限りでの引退を表明しているロハスが4号ソロを放ちダメを押した。
守っては先発のロブレスキが3回を無安打無失点の好投。4回から継投に入りトライネン、ナック、ハルボーセンとつなぎ2失点に抑え快勝した。右上腕二頭筋の炎症で負傷者リスト（IL）入りしている大谷翔平投手（32）はロサンゼルスに残留しており不在だった。
大谷と山本由伸投手（28）は3年連続、佐々木朗希投手（24）にとっては2年連続の栄誉。24年は9月26日、昨年は9月25日に優勝が決まっており、ここ3年で最も早い優勝決定となった。
ドジャースは14日のレッズとのカード初戦に勝利し、メジャータイ記録となる14年連続のポストシーズン進出を決めた。マジック「1」で迎えた前日は左腕スネルの緊急降板もあり2－6で敗戦。その後に行われた試合で2位パドレスが勝利したため優勝決定はならなかったが、一夜明けてきっちり自軍の勝利で優勝を決めた。
ポストシーズンはワイルドカードシリーズが29日（同30日）、地区シリーズが10月3日（同4日）に開幕。第2シード（地区優勝チームの中で勝率2位）までに入れば地区シリーズからのスタートになるため、今後もシード争いは続く。

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Blake Snell’s Latest Injury Comments Should Not Faze Los Angeles Dodgers Fans
item.dc:creator: TJ French
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers endured a bit of an injury scare regarding starter Blake Snell in their recent game against the Cincinnati Reds. Snell, who made the start for LA, was pulled after just one inning with groin tightness. During the game, reports surfaced that the Snell injury was not thought to be serious, and that Snell should still be in line to make his start. Well, after the end of the game, Snell spoke with the media, and his comments about the injury should give Dodgers fans some assu
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers endured a bit of an injury scare regarding starter Blake Snell in their recent game against the Cincinnati Reds.
Snell, who made the start for LA, was pulled after just one inning with groin tightness.
During the game, reports surfaced that the Snell injury was not thought to be serious, and that Snell should still be in line to make his start.
Well, after the end of the game, Snell spoke with the media, and his comments about the injury should give Dodgers fans some assurance.
More MLB on Heavy: MLB World Reacts to George Lombard Jr. Blunder in Yankees-Twins Game
What Did Blake Snell Say About His Groin Injury?
Per @SportsNetLA, here is some of what Blake Snell had to say about his early exit:
"I was gonna try to get through five, but I just knew I didn't have a good shot of doing that and remaining healthy."
He also added that he's "day-to-day", and "should be good" to make his next start.
So while many Dodgers fans may have been panicking after he was pulled from the game, it's expected to be a precautionary measure.
The Dodgers' October rotation would still look very formidable without Blake Snell in it, but considering Snell's additions last October, LA is likely going to be as careful as possible when it comes to him being at a full bill of health in a few weeks.

Going into Thursday’s game, the Dodgers held a 3 ½-game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the second seed in the NL with a magic number of seven to clinch th
item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI — A few days off sounds pretty good right about now.
“I do think this team, as much as any team we’ve had, that week off is probably most beneficial,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of locking down one of the top two seeds in the National League in order to get a first-round bye and five days off before starting the postseason.
Going into Thursday’s game, the Dodgers held a 3 ½-game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the second seed in the NL with a magic number of seven to clinch that first-round bye. The Dodgers trail the Milwaukee Brewers by three games for the top seed.
“It’s always helpful in the sense of giving your guys a break to reset,” Roberts said. “But given all the tax and where our guys are health-wise, to get that week would be huge.”
Blake Snell joined the long list of players with injury concerns when he left his start Wednesday after just one inning due to left groin tightness. The Dodgers also have questions about Shohei Ohtani (knee, biceps), Freddie Freeman (knee), Edgardo Henriquez (back), Andy Pages (hand), Roki Sasaki (blister) and Dalton Rushing (elbow).
Pages has been swinging a bat and hitting off the Trajekt machine this week, and it is “very likely” he will be activated from the IL during the homestand starting Friday, according to Roberts.
Ohtani has been “progressing” this week and is feeling “normal-ish” with no pain in his right arm or left knee, Roberts said.
“He’s doing everything he needs to do,” Roberts said. “I still don’t know when (his) time to return to play is. But everything that I hear is really positive.”
Snell could undergo an MRI to determine the severity of his groin injury. But he was optimistic after the game Wednesday that he had pulled back and left the game soon enough that it won’t be a serious issue and he might be able to make one more start before the end of the regular season.
“It’s all contingent on how he feels and potential imaging,” Roberts said. “It doesn’t make sense to just shut him down until the postseason if he can pitch. But again, if he’s not 100 percent to pitch, then we have no problem kicking the can.”
DIAZ RETURN
Right-hander Edwin Diaz completed his rehab assignment with Triple-A Oklahoma City on Wednesday and will join the Dodgers in Los Angeles this weekend with the expectation that he will be activated from the Injured List.
Diaz will be used in “low-leverage” situations, Roberts said, with a need to prove he can pitch well enough to assume a bigger role if he is on the postseason roster.
“I think, like anything, it should be a meritocracy,” Roberts said. “You have to earn the right of opportunities, but then you also have to perform, right? Eddie understands that. I think where we’re at now we just need guys to buy in, perform and go from there. That’s what he’s about.”
Roberts called Diaz’s final outing with OKC was “his best one yet.” Diaz pitched a scoreless inning, gave up a double and didn’t get a single swing-and-miss on any of 15 pitches.
“Quality of strike-throwing. Get guys out,” Roberts said of what he hopes to see from Diaz. “That’s probably it. As you get into the postseason, every inning’s leverage. So that’s kind of it. Quality of strike-throwing, and get guys out.”
UP NEXT
Giants (LHP Cesar Perdomo, 0-1, 3.68 ERA) at Dodgers (RHP Tyler Glasnow, 4-1, 3.50 ERA), Friday, 7:10 p.m., Apple TV, 570 AM

item.content:encoded:
This is your one-stop shop for every Dodgers stint on the injured list during the 2026 season. We’ll also include every time a player misses time on the paternity list, bereavement leave, or is on the family medical emergency list as well.
Basically any time a player misses time that requires a roster move, we’ll note it here.
During the 2025 season, 28 different Dodgers players spent time on the injured list, some of them for multiple stints. That matched the team total from 2024, while in 2023 the Dodgers saw 34 players miss time on the IL.
Every injured-list stint is a transaction and will also be chronicled on our 40-man roster page. Both are essentially living documents that will be constantly updated throughout the season as these moves happen.
Injured-list stints for pitchers are a minimum of 15 days, and for position players it’s at least 10 days.
During spring training, the Dodgers placed both Evan Phillips and Kiké Hernández on the 60-day injured list, which opened up space on the 40-man roster for other moves. On opening day, six more Dodgers were placed on the injured list, including Blake Snell and Tommy Edman.
For more information on each specific injured list stint, click on the links on the dates in the list below this table.

item.title: [The New York Times] Shohei Ohtani’s feeling ‘normal…ish’ as Dodgers sort out health issues before playoffs

item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI — The Los Angeles Dodgers have kept open the possibility that Shohei Ohtani will return before the end of the regular season, though they are up against a running clock.
Any progress is good progress for the Dodgers’ most important piece, so it was a good thing when Ohtani started up activity Tuesday and Thursday and didn’t report any discomfort in his bothersome biceps, balky left knee and tight neck.
“Feels normal…ish,” manager Dave Roberts said Thursday morning.
Advertisement
Ohtani went on the injured list late last week, ending a months-long injury saga and giving him a maximum of five additional regular season games to play in before another the playoffs. He is eligible to return as soon as Sept. 23, though Roberts did not commit to that timeline.
There are still steps for Ohtani to take. He swung off a tee on Tuesday, had Wednesday off from baseball activity and could hit off a coach’s pitching by the end of the week. He will need to face some sort of live pitching before he appears in a game and even then, the maximum of five games does not feel like a lot for him to get his timing right.
Especially since, given how the Dodgers tried kicking the can on shelving Ohtani, he will return after having taken just four plate appearances since Sept. 2. Ohtani, clearly compromised by his nagging injuries, had just six hits over his final 49 at-bats before hitting the IL.
They still need Ohtani, even if he is not 100 percent. The oldest lineup in baseball has shown its age. Even if Ohtani’s role on the postseason roster is simply to provide the threat of launching a ball into the seats, that is valuable in their quest for a third consecutive World Series title. The Dodgers’ first road trip without Ohtani since his arrival in 2024 has been noticeably different.
“It’s been a weird feeling because I talk to him all the time in the clubhouse,” Yoshinobu Yamamoto joked through interpreter Yoshihiro Sonoda. Yamamoto has instead had to rely on Roki Sasaki, “but he doesn’t really talk to me.”
Díaz’ place in the bullpen
Edwin Díaz will return to the Dodgers on Friday, but not as the club’s closer. Nothing is guaranteed for the guy the Dodgers gave $69 million to solve their ninth-inning problem and who now could be on the bubble for the postseason roster thanks to his 11.85 ERA.
Díaz, who has made only 16 major-league appearances thanks to arthroscopic elbow surgery and a later neck issue, has also pitched poorly in rehab. A five-run blowup on Sunday with Triple-A Oklahoma City caused the Dodgers to delay Díaz’s return. But a scoreless inning on Wednesday — albeit one in which Díaz gave up a 104 mph double and did not induce a single swing-and-miss — was enough for the Dodgers to bring him back to the big leagues.
“It was his best one yet,” Roberts said of Díaz, whose has a low bar to clear.
Advertisement
Díaz will return in lower-leverage situations and have to show prove over the final week of the regular season he deserves a spot in the Dodgers’ postseason bullpen, even if their list of right-handed relief options is thinning.
“I think like anything it should be a meritocracy,” Roberts said. “You have to earn the right of opportunities but then you also got to perform, right?”
Edgardo Henriquez was the club’s most trusted reliever before he went on the injured list on Monday. Subsequent imaging showed what Roberts dubbed a “low-grade” back strain, and the manager said he was “hopeful” that Henriquez could still be a postseason option.
Another potential solution, Sasaki, is now needed in the rotation after Blake Snell exited Wednesday’s start with left groin tightness. The Dodgers will know more about Snell’s fate once they return to Los Angeles and potentially get imaging done, but Sasaki is currently slated to pitch at some point next week against the San Diego Padres.
The Dodgers have also been cagey about Tyler Glasnow’s status. Roberts was vague after Glasnow’s last start, but said the right-hander “didn’t feel great” going into it. The Dodgers sent Glasnow directly to Los Angeles afterwards rather than have him travel with the club to Cincinnati, and Roberts said Glasnow’s preparation for Friday’s start has otherwise been normal.
Pages’ return imminent
Andy Pages will “very likely” return to the Dodgers’ lineup without playing in rehab games at some point during the six-game home stand that opens Friday. Pages has progressed quickly from left hand fracture and the Dodgers are banking on the All-Star’s defensive value in center field despite the chances he’ll struggle on offensive.
Pages moved from hitting softer baseballs to hitting normal ones this week and will hit off the Trajekt Arc machine to simulate live at-bats. There aren’t a lot of games to go around on a rehab assignment, anyway, though Oklahoma City did clinch a postseason berth on Wednesday (those games start next week).

item.title: [New York Post] Dodgers latest injury crisis throws Roki Sasaki usage plan in flux

item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI –– Even after watching Roki Sasaki complete the final checkmark in his recovery from a blister on Wednesday afternoon, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts couldn’t say for sure how the team would use the 24-year-old phenom pitcher.
All year, it seemed clear that Sasaki was destined to wind up back in the Dodgers bullpen, reprising the late-inning leverage role he unexpectedly ascended to as a rookie last October.
Though he had turned a corner as a starter during the second half of this campaign, posting a 2.31 ERA in his first six outings after the All-Star break, he had still long looked like a superfluous piece of the Dodgers’ rotation, an excess arm stuck behind the four veteran superstars the club had penciled in to lead this fall’s World Series push.
However, Roberts remained non-committal about Sasaki’s plan on Wednesday, after the right-hander completed a four-inning, 48-pitch session of live batting practice in Cincinnati, in what was hoped to be his final step before returning from the injured list.
On the one hand, the skipper noted, the Dodgers could shift Sasaki to the bullpen now, give him time to re-acclimate to relief duties, and let him focus on just short-burst stints.
But on the other, “one can argue it’s best to [let him] take down a couple starts and keep him built up,” Roberts countered. “Because if something does happen, then he is built up.”
Hours later, the something Roberts was worried about might have suddenly happened –– with Blake Snell’s groin injury having direct repercussions on Sasaki’s potential task.
In Wednesday night’s game, Snell left his start after just one inning because of left groin tightness. While he’s hopeful he avoided any serious injury, he has had bouts of groin issues in the past that have sidelined him for up to a month at a time.
If that were to be the case again now, Sasaki would be first in line to replace Snell in the Dodgers’ postseason rotation.
Mix in the uncertainty surrounding fellow starter Tyler Glasnow faced following his four-inning outing last weekend in Miami –– after which he conspicuously returned immediately to Los Angeles to limit extra travel on the rest of this road trip –– and Sasaki now seems like a valuable starting-pitching insurance policy the Dodgers might still need to utilize in the playoffs.
That’s why, by the end of Wednesday’s game, Roberts was able to at least be definitive about the team’s plan for Sasaki when he comes off the injured list, confirming he is likely to make a start sometime next week, perhaps during a visit from the San Diego Padres.
In a best-case scenario, that will be Sasaki’s last time starting a game this year, with an otherwise healthy rotation allowing the Dodgers to shift him to an equally banged-up bullpen.
But for now, the team can’t be certain of anything.
Which means, when it comes to Sasaki, all options remain on the table.

item.title: [Just Baseball] Who Will Be the Dodgers Game 1 Starter in the Playoffs? | Just Baseball
item.dc:creator: Cade Lalim
item.description: Earlier this week after Monday’s 4-1 road victory against the Cincinnati Reds, the Los Angeles Dodgers clinched a playoff berth for the fourteenth consecutive season, an all-time record that ties them with the Atlanta Braves who accomplished it from 1991 to 2005. A large part of the Dodgers’s success this season has been how good their starting rotation has been. item.content:encoded:
Earlier this week after Monday’s 4-1 road victory against the Cincinnati Reds, the Los Angeles Dodgers clinched a playoff berth for the fourteenth consecutive season, an all-time record that ties them with the Atlanta Braves who accomplished it from 1991 to 2005.
A large part of the Dodgers’s success this season has been how good their starting rotation has been. The team has an enormous amount of pitching depth which means they are constantly sending elite starting pitchers to the bump day-in-and-out.
| ERA | WHIP | BB/9 | K/9 |
| 3.45 (2nd) | 1.09 (2nd) | 2.57 (3rd) | 9.19 (4th) |
When I said that the Dodgers have an enormous amount of starting pitching depth, I really did mean a ton of depth.
Their active starting rotation currently consists of Tyler Glasnow, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell and Yoshinobu Yamamoto, but they also have Justin Wrobleski down in the bullpen who put up an excellent first-half in the starting rotation.
You’d think that’s a pretty good rotation by itself and it certainly is, but they have plenty more quality arms remain either in the minors or on the injured list. These names include: Kris Bubic, Landon Knack, Eric Lauer, Roki Sasaki, Emmet Shehaan, Gavin Stone and of course, Shohei Ohtani.
That right there is enough talent to construct two top-10 starting rotations in the majors, which is incredible. The Dodgers’ plethora of depth is great, but it brings us to an interesting discussion.
The Dodgers coaching staff will have a large selection of elite arms to choose from to open up Postseason action, but who is the most logical and realistic starting pitcher for Game 1?
All stats updated prior to games on Thursday, September 17
Blake Snell, LHP
Snell has pitched really well since returning to the starting rotation in early August. Injuries have kept him out most of the season, as his last start prior to his activation in August came back on May 9 — his season was delayed due to left shoulder fatigue. He left his start on Wednesday after just 19 pitches thanks to a groin injury, so his status is currently up in the air.
Snell has made eight total starts this season, six of those coming after he got activated off the injured list again in August. His injuries don’t seem to be lingering as he’s proven to still be one of the best pitchers in the majors.
Across 38.2 innings pitched, Snell owns a 1.86 ERA and 1.09 WHIP while his underlying metrics prove that he’s still the elite pitcher we’ve been used to. His expected numbers look great, supported by an excellent 2.16 xERA and 2.94 xFIP proving that he is more than ready for playoff action.
Snell, a veteran of 11 seasons, has plenty of postseason innings under his belt and has proved at times to be really good when it matters the most.
When I say at times, it is because last season across 13 postseason innings, he struggled with a 6.92 ERA and 1.77 WHIP. On the other hand, he’s accumulated 82.2 total playoff innings in his career, pitching to a respectable 3.27 ERA and 1.15 WHIP between the three teams he’s suited up for.
Keep in mind that Dave Roberts elected to start Snell in Game 1 of the National League Wild Card last year against the Cincinnati Reds, tossing seven quality innings allowing just two runs while striking out seven. Maybe they will go the same direction this year.
Tarik Skubal, LHP
This year’s mid-summer trade deadline was headlined by the fact that Detroit Tigers sensation Tarik Skubal would probably be on the move when it was all said and done. Well, it happened and Skubal found himself as the blockbuster of the deadline, being traded to the Dodgers.
Being named the American League Cy Young in back-to-back seasons with the Tigers in both 2024 and 2025, the Dodgers got one of the best starting pitchers in the majors.
The Dodgers likely would’ve been completely fine without him, but when a team has trade assets like the Dodgers do, it was a no-brainer for them to get a deal done.
Skubal was a solid pitcher from 2020 to 2023, but the last three seasons for him, including this year, have been absolutely phenomenal. Presently in 2026, splitting time between the Tigers and Dodgers, Skubal has logged 146.2 innings spanning 24 starts, while pitching to a 2.70 ERA and 0.95 WHIP.
If the Dodgers decide they want their ace to start Game 1, it’s going to be Skubal. He’s proved way more than he needs to show that he can be a reliable option in the Postseason. On top of his regular season success, Skubal has looked almost better in October.
He totaled 39.2 innings between the 2024 and 2025 postseasons with the Tigers and looked utterly dominant, hence his 2.04 ERA and 0.73 WHIP. Skubal’s 2025 epic performance alone is incredible.
Last year in his American League Wild Card start against the Cleveland Guardians, Skubal tossed 7.2 innings, only allowing one earned run off of three hits, along with a whopping 14 strikeouts.
Subsequently in the Tigers American League Divisional Series against the Seattle Mariners, he made two starts, totaling 13 innings where he allowed only three earned runs, seven total hits, while striking out 22 and issuing just one walk — ace quality numbers for sure.
Yoshinobu Yamamoto, RHP
Finally, we have Yamamoto, who might not be getting enough praise that he deserves. He’s in the middle of his third season with the Dodgers and has quietly asserted himself as one of the better starting pitchers in baseball.
The now two-time All-Star finished third in National League Cy Young voting in 2025, and has been incredible thus far in his young career. He’s posted a career ERA of 2.60 so far to go along with a 0.87 WHIP.
This year has been Yamamoto’s best season, and he’s been building off of his 2025 success. Over 27 starts totalling a season-high 179 innings pitched, he’s posted a 2.51 ERA and career-best 0.87 WHIP.
Yamamoto is no stranger to pitching when the lights are the brightest, as he played a massive role contributing to the Dodgers’ World Series title in 2025 against the Toronto Blue Jays. He logged 56 innings of postseason work between 2024 and 2025, resulting in a 2.25 ERA and 0.84 WHIP.
His World Series performance last year was one to remember, tossing 17.2 innings between two starts and a relief appearance with a 1.02 ERA and 0.68 WHIP. In Game 7, he pitched out of relief and closed out the game and series when he got Alejandro Kirk to ground into a double-play.
He’s been an absolute work-horse and should play a huge role this year for the Dodgers in the Postseason, no-matter what role he is given.
The Verdict…
Now onto the final verdict in pinning one of the arms mentioned above to start Game 1 in the playoffs for the Dodgers — a decision that Dave Roberts and his coaching staff won’t take lightly.
The best way to build the Dodgers starting rotation is to alter the handedness each game, so that it’s tougher on whoever their opponent may be. That means with Snell and Skubal both being left-handers and Yamamoto being a right-hander, Yamamoto is best suited to lineup as the Game 2 starter.
As I mentioned previously, the Dodgers did elect to start Snell in Game 1 of the National League Wild Card Series last year, but I do think there will be a change of guard this year.
The Dodgers didn’t go and acquire Skubal to be their Game 3 starter; they acquired him to be their bonafide ace and lead them to another World Series title. It only fits best that he takes the ball for Game 1, meaning Snell would line up best for Game 3.
Skubal, being a two-time Cy Young award winner, two-time All-Star, Triple Crown winner and two-time ERA title winner, indicates that he is more than ready and able to be the Dodgers rotation anchor and leader when October baseball rolls around in a few weeks.

item.content:encoded:
【シンシナティ（米オハイオ州）16日（日本時間17日）＝横山尚杜】米大リーグ、ドジャースの佐々木朗希投手（24）がレッズ戦の試合前にライブBP（実戦形式の打撃練習）に登板。「右手中指のまめ」で負傷者リスト（IL）入り後、2度目で4回50球を消化した。レッズ戦に先発したスネルが「左股関節の張り」を訴え、1回19球で緊急降板。ポストシーズンの先発に暗雲が立ち込め、佐々木は復帰戦で先発する見込みとなった。
地区優勝が手に届く直前で、アクシデント続きだ。ドジャースは先発したスネルが1回19球で緊急降板。既往歴4度の「左股関節の張り」を訴え、次回登板が白紙。ポストシーズン（PS）に黄色信号が灯った。一方、「右手中指のまめ」から復帰目前の佐々木は、試合前のライブBPで4回50球を消化。救援転向が濃厚な状況から一気に風向きが変わった。
「ロウキは今週末のジャイアンツ戦では先発しないと思う。ただ、彼の次の登板は先発になると思う」
試合後のロバーツ監督は佐々木の復帰戦が先発になる見込みだと明言。当初は山本由伸、スクバル、スネル、グラスノーでPS先発枠は満席だったが、空席が出る可能性が浮上。この日の佐々木は患部に公式戦でも使用可能なダーマボンド（皮膚接着剤）を患部に施し、球威抜群の速球を投げ込んだ。
ドジャースはスネル緊急降板で、救援陣をつぎ込むも敗戦。地区優勝マジック「1」で迎えたが、自力で決められず2位パドレスも勝利したため、敵地に用意されたシャンパンの封は閉ざされたままとなった。17日（同18日）レッズ戦で勝利するか、パドレスがロッキーズに敗れた時点で5年連続の地区優勝が決定する。
「彼は重要な存在になる」。ロバーツ監督は佐々木をポストシーズンのキーマンに挙げた。後半戦は内容のある投球を見せていた矢先のアクシデントだった。シーズン最終週で、2年連続のPSに弾みをつける。

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Blake Snell Provides Injury Update As Concern Grows
item.dc:creator: Aaliyan Mohammed
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers pulled Blake Snell from Wednesday's start after just one inning with left groin tightness. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers pulled Blake Snell from Wednesday's start after just one inning with left groin tightness.
Snell threw just 19 pitches, and the timing of the injury is a major concern. The regular season is coming to an end, and the Dodgers are about to start playing postseason baseball. Snell was expected to be in the postseason rotation, so an injury has the potential to throw off the Dodgers' plans.
The extent of Snell's injury is unknown, but he does not think it is anything too serious.
"I think it was more of a scare," Snell told The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya.
"I'll see where I'm at, day to day," Snell said, "but I should be good."
Snell said he first felt the issue in the bullpen on a slider, and then was trying to avoid using his lower half on the mound. His velocity was down a tick, and at this point in the year, it's better to be safe than sorry. The game turned into a bullpen day for the Dodgers, and they ultimately lost to the Cincinnati Reds.
"I wasn't trying to use my lower half. It was only a couple pitches where I got into my legs and threw the ball hard," Snell said. "Outside of that, I was kind of guiding it in there."
Snell has missed most of the season with injuries. It started with shoulder fatigue and then a procedure to remove loose bodies from his elbow. However, when he has been on the mound, he looks like the Cy Young Award winner he is.
The Dodgers will reportedly wait to see how he feels on Thursday before sending him for imaging. If he goes to the injured list, the Dodgers may have no choice but to return Roki Sasaki as a starter off the injured list. There was discussion about sending him to the bullpen now since that will likely be his role in October, but plans may change.

item.title: [FanSided] Ranking the most important Dodgers who could come back for the MLB Playoffs
item.dc:creator: Christopher Kline
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are on track to win the NL West and probably earn a first-round bye in the postseason. That comes despite a recent onslaught of injuries. Los Angeles is not unaccustomed to a stacked injury list, but the Dodgers' elite depth — aided by a top-ranked farm system and unrivalred spending power — makes them uniquely resilient. What has helped L.A. win back-to-back World Series titles, however, is their knack for getting healthy at the right time and charging into October at fu
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are on track to win the NL West and probably earn a first-round bye in the postseason. That comes despite a recent onslaught of injuries. Los Angeles is not unaccustomed to a stacked injury list, but the Dodgers' elite depth — aided by a top-ranked farm system and unrivalred spending power — makes them uniquely resilient.
What has helped L.A. win back-to-back World Series titles, however, is their knack for getting healthy at the right time and charging into October at full strength. The Dodgers are hoping to do just that, again. Let's rank six potential returners who could make an outsized impact.
6. RHP Edwin Díaz
Should Edwin Díaz actually come back for the playoffs? He got rocked in his recent Triple-A rehab appearance. The Dodgers' prized $69 million investment has only pitched 13.2 innings in the majors this season, with a disastrous 11.85 ERA (not a typo). Díaz has not looked right at any point.
While the Dodgers presumably want such an expensive and accomplished reliever on the postseason roster, it may be smarter to punt on this season entirely. Díaz is more than capable of rebuilding confidence and getting healthy in the offseason, but it's unclear if L.A. can rely on him in even the lowest-leverage spots currently. Rather than playing with fire, so to speak, the Dodgers should probably lean on their spectacular bullpen depth and keep Díaz on the sidelines. The risk far outweighs the potential reward of rushing him back.
That said, when healthy, Díaz has a long track record as one of MLB's best closers. We know he can electify in the late innings. If the Dodgers are confident for reasons we on the outside aren't privy too, never say never on a triumphant turnaround.
5. RHP Roki Sasaki
Through two seasons, the Rōki Sasaki experience has not quite lived up to expectations for Dodgers fans. Hailed as the best Japanese pitching prospect in a generation, the 24-year-old looks an awful lot like... a prospect. A work in progress. Los Angeles expected immediate results. Now, the Dodgers are hoping Sasaki can iron out command issues against MLB competition. He appeared briefly in the minors this season, but the Dodgers are effectively all-in on Sasaki as a major league pitcher.
Sasaki is expected to recover from a blister before the playoffs, although the Dodgers are uncertain about his exact role. The rotation is much too deep for Sasaki to start in a must-win environment. He was effectively L.A.'s closer last October — a role in which he thrived — but a healthy Tanner Scott removes Sasaki from consideration for that role. Expect him in the bullpen, probably handling bulk work if one of L.A.'s starters is forced out early.
4. C Dalton Rushing
Dalton Rushing was recently returned to the IL after suffering a setback in his recovery from UCL surgery. He's done catching for the season, but L.A. still hopes the 25-year-old can return as a hitter. Of course, if Rushing is effectively relegated to DH, it will be hard to get him in the lineup with Shohei Ohtani also on the roster. Rushing could end up as a situational, pinch-hitter type in October, if he's even on the roster.
It's a credit to how deep the Dodgers are that Rushing being "situational," rather than essential, is even in the cards. The rookie backstop cooled off after the All-Star break, but he's still phenomenally talented. He has a .798 OPS and 120 wRC+ as a rookie, with 12 home runs in only 250 at-bats.
Rushing is stuck behind Will Smith on the org chart, which complicates his future somewhat, but the Dodgers will find ways to use him if he's available.
3. RHP Edgardo Henriquez
The Dodgers hope Edgardo Henriquez can return from a low-grade back strain come the playoffs. The 24-year-old fireballer has quickly established himself as one of baseball's most dominant relievers. He has a 2.85 ERA and 1.03 WHIP with 71 strikeouts in 60.0 innings pitched this season; he ranks in MLB's 99th percentile for both hard-hit rate (27.1 percent) and average fastball velo (100.8 mph).
Henriquez is more than a hard-thrower. He misses barrels and limits explosive hits, able to force groundballs or lifeless bloopers just as often as he forces swing-and-miss. He leans heavily on his four-seam and sinker combo, with a sweeping slider that leaves opposing hitters gasping for air (.191 xwOBA). Should Henriquez return in time, the Dodgers can plug him right into high-leverage spots and expect results. He's the real deal, folks.
2. OF Andy Pages
Andy Pages is back in the batting cage after breaking his hand in mid-August. The Dodgers' centerfielder has enjoyed a proper breakout campaign, posting a .797 OPS and 119 wRC+ with elite defensive metrics and 12 stolen bases. In terms of fWAR, or wins above replacement, Pages ranks third among L.A. positional players (3.9), behind only Shohei Ohtani (6.8) and Max Muncy (4.0).
The Dodgers really need Pages on cleanup duty in centerfield. He covers so much ground and features a killer arm, which wipes runs off the board. Pages' bat cooled down before the injury, but he's still far more dangerous than L.A.'s alternatives — although the recent promotion of top prospect Josue De Paula does create a difficult decision for manager Dave Roberts, assuming the DH spot reverts back to Ohtani.
Speaking of which...
1. DH Shohei Ohtani
This was obvious, yeah? Shohei Ohtani is currently on ice as he attempts to shed bicep and knee problems. That said, the Dodgers plan to get him back before the regular season ends — and it would be absolutely shocking if Ohtani weren't leading off in Game 1 of the Dodgers' first postseason series.
The nagging nature of Ohtani's injuries mean he won't take the mound again in 2026, but he's still the most valuable hitter in the majors, on balance. Yes, Yordan Álvarez and Pete Crow-Armstrong are enjoying better seasons, but Ohtani is the man you want at the plate in a big spot. Drafting a fantasy team, he's your No. 1 pick. So on and so forth.
After spending the early portion of his MLB career on an unserious Angels team, Ohtani is two-for-two in the World Series since joining the Dodgers. He has consistently come up large in the playoffs. Assuming Ohtani is anywhere close to 100 percent, the Dodgers are once again (easy) favorites to win it all.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] The Shoulders on Which Titles Are Built: Tarik Skubal Is Calibrated for October
item.dc:creator: Tom Verducci
item.description: In the last moment before fury overtakes calm, Tarik Skubal stands on the plateau of a 10-inch-tall pedestal of dirt and clay as an imposing and finely calibrated 240 pounds of human pitching machinery. Nothing superfluous. Nothing without purpose. Brutally efficient. The calibrations that lead him to the mound for a playoff game are no different than for a midseason start.
